Cujus rei causas apud Thuanum, & post illum etiam Petrum de Marco de Concord. Sacerd. & Imperii lib. II. 17. aliosque legere est.
units.tr: wrote to Pope Pius a letter in which he complained bitterly that the Council was not proceeding in the manner and order that the pious would wish, nor as the afflicted state of Christendom required: that matters were handled sluggishly, that the Fathers were torn apart by quarrels and dissensions, and that the Council's freedom was not safe and intact. And other such things. He also sent to the Council a volume of demands, of the following kind: that the Pope graciously allow himself and the Roman Curia to be reformed; that the number of Cardinals be reduced; that provision be made so that no more scandalous dispensations are granted; that the exemptions granted here and there against the common laws be revoked; that the pluralism of benefices be abolished entirely; that bishops be compelled absolutely to residence; that communion under both kinds be decreed, that something be relaxed from the former rigour regarding the eating of meat and fasts, and that marriage be allowed to priests in certain nations. Both the letter and the articles are found in Goldast, in the second part of the Imperial Constitutions. But Pallavicini records in his History of the Council of Trent, book XVII, 1:6, that the legates at Trent were strongly disturbed by Ferdinand's written request, because they judged that it came from the craft of those who devoted all their effort to lowering the dignity of the Synod and its presidents, and to diminishing the splendour of the Papacy, and therefore that it should not even be handed to the assembly, but held back for the time being, until they might, through the good offices of the Nuncio, remove Ferdinand from that undertaking. Goldast relates in the third part similar articles sent to the Council by the King of France, with the addition of a solemn protest by the same king against the Council, in which, among other things, the French speak thus: We Frenchmen were hungry and famished, asking the Most Blessed Pope, as a common Father, for bread, not indeed natural bread, of which France, a most fertile kingdom, has no need, but that divine, supersubstantial bread of the Angels, of which in almost the whole Christian world there was first such abundance, and then now such want, that never since the birth of Christ was there scarcity greater. He, however, gave not the bread we asked for, but a scorpion, whose tail with a single blow would at once strike two most powerful kings, the Gallican Church, and the doctrine of the Parisian theologians. After other things said against Pope Pius [philippically] [Φιλιππικῶς], the same Fathers address the Council thus: What is proposed to you for judgment, or published by you as judged, which has not first been sent from Rome and pleased Pius IV? They conclude: We refuse the rule of Pius IV; whatever his judgments and sentences are, we reject, repudiate and despise. And again the Fathers address the Council thus: Since nothing is done by you, but everything at Rome rather than at Trent, and what is published here is judged to be the decisions of Pius IV rather than the decrees of the Council of Trent by right; we declare and protest that whatever is decreed and published in this assembly, that is, by the mere nod and will of Pius IV alone, neither the Most Christian King will approve, nor will the Gallican Church hold it as a decree of an Ecumenical Council. That these thunderbolts were not empty was made known by the facts themselves and by experience, since France, although the clergy resisted, and though even in the public assemblies there was a certain reservation urging the confirmation of the Council, has so far not been brought to acknowledge its authority. The causes of this may be read in Thuanus, and after him also in Peter de Marca, On the Concord of Priesthood and Empire, book II, 17, and others.

units.la: CLXXXVII. Finem habuit Concilium die III. Dec. A. M. D. LXIII. quo Patres anathema dixerunt cunctis haereticis, indiscretè, non diserte his vel illis plane quod in Concilio etiam Archiepiscopus Hydruntinus monuit, contra consuetudinem veterum Conciliorum, in quibus anathema dici suevit non haereticis in genere, sed definitè iis, qui doctrinam Concilii decretis repugnantem pertinaciter foverent, ejusque authores vel sectarii etiam extitissent. Sed vellicaverat aurem Patribus Cardinalis Lotharingus, caussatus scilicet, haereticorum capita esse Reginam Angliæ, Reginam Navarræ, Principem Condeum, Electorem Palatinum, Saxoniæ, &c. Hos nominandos, siquidem haereticos nominatim exprimere placeat. Atque id turbis occasionem præbiturum. Agnoscimus certè Divinam Providentiam, qua refrenati homines illi nominatim nobis anathema dicere non sustinuerunt. Quanquam verendum non erat, ne excommunicati ipsi à Deo excommunicare alios, & prostrati jam verbi Divini gladio, dejicere eos, qui postraverunt, possent.
units.tr: CLXXXVII. The Council came to an end on the 3rd of December in the year 1563, when the Fathers pronounced anathema on all heretics, indiscriminately, not expressly on this or that particular group. This the Archbishop of Otranto also warned against in the Council, contrary to the custom of the older Councils, in which anathema was usually pronounced not on heretics in general, but definitely on those who stubbornly fostered doctrine contrary to the decrees of the Council, and who had themselves been the authors or even the sectarian leaders. But the Cardinal of Lorraine had tugged at the Fathers' ear, alleging, of course, that the heads of the heretics are the Queen of England, the Queen of Navarre, Prince Condé, the Elector Palatine, of Saxony, etc. These are to be named, if it is pleasing to name the heretics expressly. And this would give occasion to disturbances. We certainly acknowledge the Divine Providence by which those men, held in check, did not dare to pronounce anathema on us by name. Yet there was no need to fear that those who had themselves been excommunicated by God might excommunicate others, and, already struck down by the sword of the Divine Word, might cast down those who had struck them down.

units.la: CLXXXVIII. Solicitè equidem Pallavicinus Hist. Concil. Trid. lib. XXIV. cap. II. 2. &c. requirit eos, qui Concilii authoritatem agnoscentes, solenniter illud receperunt, & in ditionibus suis promulgari curarunt. Nominat autem laudatque eo nomine Venetos, Philippum Hispaniæ Regem, Provincias Austriacæ familiæ hæreditarias, Poloniam, ubi in Comitiis Commendoni opera exceptum illud narrat. Potuisset Cantones quosdam Helvetios adjungere, si instrumentum fœderis Pium inter & illos initi, hunc fere in finem ut Sanctiones piæ Sacrosancti Oecumenici Concilii Tridentini ad effectum (NB) tandem producantur, ei innotuisset. Saltem plures, ne Pontificios quidem, nominare potuit. Certè nec Ferdinandus Imperator, nec vel Gallia, vel Germania, vel Hungaria, vel Bohemia, vel Lusitania, vel Hibernia, qua Pontificiarum partium sunt, Concilium eadem ratione, qua in Hispania, Polonia & Venetiis factum narravit, promulgantes à Pallavicino, induci potuerunt.
units.tr: CLXXXVIII. Pallavicini, in his History of the Council of Trent, book XXIV, chapter II, 2, etc., diligently enumerates those who, acknowledging the authority of the Council, received it solemnly and took care to have it promulgated in their dominions. He names and praises by that title the Venetians, Philip King of Spain, the hereditary provinces of the Austrian house, and Poland, where he relates that it was received at the Diet through the work of Commendone. He could have added some Swiss cantons, if the instrument of the covenant made between Pius and them, made almost for this purpose that the pious sanctions of the Most Holy Ecumenical Council of Trent might at last be brought into effect (NB), had become known to him. At least he could not name more, not even among the Papists. Certainly neither Emperor Ferdinand, nor France, nor Germany, nor Hungary, nor Bohemia, nor Portugal, nor Ireland, which are on the Papist side, could be induced to promulgate the Council in the same way as, he reports, was done in Spain, Poland and Venice.

units.la: CLXXXIX. Protestantes verò in Anglia, Scotia,
units.tr: CLXXXIX. But the Protestants in England, Scotland,

units.la: Gallia, Germania, Suecia, Dania, Norwegia, Pannonia, Helvetia, & procedente tempore etiam in Belgio, & quot quot usquam terrarum hæserunt, vel hærent etiamnum, illud ceu Conciliabulum profanorum hominum, Christianismi & Principum Christianorum inane ludibrium, rationibus inducti gravissimis repudiárunt, condemnárnnt, atque eo velut sepimento quodam & intergerino pariete à Papatu Romanensi sese discreverunt, separarúntque in æternum. Nimirum sapere Dei gratia pridem cœpit Christianus orbis, patefactæ sunt nebulonum fraudes, aperti doli, detracta persona. Contemnuntur Papæ tonitrua è pelvi. Bullæ ipsæ Papales pro bullis habenter, brutáque illa fulgetra & luteæ bullæ tam ludi nobis sunt, quàm Vulcanus, suam illam terens incudem, Brontesque steropesque & nudus membra Pyracmon. Nihil præter Evangelium admittitur. Et quoniam vox Cœlestis de Christo, Ipsum audite, præcipit; nihil jam morantur authoritatem Papæ, & Sanctulorum ejus, Dominici, Francisci, similiúmque nihil deliramenta Monachorum, nihil apparitiones mortuorum. Ipsum, ipsummet Christum solum illis audire volupe est. Atque eò denique apud illos feré promotum est, ut unà cum Romani idoli dominatione & religione mendax & fucosa superstitio sublata è medio, atque extincta radicitus ex animis eorum ploret.
units.tr: France, Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Pannonia, Switzerland, and in time also in the Low Countries, and wherever else on earth they have adhered or still adhere, on weighty grounds rejected and condemned that council as a "conventicle of profane men, an empty mockery of Christianity and of Christian princes," and by that wall, as it were, and intervening partition, they separated themselves from the Roman Papacy and cut themselves off for ever. Indeed, by the grace of God the Christian world began long ago to become wise: the frauds of scoundrels have been exposed, their open tricks revealed, and their mask torn off. The thunders of the Pope out of a basin are despised. The Papal bulls themselves are regarded as bulls, and those brutish lightning-bolts and leaden bulls are as much a joke to us as Vulcan, beating away at his anvil, with Brontes and Steropes and naked Pyracmon. Nothing is admitted but the Gospel. And since the heavenly voice concerning Christ commands, Hear ye him, they now pay no regard to the authority of the Pope and of his saints, Dominic, Francis, and the like, nor to the ravings of the monks, nor to the apparitions of the dead. It is a pleasure for them to hear Christ himself, Christ alone. And indeed among them it has been brought to such a point that, together with the dominion of the Roman idol, the lying and painted superstition has been removed from the midst and, uprooted from their minds, lies dead.

units.la: ECCLESIÆ ROMANÆ PERIODUS SEPTIMA.
units.tr: THE SEVENTH PERIOD OF THE ROMAN CHURCH.

units.la: Seu Historia Ecclesiæ Romanæ, per decreta falsæ fidei & Anathematismos Tridentinos in errore obfirmatæ, & cum separata à se vera Christi Ecclesia, fraude & vi continuò decertantis.
units.tr: Or, the History of the Roman Church, hardened in error by the decrees of false faith and the Tridentine anathemas, and continually contending by fraud and force with the true Church of Christ, which has separated from it.

units.la: Inde à fine Concilii Tridentini, seu A. C. M. D. LXIII. ad nostra usque tempora.
units.tr: From the end of the Council of Trent, that is, from the year 1563, down to our own times.

units.la: BREVIARIUM.
units.tr: SUMMARY.

units.la: CXC. Ecclesia Romana post Concilium Tridentinum in errore obfirmata, impudentior & truculentior evasit. Illustratur id similitudine meretricis exoletæ, in obscœnitate deprehensæ. CXCI. Pius V. de salute desperat. Concilii Trid. executioni intentus, adversus fideles sævit, & apud Maximilianum Religionis libertatem Protestantibus impertientem protestatur. CXCII. Angliam, Scotiam frustra turbare conatur. Galliam per Guisios efficacius tentat. CXCIII. Ejusdem artibus Belgii Hispanici tragædia excitata. Cujus causæ & progressus narrantur. CXCIV. Carolo Hispaniæ Infanti, & Isabellæ matri favor erga Evangelicos exitium affert.
units.tr: CXC. After the Council of Trent the Roman Church, hardened in error, became more shameless and savage. This is illustrated by the likeness of a worn-out harlot caught in obscenity. CXCI. Pius V, despairing of salvation, intent on carrying out the Council of Trent, rages against the faithful, and protests before Maximilian, who grants liberty of religion to the Protestants. CXCII. He tries in vain to disturb England and Scotland. He attempts France more effectively through the Guises. CXCIII. By his arts the tragedy of the Spanish Netherlands is stirred up. Its causes and progress are related. CXCIV. Favour towards the Evangelicals shown by Charles, Infante of Spain, and his mother Isabella brings them ruin.

units.la: CXCV. Gregorii XIII. Papatus. Ejus initia laniena Parisiensis horribilis fœdat.
units.tr: CXCV. The papacy of Gregory XIII. Its beginnings are disfigured by the horrible Parisian slaughter.

units.la: CXCVI. Frustra à Gallis nonnullis excusata ; à Thuano, Maximiliano, Imp. Turca, ipso denique Rege Carolo IX. pœnitente damnata.
units.tr: CXCVI. Excused in vain by some Frenchmen; condemned by de Thou, by Maximilian, by the Turkish emperor, and finally by King Charles IX himself, who repented.

units.la: CXCVII. A Gregorio verò Papa, & modernis etiam Jesuitis, Strada & Baptista Gallo, laudata.
units.tr: CXCVII. But it was praised by Pope Gregory, and by modern Jesuits too, Strada and Baptista Gallo.

units.la: CXCVIII. Gregorius idem Calendarium corrigit, seminaria instituit, Jesuitas fovet, Hiberniam Elisabetha subtrahere conatur, Belgas oppugnat. Oraculi de ipso eventus.
units.tr: CXCVIII. The same Gregory corrects the calendar, founds seminaries, favours the Jesuits, tries to withdraw Ireland from Elizabeth, and attacks the Netherlanders. The outcome of his oracle concerning himself.

units.la: CXCIX. Sixti V. crudelitas. Ejusdem contra Henricum Navarrum & Henricum Condæum fulmina bruta. Ab iisdem spreta merito.
units.tr: CXCIX. The cruelty of Sixtus V. His brutish thunderbolts against Henry of Navarre and Henry of Condé. Justly despised by them.

units.la: CC. Monitorium ejusdem adversus Henricum III. diploma. Rex Venetorum consilio, asperè ei respondet. & mox à Clemente interficitur.
units.tr: CC. His monitory against Henry III, and the diploma. The King, on the advice of the Venetians, answers him harshly, and soon afterwards is killed by Clement.

units.la: CCI. Parricidium Clementis à Papa nefariè laudatum. Scripta eidem Anti-Sixti, & Fulminantis titulo opposita.
units.tr: CCI. The parricide of Clement is wickedly praised by the Pope. Writings against him, the Anti-Sixtus, and the title Fulminans are set in opposition.

units.la: CCII. Sixtina vulgatæ versionis recognitio, à Clemente VIII. rejecta.
units.tr: CCII. The Sixtine revision of the Vulgate version, rejected by Clement VIII.

units.la: CCIII. Sixtus Hispanis infensior, Henrici IV. & Elisabethæ Anglæ gratiam ambit. Unde ei mors ab Hispanis acceleratur.
units.tr: CCIII. Sixtus, more hostile to the Spanish, seeks the favour of Henry IV and of Elizabeth of England. Hence his death was hastened by the Spanish.

units.la: CCIV. Gregorius XIV. Henricum IV. persequitur, dirisque devovet. Monitoria ejus in Gallia spreta ; sancitúmque, ne aurum vel argentum ex Gallia Romam ullum deinceps inferatur.
units.tr: CCIV. Gregory XIV persecutes Henry IV and devotes him to dreadful curses. His monitories are scorned in France; and it is decreed that no gold or silver shall henceforth be carried from France to Rome.

units.la: CCV. Henricus Pontificum odiis succumbens religionem Evangelicam ejurat, & Carnuti coronatur. Ejus jugulum à Castello, Jesuitis conscius, frustra appetitum. Jesuitæ ex Gallis proscripti, post decennium, in Pontificis & Mariæ Medicæ gratiam, in eas postliminio admissi sunt. Henricus Pontifici reconciliatus, à Ravaillaco, Jesuitarum pallo, denique perimitur.
units.tr: CCV. Henry, yielding to the hatred of the Popes, renounces the Evangelical religion and is crowned at Chartres. An attempt on his throat by Castel, a man in league with the Jesuits, fails. The Jesuits, banished from France, after ten years were readmitted to them by right of return, to the favour of the Pope and Marie de Medici. Henry, reconciled to the Pope, is finally killed by Ravaillac, a creature of the Jesuits.

units.la: CCVI. Fœdus sacrum, Clemente Pontifice coryphæo, Pontificios inter Principes adversus Protestantes initum. Congregatio gemina de propaganda fide, & sacri fœderis erigitur. Executio fœderis à Stiria, Carinthia, Carniola initium capit.
units.tr: CCVI. The holy league, with Pope Clement as its leader, entered into by the Popish princes against the Protestants. Two congregations, one for the propagation of the faith and one for the holy league, are set up. Execution of the league begins in Styria, Carinthia and Carniola.

units.la: CVII. Intestina Romanam Ecclesiam dissidia exercent, ob quæstiones à Jesuitis motas, de Papa. Confessione & gratiæ auxiliis ac libero arbitrio. cujus postremæ inter Jesuitas & Dominicanos diu agitatæ historia texitur.
units.tr: CVII. Internal dissensions vex the Roman Church, on questions raised by the Jesuits concerning the Pope, confession, the auxiliary grace and free will. The history of the last of these, long debated between the Jesuits and the Dominicans, is here woven.

units.la: CCVIII. Sacerdotes ex Romano Seminario egressi & Jesuitæ in Anglia secretam Hierarchiam constituunt. Occulta inter alumnos seminarii & Jesuitas dissidia.
units.tr: CCVIII. Priests who have left the Roman seminary, and Jesuits in England, set up a secret hierarchy. Hidden dissensions between the students of the seminary and the Jesuits.

units.la: CCIX. Conspirationes & molimina varia adversus Elisabetham Reginam Angliæ, & Jacobum VI. præsente Numine discussa.
units.tr: CCIX. Various conspiracies and plots against Elizabeth, Queen of England, and James VI, are broken up by the presence of God.

units.la: CCX. Clementis de fide tutò à supremis Principibus violanda, doctrina perfida.
units.tr: CCX. Clement's perfidious doctrine that faith may safely be violated by supreme princes.

units.la: CCXI. Conspirationis pulveraria adversus Parlamentum Anglicanum historia narratur.
units.tr: CCXI. The history of the gunpowder conspiracy against the English Parliament is narrated.

units.la: CCXII. Ejus atrocitas exaggerata.
units.tr: CCXII. Its atrocity is exaggerated.

units.la: CCXIII. Ecclesiam Romanam per Jesuitas conspirationis ejus participem fuisse, probatur.
units.tr: CCXIII. It is proved that the Roman Church, through the Jesuits, took part in that conspiracy.

units.la: CCXIV. Jesuitarum hæresis singularis prima de jure occidendi Reges & Principes Romano Pontifici non obsequentes.
units.tr: CCXIV. The first singular heresy of the Jesuits, on the right to kill kings and princes who do not obey the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: CCXV. Eorundem hæresis singularis secunda de æquivocationum & reservationum mentalium jure.
units.tr: CCXV. The second singular heresy of the same men, on the right of equivocations and mental reservations.

units.la: CCXVI. Ecclesia Romana hoc tempore duos insignes Atlantes habuit, Baronium & Bellarminum Cardinales. Baronii Annales cujusmodi sint? Pontificiorum de iisdem judicium minùs favorabile.
units.tr: CCXVI. At this time the Roman Church had two notable Atlases, the cardinals Baronius and Bellarmine. What sort of Annals are Baronius's? The Papists' judgement of them is less favourable.

units.la: CCXVII. Bellarminus à Pontificiis quo in pretio habitus? In controversiarum Tomis ab eo editis laudem nonnulla merentur: plura verò reprehensione gravi digna sunt. Inconstans passim doctrinæ nostræ patrocinatur. Erga Reges & Principes infensum animum prodidit.
units.tr: CCXVII. How highly Bellarmine was valued by the Papists? In the volumes of controversies published by him, some things deserve praise, but more are worthy of grave reproof. He inconsistently defends our doctrine here and there. He showed a hostile spirit towards kings and princes.

units.la: CCXVIII. Deserta ejus Methodo ad novas artes confugerunt Methodistæ novi, puta Veronistæ, Barth. Nihusius, Walenburgii, Richelius, Valerianus Magnus, Masenius, Marcellius, Bossuet Condomensis Episcopus. Novi illi Methodistæ causæ Pontificiæ proditores merito habentur. CCXIX. Lea
units.tr: CCXVIII. Their method abandoned, the new Methodists took refuge in new arts, namely the Veronists, Barth. Nihusius, the Walenburgs, Richelius, Valerianus Magnus, Masenius, Marcellius, and Bossuet, Bishop of Condom. Those new Methodists are rightly regarded as traitors to the Papal cause. CCXIX. Leo

units.la: CCXIX. Leo XI. sex dierum scenicus Papa. Paulus V. miris factionibus electus. Arcana Conclavis Leonis XI. & Pauli V. à Card. Perrono prodita. Paulus Divinis titulis se ornari patitur.
units.tr: CCXIX. Leo XI, a theatrical Pope for six days. Paul V, elected by remarkable factions. The secrets of the conclave of Leo XI and Paul V were revealed by Cardinal Perron. Paul allows himself to be adorned with divine titles.

units.la: CCXX. Historia dissidii Paulum inter & Venetos, ob interdictum de bonis soli & immobilibus Ecclesiasticis non acquirendis, aliáque, suborti, fusius narrata. Sicarii in caput F. Pauli Servita, ob Venetorum causam strenuè assertam, subornati.
units.tr: CCXX. The history of the quarrel between Paul and the Venetians, arising from the interdict on acquiring goods of the soil and immovable ecclesiastical property, and other matters, is narrated at greater length. Assassins were suborned against the head of Fra Paolo, the Servite, on account of the vigorous defence of the Venetians' cause.

units.la: CCXXI. Claudii Espencaei Parisiensis Theologi verbis Ecclesiae Romanae facies depingitur.
units.tr: CCXXI. The face of the Roman Church is depicted in the words of Claude d'Espence, Parisian theologian.

units.la: CCXXII. Paulus V. Ecclesiae non reformator, sed deformator.
units.tr: CCXXII. Paul V is not a reformer of the Church, but a deformer.

units.la: CCXXIII. Controversias de auxiliis gratiae & conceptione Mariae definire non est ausus. Motus in Hispania ob posteriorem excitati. Gregorii XV. & Alexandri VII. de eadem definitiones.
units.tr: CCXXIII. He did not dare to settle the controversies on the auxiliaries of grace and the conception of Mary. Disturbances in Spain were stirred up over the latter. The definitions of Gregory XV and Alexander VII on the same matter.

units.la: CCXXIV. Nova tempestas adversus Ecclesiam à Iesuitis per Ferdinandum Archiducem Austriae, excitata. Occasio ejus fuit favor Rodolphi II. erga Ecclesias Bohemicas.
units.tr: CCXXIV. A new storm against the Church was raised by the Jesuits through Ferdinand, Archduke of Austria. The occasion was the favour shown by Rudolph II towards the Bohemian churches.

units.la: CCXXV. Rodolphus acie victus moritur. Matthias successor improles Bohemis Ferdinandum successorem obtrudit. Ordines Regni turbatores Pacis consiliarios Pontificios & Iesuitas compescunt, & Fridericum Palatinum Regem eligunt. Inde bello victa Bohemia Ferdinando succumbit.
units.tr: CCXXV. Rudolph dies, defeated in battle. Matthias, his successor, having no children, forces Ferdinand on the Bohemians as their successor. The orders of the kingdom suppress the disturbers of peace, the Papal and Jesuit counsellors, and elect Frederick the Palatine as king. Thence Bohemia, defeated in war, succumbs to Ferdinand.

units.la: CCXXVI. Nova Methodus, qua ex Bohemia religionem veram Iesuitae profligarunt.
units.tr: CCXXVI. The new method by which the Jesuits overthrew the true religion in Bohemia.

units.la: CCXXVII. Anceps inde Ecclesiae Euangelicae status maximè. Sciopius classicum belli sacri canit. Paulus Papa ex decimis Italiae, aliarumque regionum bellum sustentat.
units.tr: CCXXVII. Hence the state of the Evangelical Church was uncertain for a long time. Scioppius sounds the trumpet of holy war. Pope Paul sustains the war from the tithes of Italy and other regions.

units.la: CCXXVIII. Palatinatus & universae Germaniae calamitas. Ferdinandus à Protestantibus bona ecclesiastica repetit. Conclamatis rebus DEVS velut e machina succurrens, Gustavum Adolphum submittit, qui Henoticis domitis Ecclesiam feliciter adjuvat.
units.tr: CCXXVIII. Calamity of the Palatinate and of all Germany. Ferdinand demands back the ecclesiastical goods from the Protestants. When affairs were despaired of, God, as if from a machine, came to help, and sent Gustavus Adolphus, who, having subdued the Henotics, happily aided the Church.

units.la: CCXXIX. Laniena in Valle Telina adversus Euangelicos patrata historia terribilis. A clero & Pontifice illa defenditur & probatur.
units.tr: CCXXIX. A terrible account of the slaughter in the Valtellina carried out against the Evangelicals. It is defended and approved by the clergy and the Pope.

units.la: CCXXX. Gregorii XV. Papatus, Formam eligendi Papæ præscribit, & Jesuitas quatuor, aliosque in Divorum numerum refert.
units.tr: CCXXX. The papacy of Gregory XV. He prescribes the form of electing a Pope, and enrols four Jesuits and others among the number of the saints.

units.la: CCXXXI. Ferdinandum collatione pecuniarum & copiarum adjuvat; Ludovicum XIII. adversus Euangelicos etiam Genevenses accendit, & Venetis ob concessum Græcis Templum, irascitur.
units.tr: CCXXXI. He helps Ferdinand with money and troops; he stirs up Louis XIII against the Evangelicals, including those of Geneva, and is angry with the Venetians for granting a temple to the Greeks.

units.la: CCXXXII. In Hispania secta Illuminatorum emergens, spe veniæ facta, opprimitur.
units.tr: CCXXXII. In Spain the sect of the Illuminati emerges; with the hope of pardon held out, it is suppressed.

units.la: CCXXXIII. Gregorio defuncto Roma factionibus turbatur. Eligitur tandem Barbarinus, seu Vrbanus VIII. qui Nepotes impudenter promovet.
units.tr: CCXXXIII. On the death of Gregory, Rome is thrown into turmoil by factions. At last Barberini, that is Urban VIII, is chosen, who shamelessly advances his nephews.

units.la: CCXXXIV. Canonizationis Lojolæ, Xaverii, aliorum bullas conficit. Eorum miracula falsò laudat. Vera Jesuitarum miracula ex Deza & Sciopio depicta.
units.tr: CCXXXIV. He draws up the bulls for the canonization of Loyola, Xavier and others. He falsely praises their miracles. The true miracles of the Jesuits, as depicted by Deza and Scioppius.

units.la: CCXXXV. Jesuitæ expuncto Germano, & intruso Lojola temerantes fastos, repressi. Jesuitissarum secta ab Vrbano abolita.
units.tr: CCXXXV. The Jesuits, having struck out Germanus and thrust in Loyola, defiling the calendar, were repressed. The sect of the Jesuitesses was abolished by Urban.

units.la: CCXXXVI. Valle Telina exigere Gallos idem satagit.
units.tr: CCXXXVI. He strives to make the French give up the Valtellina likewise.

units.la: CCXXXVII. Occasione dissidii illius adversus Regem Galliæ & Richelium libellis seditiosis vulgatis, in jugulum Regis denuo culter acuitur. Libelli ii à Clero Gallicano damnati. Ob censuram Stampesii dissidium clerum inter & Parlamentum oritur, & à Rege ipso finitur.
units.tr: CCXXXVII. On the occasion of that quarrel against the King of France and Richelieu, seditious pamphlets were published, and the knife is sharpened anew against the King's throat. Those pamphlets were condemned by the Gallican clergy. Because of the censure of Stampesius, a dispute arises between the clergy and the Parliament, and it is ended by the King himself.

units.la: CCXXXVIII. Santarelli de potestate Pontificis liber Regum potestati iniquissimus. Sorbonæ adversus eundem censura acris. In Jesuitas Claromontanos de eodem instituta inquisitio, malam eorum conscientiam profert.
units.tr: CCXXXVIII. Santarelli's book on the power of the Pope is most unjust to the power of kings. The Sorbonne's sharp censure against it. An inquiry instituted on the same matter against the Jesuits of Clermont brings their bad conscience to light.

units.la: CCXXXIX. Cotonus tædio inquisitionis illius moritur. Ejusdem quæstiones curiosæ dæmoni Hadrianæ Fraxineæ propositæ.
units.tr: CCXXXIX. Coton dies from weariness of that inquiry. His curious questions are put to the demon of Hadriana Fraxinea.

units.la: CCXL. Vrbanus Bullam Cœnæ Domini renovat. Ejus origo & mutationes variæ. Reges & Ecclesias Galliæ in ea excommunicari, adversus P. de Marca asseritur.
units.tr: CCXL. Urban renews the Bull of the Lord's Supper. Its origin and various changes. It is asserted, against P. de Marca, that the kings and churches of France are excommunicated in it.

units.la: CCXLI. Rupella à Ludovico XIII. Euangelicis erepta. Vrbani lætitia inde concepta à Iof. Hallo objurgatur.
units.tr: CCXLI. Rochelle is taken from the Evangelicals by Louis XIII. Urban's joy at this is rebuked by Joseph Hall.

units.la: CCXLII. Pontificum & Iesuitarum in Æthiopia seu Habessinia Sedi suæ subjicienda conatus, Vrbani tempore infelicem exitum sortiuntur.
units.tr: CCXLII. The attempts of the Popes and the Jesuits to bring Ethiopia, or Abyssinia, under their See end in an unhappy outcome in Urban's time.

units.la: CCXLIII. Similis catastrophe fuit moliminum in subjuganda Romanæ Ecclesiæ Iaponia. Persecutio immanis Iaponum adversus Christianos à Iesuitis conversos. Eus causa fuit Hispanorum & Iesuitarum consilium de Iaponibus legitimo Regi subducendis. Simile Pontificiorum fatum in Sina.
units.tr: CCXLIII. The efforts to bring Japan under the Roman Church met a similar catastrophe. A savage persecution of the Japanese Christians, converted by the Jesuits, followed. Its cause was the plan of the Spaniards and the Jesuits to withdraw the Japanese from their lawful king. The Papists met a similar fate in China.

units.la: CCXLIV. Vrbanus Cæsaris & Hispani in Germania potentiam suspectans, adversus eos Gallum inflammat. Iesuita Hispanus edito libro Papæ potestatem infringit. Hispanorum adversus Vrbanum consilia.
units.tr: CCXLIV. Urban, suspicious of the power of the Emperor and the Spaniard in Germany, stirs up France against them. A Spanish Jesuit, by publishing a book, undermines the power of the Pope. The Spanish plots against Urban.

units.la: CCXLV. Dissidii Iansenitas & Molinistas instar in Belgio & Gallia erumpentis historia fusè narrata.
units.tr: CCXLV. The history of the dispute that broke out like a fire between the Jansenists and the Molinists in Belgium and France is told at length.

units.la: CCXLVI. Propositiones quinque Iansenii ab Innocentio damnatæ.
units.tr: CCXLVI. The five propositions of Jansenius are condemned by Innocent.

units.la: CCXLVII. Galliæ Episcoporum in recipienda Innocentii adversus Iansenitas Bulla divortium.
units.tr: CCXLVII. The divorce of the bishops of France from the acceptance of Innocent's bull against the Jansenists.

units.la: CCXLVIII. Jansenitarum adversus Innocentii Bullam exceptio, ab Alexandro VII. editâ Bullâ, eliditur. Formula conficitur adversus Jansenium, in cujus verba Pontifex clerum suum adigit.
units.tr: CCXLVIII. The Jansenists' objection to Innocent's bull is crushed by the bull issued by Alexander VII. A formula is drawn up against Jansenius, to which the Pontiff binds his clergy by their words.

units.la: CCXLIX. Non tam Iansenium, quàm Augustinum à Pontificibus damnatum esse, Iansenitæ confirmant. Controversia tota denique in quæstionem de infallibilitate Papæ exiit.
units.tr: CCXLIX. The Jansenists maintain that it was not so much Jansenius as Augustine whom the Pontiffs condemned. Finally the whole controversy comes down to the question of the infallibility of the Pope.

units.la: CCL. Tertia Iesuitarum singularis hæresis, ex pluribus constata, de Gratia & arbitrio.
units.tr: CCL. The third peculiar heresy of the Jesuits, established by several witnesses, concerning grace and free will.

units.la: CCLI. Laniena Euangelicorum in Hibernia, Vrbano Pontifice, patratæ historia horribilis compendiosè narrata.
units.tr: CCLI. The horrible slaughter of the Evangelicals in Ireland, carried out under Pope Urban, is briefly narrated.

units.la: CCLII. In Pontificis gratiam tot in Hibernia cæsæ victimæ sunt.
units.tr: CCLII. So many victims were butchered in Ireland to win the Pope's favour.

units.la: CCLIII. Vrbanus pacis prætextu belli in Germania continuationem promovet.
units.tr: CCLIII. Under the pretext of peace, Urban promotes the continuation of the war in Germany.

units.la: CCLIV. Vrbano succedit Innocentius X.
units.tr: CCLIV. Innocent X succeeds Urban.

units.la: CCLV. Admittit is elogium blasphemiis refertum ab Italo-Græco cusum, quo Pamphilius Filio Dei præfertur.
units.tr: CCLV. He admits a eulogy, full of blasphemies, printed by an Italo-Greek press, in which Pamphilius is preferred to the Son of God.

units.la: CCLVI. Pz-
units.tr: CCLVI. Pz-

units.la: CCLVI. Papatum eo tempore non Innocentius, sed ejus glos Olympia
units.tr: CCLVI. At that time the papacy was administered not by Innocent himself but by his sister-in-law

units.la: Maldachina administrat. Historia ejus ex Abbate Gualdo contracta.
units.tr: Olympia Maidalchini. Her history, drawn from the Abbot Gualdo in summary.

units.la: CCLVII. Innocentio quæ causa Iansenitarum damnandorum fuerint?
units.tr: CCLVII. What were the causes of Innocent's condemnation of the Jansenists?

units.la: CCLVIII. Ejusdem & Nuntii ejus, Fabii Chisii, Bullæ & Pro-
units.tr: CCLVIII. The bulls and protests of Innocent himself and of his nuncio, Fabio Chigi, against the peace of Germany, are most insolent.

units.la: testationes adversus pacem Germaniæ, insolentissimæ.
units.tr: protestations against the peace of Germany, most insolent.

units.la: CCLIX. Ernesti de Eusebiis de Pace Protestantibus non danda,
units.tr: CCLIX. Ernest's book On the Eusebii, that peace is not to be granted to the Protestants,

units.la: liber, Fabii Chisii jussu vulgatus. Responsum ad eum Caramuelis,
units.tr: published by order of Fabio Chigi. A reply to it by Caramuel.

units.la: Dorschæi, Conringii. Innocentii adversus Pacem Bulla ab eodem
units.tr: (Continuation of the above)

units.la: Coringio, Blondello, Hoornbekio discutitur.
units.tr: (Continuation of the above)

units.la: CCLX. Innocentii mors. Historia Conclavis Alexandri VII. au-
units.tr: CCLX. The death of Innocent. The history of the conclave of Alexander VII, published by an Italian author, is presented in summary.

units.la: thore Italo edita, & contracta exhibetur.
units.tr: (Continuation of the above)

units.la: CCLXI. Ejus occasione quæstiones de electione Papæ motæ.
units.tr: CCLXI. Questions about the election of the Pope raised on this occasion.

units.la: CCLXII. In electione Pontificis quid potissimum Cardinales,
units.tr: CCLXII. It is inquired what the cardinals chiefly look to in the election of a Pontiff, and what the laymen look to.

units.la: quid Seculares spectent, inquiritur.
units.tr: (Continuation of the above)

units.la: CCLXIII. Alexandri encomium ab authore Conclavis ejus con-
units.tr: CCLXIII. The eulogy of Alexander, set out by the author of his conclave. His love of learning, and the degrees of kinship by which he reached Mahomet, the Turkish emperor.

units.la: textum. Ejus Philomathia, & gradus consanguinitatis, quo Ma-
units.tr: (Continuation of the above)

units.la: humetem Imp. Turcicum attigit.
units.tr: touched upon the Turkish Emperor.

units.la: CCLXIV. Papatus ejus initia Pedemontana laniena fœdantur. Con-
units.tr: CCLXIV. The beginnings of his papacy are defiled by the Piedmontese slaughter.

units.la: tinuatio persecutionis Waldensium sub Philippo II. Carolo, Philiberto,
units.tr: The continuation of the persecution of the Waldensians under Philip II, Charles, and Philibert,

units.la: CCLXV. Horribilis eorundem laniena ex Morlando repetita.
units.tr: CCLXV. The horrible slaughter of the same people, retold from Morland.

units.la: Ejus vera causa inquiritur.
units.tr: Its true cause is inquired into.

units.la: CCLXVI. Vindicta de persecutoribus non sine præsente Numine
units.tr: CCLXVI. Vengeance on the persecutors, taken not without the present hand of God.

units.la: CCLXVII. Imago quædam pacis iis ab Angliæ, Galliæ, Belgii,
units.tr: CCLXVII. A kind of image of peace, brought about for them by the envoys of England, France, Belgium and Switzerland, is soon broken again and again.

units.la: Helvetiæ Legatis conciliata, iterum mox iterúmque violatur.
units.tr: brought about through the envoys of Helvetia, is soon violated again and again.

units.la: CCLXVIII. Alexandri Bulla, qua Pacis Catholicorum Prin-
units.tr: CCLXVIII. Alexander's bull, by which, under the pretext of mending the peace of the Catholic princes, he seeks to rouse them against the Protestants, and

units.tr: Sweden.

units.la: CCLXIX. Ex Suecia prædam Alexander reportat, Christinam
units.tr: CCLXIX. From Sweden Alexander carries off a prize, Queen Christina, whose history of passing over to the papacy is narrated.

units.la: Reginam, cujus ad Papatum transeuntis historia narratur.

units.tr: CCLXX. Ejusf-

units.la: CCLXX. Ejusdem Alex. Nepotismus, Pallavicini consiliis adjutus describitur.
units.tr: CCLXX. The nepotism of the same Alexander, aided by the counsels of Pallavicini, is described.

units.la: CCLXXI. De Pontificum Nepotismo querela Alvari Pelagii, ejusdem arcana detegentis,
units.tr: CCLXXI. The complaint of Alvaro Pelayo about the nepotism of the Pontiffs, who disclosed its secrets.

units.la: CCLXXII. Francisci Rothomagensis. Conciliorum adversus eundem Canones.
units.tr: CCLXXII. Of Francis of Rouen. The canons of the councils against the same man.

units.la: CCLXXIII. Canonizatio Thomæ Villanovani, in gratiam Hispan.
units.tr: CCLXXIII. The canonisation of Thomas of Villanueva, to win favour with the Spanish.

units.la: CCLXXIV. & Francisci Salesii, in gratiam Gallorum. Blasphemiæ de hujus ἀναμαγτησία & perfectione voces Caroli Augusti Salesii.
units.tr: CCLXXIV. And of Francis de Sales, to win favour with the French. Blasphemous words of Charles Augustus Sales about his ἀναμαρτησία and perfection.

units.la: CCLXXV. Ejusdem erga Ecclesiam Romanam merita, & consilia erga Reformatos sanguinaria.
units.tr: CCLXXV. His merits towards the Roman Church, and his bloody counsels against the Reformed.

units.la: CCLXXVI. Jesuitarum hæresis singularis quarta de infallibilitate Papæ in quæstionibus facti, Lutetiæ in collegio Claromontano prodita.
units.tr: CCLXXVI. The fourth peculiar heresy of the Jesuits, concerning the infallibility of the Pope in questions of fact, brought forward at the Clermont college in Paris.

units.la: CCLXXVII. A sanioribus Galliæ Theologis eadem libello ad Episcopos misso graviter obnuntiatur.
units.tr: CCLXXVII. The more sensible theologians of France gravely rebuke the same heresy in a pamphlet sent to the bishops.

units.la: CCLXXVIII. Eadem hæresis in Sorbonam penetrans, ibidem defendenda suscipitur; intercedente Suprema Curia Parisiensi, à qua Sorbonæ circa authoritatem Papæ declaratio flagitatur.
units.tr: CCLXXVIII. The same heresy, penetrating into the Sorbonne, is taken up there to be defended. The Parisian Supreme Court intervenes, and demands from it a declaration of the Sorbonne concerning the authority of the Pope.

units.la: CCLXXIX. Summa declarationis Sorbonæ.
units.tr: CCLXXIX. The substance of the declaration of the Sorbonne.

units.la: CCLXXX. Dissidium Jesuitas inter & Sorbonam ac Curiam Parisiensem novum occasione tum controversiæ Curatos inter & Monachos de munere prædicandi:
units.tr: CCLXXX. A new dispute between the Jesuits and the Sorbonne and the Parisian Court, arising on the occasion of a controversy between the parish priests and the monks over the duty of preaching.

units.la: CCLXXXI. Vbi Sorbona Vernantii de potestate Papæ propositiones varias obelo configit.
units.tr: CCLXXXI. Where the Sorbonne marks with the obelus various propositions of Vernantius concerning the power of the Pope.

units.la: CCLXXXII. Tum novitiæ Theologiæ Moralis Jesuitarum, ceu quintæ eorundem hæreseos.
units.tr: CCLXXXII. Then the novel Moral Theology of the Jesuits, as the fifth of their heresies.

units.la: CCLXXXIII. Cujus præcipuæ hypotheses, veluti de probabilitate, methodo dirigendæ intentionis, arte mutandi definitiones virtutum & vitiorum, cogitationibus bonis, & attritione perstringuntur.
units.tr: CCLXXXIII. Its chief hypotheses, such as probabilism, the method of directing the intention, the art of changing the definitions of virtues and vices, good thoughts, and attrition, are assailed.

units.la: CCLXXXIV. Guimenii opusculum eam in rem editum à Sorbona ad incudem revocatur.
units.tr: CCLXXXIV. Guimenius's little work published for this purpose is called back to the anvil by the Sorbonne.

units.la: CCLXXXV. Alexander Theologiæ illi succensêt; at mox favere incipit.
units.tr: CCLXXXV. Alexander is angry with that theology, but soon begins to favour it.

units.la: CCLXXXVI. Sorbonam apud Regem ob geminam censuram idem graviter accusat.
units.tr: CCLXXXVI. The same Alexander gravely accuses the Sorbonne before the King on account of its double censure.

units.la: CCLXXXVII. Breve Pontificium eam in rem oblatum Suprema Curia censura subjicitur.
units.tr: CCLXXXVII. A papal brief offered for this purpose is submitted to the censure of the Supreme Court.

units.la: CCLXXXVIII. Ejus consilium infallibilitati Papæ opppositum gravissimum.
units.tr: CCLXXXVIII. Its counsel, opposed to the infallibility of the Pope, is most weighty.

units.la: CCLXXXIX. Index librorum prohibitorum Alexandri jussu vulgatus, Pontificum Bullas, Pontificiósque libros expurgans, servitutem Papatus propalat.
units.tr: CCLXXXIX. The Index of Prohibited Books, published by order of Alexander, which purges the bulls and books of the Pontiffs, reveals the servitude of the Papacy.

units.la: CCXC. Eiusdem censura acerba Missalis Romani Gallicè editi; zelum pro latinitate arguit.
units.tr: CCXC. Its bitter censure of the Roman Missal printed in French argues a zeal for Latinity.

units.la: CCXCI. Pallavicini & Julii Clementis Scoti de Ecclesia Pontificia in pejus degenerante contentio.
units.tr: CCXCI. The dispute of Pallavicini and of Julius Clemens the Scot about the Papal Church, degenerating for the worse.

units.la: CCXCII. Post Concilium Tridentinum Ecclesiam Pontificiam in melius mutatam non esse, idem Julius Clemens fusè efficaciterque demonstrat.
units.tr: CCXCII. That after the Council of Trent the Papal Church has not been changed for the better is fully and effectively demonstrated by the same Julius Clemens.

units.la: CCXCIII. Episcopi Germaniæ nonnulli Marti litant.
units.tr: CCXCIII. Some bishops of Germany sacrifice to Mars.

units.la: CCXCIV. Verbi Divini & vetustorum canonum adversus Episcopos milites sententia. Gregorii VII. & Bonifacii VIII. contrarii dictatus. Ximenii & Philippi Belluacensis historia.
units.tr: CCXCIV. The sentence of the Word of God and of the ancient canons against bishops who serve as soldiers. The contrary dictates of Gregory VII and Boniface VIII. The history of Ximenes and Philip of Beauvais.

units.la: CCXCV. Ecclesiasticorum militantium impietas verbis Erasmi & Wicelii depicta.
units.tr: CCXCV. The impiety of churchmen who fight, depicted in the words of Erasmus and Wicelius.

units.la: CCXCVI. Controversia de Attritionis efficacia Jansenitas & Jesuitas inter fervet.
units.tr: CCXCVI. The controversy over the efficacy of attrition rages between the Jansenists and the Jesuits.

units.la: CCXCVII. Jesuitarum de eadem attritione haeresis singularis sexta. Alexandri Bulla, qua haeresin illam reprehendi impiè vetat.
units.tr: CCXCVII. The sixth peculiar heresy of the Jesuits concerning the same attrition. Alexander's bull, by which he impiously forbids that this heresy be censured.

units.la: CCXCVIII. Alexandri mors. Ei Julius Rospigliosus, Clementis IX. nomine insignis, succedit. cujus res gestæ strictim narrantur.
units.tr: CCXCVIII. The death of Alexander. Julius Rospigliosi, distinguished by the name of Clement IX, succeeds him. His deeds are briefly narrated.

units.la: CCXCIX. Eum mox Æmilius Altierius, seu Clemens X. excipit.
units.tr: CCXCIX. Soon after him Emilio Altieri, or Clement X, takes over.

units.la: CCC. Hungaricas is Ecclesias per satellites suos evertere laborat.
units.tr: CCC. He labours through his satellites to overthrow the churches of Hungary.

units.la: CCCI. Euangelicæ in Hungaria religionis fata sub Regibus Ludovico; Johanne de Zapolya & Ferdinando I. obiter narrantur. Pacificatio Viennensis à Rodolpho inita, & ab Impp. Matthia, Ferdinando II. & III. nec non Leopoldo confirmata.
units.tr: CCCI. The fortunes of the Evangelical religion in Hungary under the kings Louis, John Zapolya and Ferdinand I are briefly narrated. The Peace of Vienna, made by Rudolf and confirmed by the emperors Matthias, Ferdinand II and III, and also by Leopold.

units.la: CCCII. Liberum religionis exercitium ab Hungariæ Regibus pactum, Georgius Barzon, Varadiensis Episcopus, libello A. 1671. edito oppugnat.
units.tr: CCCII. George Barzon, bishop of Varad, attacks the free exercise of religion agreed by the kings of Hungary, in a little book published in 1671.

units.la: CCCIII. Triplex ejusdem argumentum ad partes vocatum.
units.tr: CCCIII. His threefold argument, brought forward into the open.

units.la: CCCIV. Cleri Pontificii machinationes à Bots-Kajo, Bethlenio, Rackozio repressæ. Denuo Ecclesiæ Hungaricæ à terrestribus Dominis persecutionem patiuntur.
units.tr: CCCIV. The machinations of the Papist clergy are checked by Bocskay, Bethlen and Rákóczi. Again the churches of Hungary suffer persecution from the lords of the land.

units.la: CCCV. Civitates mox etiam Regiæ & liberæ, eversis earum Templis, vexatis expulsisque Pastoribus, invaduntur.
units.tr: CCCV. Soon the cities, even royal and free ones, are attacked, their churches overthrown, and their ministers harassed and expelled.

units.la: CCCVI. Tribunal Posoniense rebellionis prætextu Euangelicos Magnates plures evertit.
units.tr: CCCVI. The tribunal of Pressburg, under the pretext of rebellion, overthrows several Evangelical magnates.

units.la: CCCVII. Pastoribus quoque eodem prætextu evertendis alia quoque tribunalia Tyrnaviæ & Posonii constituta; libellique præscripti, quibus mortis periculum eluctaturi subscribentes, ministerii abdicationem, exilium spontaneum, vel apostasiam promitterent.
units.tr: CCCVII. Other tribunals are also set up at Tyrnau and Pressburg, with the same pretext of overthrowing the ministers; and the prescribed documents, by which those who wish to escape the danger of death would sign, promising renunciation of the ministry, voluntary exile, or apostasy.

units.la: CCCVIII. Citatio ad tribunal illud prima Pastorum Augustanæ Confessionis, qui comparentes male persecutionis impetum sustinent.
units.tr: CCCVIII. The first summons to that tribunal of the pastors of the Augsburg Confession, who, appearing, bear the brunt of the persecution badly.

units.la: CCCIX. Citatio secunda universalis omnium per Hungariam Euangelicorum Ministrorum cui alii obedire prohibentur; alii parent, gravibus rationibus inducti.
units.tr: CCCIX. A second, general summons of all the Evangelical ministers throughout Hungary, which some are forbidden to obey, while others obey, led by grave reasons.

units.la: CCCX. Numerus comparentium utriusque confessionis. Actionis totius series exponitur. Accusationis capita. Accusatorum Iudicumque strophæ. Perduellionis culpa accusati liberantur prægnantibus argumentis.
units.tr: CCCX. The number of those appearing from each confession. The whole course of the action is set out. The heads of the accusation. The shifts of the accusers and judges. The accused are cleared of the charge of treason by weighty arguments.

units.la: CCCXI. Accusati innocentes damnantur, & in libera custodia, paucis exceptis, detinentur, variis artibus ad subscriptionem libellorum pellecti. Subscribentibus Augustanis fratribus non paucis, reliqui in carceres varios distribuuntur. Reformati, duobus exceptis, omnes, subscriptionem constanter abnuentes, in vincula itidem rapti, atque inde producti, diversaque in Hungariæ munimenta relegati sunt.
units.tr: CCCXI. The innocent accused are condemned and, with few exceptions, kept in free custody, enticed by various arts into subscribing the libels. Not a few of the Augsburg brethren subscribe, and the rest are distributed among various prisons. The Reformed, all but two, steadfastly refusing to subscribe, are likewise seized and put in chains, then led out and banished to various fortresses of Hungary.

units.la: CCCXII. Vexatio horrenda fratrum Berenschinum, Comarinum, Eberhardinum, & Leopoldopolin asportatorum. CCCXIII. Violentia in cogendis iis ad cultum Panacei Numinis adhibita. CCCXIV. Astutia Kellionis, testificationem humanitatis suæ in levibus nonnullis captivis præstitæ, ab iisdem extorquentis. CCCXV. Damnatio nova Pastorum, & raptatio crudelissima ad triremes. CCCXVI. Tentationes eorundem, ut militiæ nomen dent, fortiter excussæ. Venditio eorum ad triremes, vexatio horrenda in iis, & ex iisdem Divina liberatio. CCCXVII. Historia reliquorum Pastorum viginti, in carceribus Sarvar, Kapuvar Tergesti & Buccaris inauditis modis vexatorum quorum pars Buccari persecutioni succumbit, pars ad extremum usque eandem sustinet, & vicina jam morti liberatur. CCCXVIII. Examen Extractus Judicialis Tyrnaviæ editi, quo author demonstrare conatur Pastores non ob religionem, sed ob rebellionem horrendam adeo tempestatem subivisse. CCCXIX.. Concluditur historia persecutionis Hungaricæ. CCCXX. Veritas in Papatu hoc tempore erumpens, atque mox sopita iterum, circa cultum B. Virginis Mariæ. CCCXXI. Nec non venerationem imaginum, CCCXXII. Clementi X. succedit Innocentius XI. cujus studium reformandi nonnulla, leviora licet, commendatur. CCCXXIII. Indulgentias idem complures abolet. CCCXXIV. Cleri Pontificii Jesuitarum inprimis, adversus Regem Angliæ, religionem, statumque universum Angliæ terribilis conspiratio. CCCXXV. Detecta per Titum Oatem, & suppliciis reorum magis patefacta. CCCXXVI. Clerus in Anglia magnis ausibus excidens, ad Ecclesias Gallicanas pervertendas sese convertit. CCCXXVII. Edicti Nannetensis, quo Ecclesiarum Gallicarum Ref. libertas nititur, historia narrata. CCCXXVIII. Modernis persecutionibus violari illud varie ostenditur. CCCXXIX. Nominatim in articulis concernentibus libertatem conscientiæ;
units.tr: CCCXII. The horrible vexation of the brethren Berenschin, Comarin and Eberhard, and of those carried off to Leopoldopolis. CCCXIII. The violence used to compel them to the worship of the Panacean Deity. CCCXIV. The cunning of Kellio, who extorts from them a testimony to his humanity, shown to some captives in slight matters. CCCXV. The new condemnation of the ministers, and their most cruel dragging off to the galleys. CCCXVI. Their temptations to enlist as soldiers, bravely shaken off. Their sale to the galleys, the horrible vexation among them, and divine deliverance from them. CCCXVII. History of the remaining twenty ministers, harassed in unheard-of ways in the prisons of Sarvar, Kapuvar, Trieste and Buccari. Some of them succumb to the persecution at Buccari; others endure it to the end and are freed when already close to death. CCCXVIII. Examination of the Judicial Extract published at Tyrnau, in which the author tries to show that the ministers underwent that storm not on account of religion but on account of a horrible rebellion. CCCXIX. The history of the Hungarian persecution is concluded. CCCXX. Truth breaking out in this Papacy at this time, and soon suppressed again, concerning the cult of the Blessed Virgin Mary. CCCXXI. Likewise concerning the veneration of images. CCCXXII. Clement X is succeeded by Innocent XI, whose zeal for reforming some matters, though lesser ones, is commended. CCCXXIII. The same man abolishes many indulgences. CCCXXIV. The terrible conspiracy of the Papist clergy, especially the Jesuits, against the King of England, against religion and against the whole state of England. CCCXXV. Detected by Titus Oates, and made clearer by the punishments of the guilty. CCCXXVI. The clergy in England, falling away in great daring, turns itself to overthrowing the Gallican churches. CCCXXVII. The history of the Edict of Nantes, on which the liberty of the Reformed churches of France rests, narrated. CCCXXVIII. It is shown in various ways that this edict has been violated by modern persecutions. CCCXXIX. Particularly in the articles concerning liberty of conscience;

units.la: CCCXXX. Ægrorum & afflictorum consolationem ;
units.tr: The comfort of the sick and afflicted;

units.la: CCCXXXI. Liberorum educationem.
units.tr: The education of children;

units.la: CCCXXXII. Religionis exercitium publicum.
units.tr: The public exercise of religion.

units.la: CCCXXXIII. Variis modis labefactatum.
units.tr: Shaken in various ways.

units.la: CCCXXXIV. Vexationes & pericula Pastorum in Ecclesiis ad-huc superstitibus.
units.tr: The vexations and dangers of the ministers in the churches still surviving.

units.la: CCCXXXV. Scholarum & Academiarum restrictio vel suppressio.
units.tr: The restriction or suppression of schools and academies.

units.la: CCCXXXVI. Exercitii disciplinae Ecclesiasticae infractio multiplex.
units.tr: The manifold breaches of the exercise of ecclesiastical discipline.

units.la: CCCXXXVII. Camerarum Edicti usus.
units.tr: The use of the Edict of the Chambers.

units.la: CCCXXXVIII. & violenta suppressio.
units.tr: and its violent suppression.

units.la: CCCXXXIX. Parium cum Pontificiis Prærogativarum abrogatio.
units.tr: The abrogation of the privileges shared with the Papists.

units.la: CCCXL. Persecutio Ecclesiæ ejusdem ingravescens, & pressorum oppressorumque innocentia, patientiaque laudabilis.
units.tr: The persecution of the same Church growing worse, and the innocence and laudable patience of the pressed and oppressed.

units.la: CCCXLI. Non parum persecutionem eam exasperavit controver-sia cum Pontifice circa jus Regalia, cujus origo exponitur.
units.tr: The controversy with the Pontiff concerning the right of the Regalia, which did not a little to exasperate that persecution; its origin is set out.

units.la: CCCXLII. Recentissima circa illud dissidii historia.
units.tr: The most recent history of that dispute.

units.la: CCCXLIII. Congregatio Cleri Gallicani jus Regalia Regi vin-dicat, & literis ad Pontificem exaratis sententiam suam tuetur.
units.tr: The Congregation of the Gallican clergy vindicates the Regalia for the King, and by letters written to the Pontiff defends its opinion.

units.la: CCCXLIV. Mox etiam Pontificiam potestatem definitionibus quatuor Regio Edicto graviter sancitis, restringit.
units.tr: Soon afterwards it also restricts the papal power by four definitions solemnly enacted by royal edict.

units.la: CCCXLIV. Romani Pontificis ad Cleri Gallicani literas super jure Regalia, acris responsio. Epicrisis circa eandem authoris.
units.tr: CCCXLIV. The Roman Pontiff's sharp reply to the letters of the Gallican clergy on the right of the Regalia. The author's epicrisis on the same.

units.la: CCCXLV. Congregationis Cleri Gallicani ejusdem pro revocan-dis ad Papatum Evangelicis studia, & literæ circulares ad Episco-pos, quibus negotium extinguendi schismatis commendatur, & dissidium cum Pontifice excusatur.
units.tr: CCCXLV. The same Congregation of the Gallican clergy's efforts to recall the Evangelicals to the Papacy, and its circular letters to the bishops, in which the business of extinguishing the schism is commended and the dispute with the Pontiff is excused.

units.la: CCCXLVI. De literis illis circularibus judicium authoris.
units.tr: The author's judgment on those circular letters.

units.la: CCCXLVII. Ejusdem Congregationis literæ ad fratres secessio-nis Calvinianæ monitoriæ.
units.tr: The admonitory letters of the same Congregation to the brethren of the Calvinist secession.

units.la: CCCXLVIII. Fucus earundem detectus.
units.tr: Their pretence detected.

units.la: CCCXLIX. Finis operi imponitur.
units.tr: An end is put to the work.

units.la: CCCL. Prosphonesis ad Romam ; & Ecclesiæ triumphantis mili-tantisque ardentia vota.
units.tr: Prosphonesis to Rome; and the ardent vows of the Church triumphant and militant.

units.la: CXC.
units.tr: CXC.

units.la: {a}POst Tridentinum Concilium Papatus reliquus factus est longè deterior quàm antehac, ante Reformationem inprimis, cùm vera Ecclesia ei adhuc captivæ instar commixta ejus corruptioni, erroribus tyrannidi alacriter obstrepuit. Separatis ab ea non volentibus duntaxat, sed per anathematismos etiam Tridentinos coactis fidelibus, reliqui decretis insanis Consilii dementati, querelas veteres justissimas in Romanæ Ecclesiæ laudes convertere, & perpetuam ei ἀναμαγτησίαν tribuere coeperunt, perfricta fronte negantes, Papam in fide, addunt hodie Lojolitæ, etiam in facto, unquam erràsse, vel errare potuisse. quod Paradoxum Tridentinum demum Concilium peperit. In errore igitur suo obfirmati, impudentiores & adversus eos, qui discessionem ab iis fecerunt, &
units.tr: After the Council of Trent the Papacy became far worse than it had been before, especially before the Reformation, when the true Church, still held captive and mixed in with its corruption, loudly opposed its errors and tyranny. Those who had left the Papacy were not merely unwilling to stay, but were forced out by the Tridentine anathemas. The remaining Papists, maddened by the mad decrees of that Council, began to turn their old and most just complaints into praise of the Roman Church, and to ascribe to it a perpetual sinlessness [ἀναμαρτησίαν]. With brazen faces they denied that the Pope had ever erred, or could ever err, in faith, and the Jesuits today add, even in fact. This paradox was finally brought forth by the Council of Trent. Therefore, hardened in their error, they became more shameless and more hostile toward those who had withdrawn from them, and

units.la: {a} Ecclesia Romana post Concilium Tridentinum in errore obfirmata, impudentior & truculentior evasit. Papæ tyrannidem ac idololatriam reprehenderunt, truculentiores longè evaserunt. Sic scilicet fieri par erat. Ut enim non illas modò mulieres, quæ primum virginitatis naufragium fecerunt: sed & quæ longo usu consuetudinem ac habitum induere, peccati tamen sui pudet, adeò ut (verbis Martialis utar) abscondant spurcas & monumenta lupas; at verò deprehensæ bene gnavitérque fiunt impudentes, & olenti in fornice stando palàm profitentur impudicitiam, quin eam tantùm non jactant, iram atque animos à crimine sumunt; ita Romana illa mulier à paucis in flagitiis & obscœnitate deprehensa, pudoris adhuc aliquid retinuit. Ex quo verò cum amasiis suis nefando complexu constrictam atque irretitam universus propalam orbis conspexit, tum verò nil mirum est frontem ei periße, & vel de inferis extitisse, qui consumpta ignominia audaciam pro muro habentes, omnem turpitudinis infamiam impudentiæ tiæ magnitudine & perseverantia, quin & sævitia adversus accusatores, discuterent. Idque procedens Papatus Romani historia manifestum faciet.
units.tr: The Roman Church, hardened in error after the Council of Trent, became more shameless and more savage. They rebuked the tyranny and idolatry of the Pope, and became far more savage themselves. Of course it had to happen this way. Consider women who have suffered the first shipwreck of their virginity. Some, having long practised and settled into the habit, still feel shame for their sin, so that, to use Martial's words, they hide their filthy whores' monuments. But when they are caught, they become bold and openly profess their immodesty, standing in a stinking brothel. They do not merely boast of it; they take their anger and their spirit from their crime. So that Roman woman, caught in a few shameful acts and obscenity, still kept some trace of modesty. But once the whole world saw her openly bound and entangled in an unspeakable embrace with her lovers, it is no wonder that she lost her face, and that she, whose disgrace was used up, made boldness her wall and tried to shake off all the infamy of her shame by the magnitude and persistence of her shamelessness, and even by savagery against her accusers. The history of the Roman Papacy, which follows, will make this plain.

units.la: CXCI. Qui igitur Pium IV. excepit Pius V. Infuber, sive Lombardus, Michael Giflerius ante dictus, officii Inquisitionis hactenus Commissarius, opilionis, ut scribunt, filius, apud Carolum Stengelium, Abbatem Anhusanum 2. Optic. Prælat. 3. p. 153. referente etiam Cornelio à Lapide in Ecclesiastic. 32. 1. & Apoc. 3. 1. statim atque Papa creatus est, fassus est, se Religiosum adhuc bene sperâsse de salute sua: Cardinalem factum cœpisse timere: Papam creatum pœne de ea desperare; Concilii Tridentini executionem, ceu præcipuum actionum suarum scopum is sibi propositum habuit. Ex decretis Concilii ejus Catechismum confici curavit, qui Catechismi Romani nomine venit. Quoscunque Euangelicis vel minimum favere suspicatus est, ad dira supplicia inexorabilis rapuit. Inde scilicet, Thuano Histor lib. XXXIX. aliisque testibus, Nicolaum Francum ad furcam, Julium verò Zoanetum, Petrum Carnesecam, & Antonium Palearium, quòd Inquisitionem nominaverint sicam in litteratos distrietam, ad ignem damnavit. Maximiliano II. Imperatori, cùm is in Imperii Comitiis Augustanis libertatem Religionis Protestantibus concessurus esset, per Nuntium suum satis pro imperio significavit: se id nullo modo permissurum. Nec ullius Principis Secularis esse, ejusmodi sibi potestatem & authoritatem arrogare. Improba non minùs quàm superba denuntiatio; quæ apud Imperatorem tamen sapientissimum parùm valuit.
units.tr: CXCI. Pius V, who succeeded Pius IV, was Michael Ghislieri of Bosco, or the Lombard, mentioned above, hitherto a Commissary of the Office of the Inquisition, said to be the son of a shepherd. As Carolus Stengelius, Abbot of Anhausen, reports in Optic. Prælat. 3. p. 153, and as Cornelius a Lapide also reports on Ecclesiasticus 32 and Revelation 3:1, he confessed as soon as he was made Pope: "I had hoped well for my own salvation while I was still a religious man; when I became a Cardinal I began to fear; now that I have been made Pope I almost despair of it." He set before himself, as the chief aim of his actions, the execution of the decrees of the Council of Trent. From those decrees he had a catechism prepared, which came to be called the Roman Catechism. Whomever he suspected of favouring the Evangelicals even slightly, he pitilessly subjected to dreadful punishments. Hence, as Thuanus reports in History, book XXXIX, and other witnesses confirm, he condemned Nicolaus Franck to the gallows, and Julius Zoanetus, Peter Carnesecca and Antonius Palearius to the fire, because they had called the Inquisition a sword drawn against men of learning. When Emperor Maximilian II was about to grant freedom of religion to the Protestants at the Diet of Augsburg, Pius sent word through his Nuncio, with sufficient arrogance toward the Empire, that "he would by no means permit it; nor did it belong to any secular prince to claim such power and authority for himself." It was an improper threat, no less than it was proud; yet it had little effect on the very wise Emperor.

units.la: CXCII. Quas verò non Impius ille in Hispania, Belgio cum primis Hispanico, Gallia, Anglia, Scotia, religionis sanioris exturbandæ & profligandæ penitus, turbas dedit? Historiæ ejus rei testes locupletes passim prostant. Et in Angliam quidem misit Nicolaum Marianum, AnAnglum, ut Elisabethæ Reginæ pro stabilienda religione Euangelica conatus infringeret. Quin & ipsam Reginam, ceu hæreticam, Bulla edita diris devovere, potestate in Regnum omni, quantum in se fuit, exuere, subditos à juramento fidelitatis & obedientia omni liberare non dubitavit. Bullam, quam Johannes Feltonus Londini incredibili audacia foribus Episcopi affixit; ad partes Humfredus de Rom. Curiæ praxi pag. 81. & dedita opera Bullingerus vocârunt. In Scotia, eodem Papa & Lothareno instigantibus, à Regina Maria & Bothuelio Rex è medio sublatus est. Neque tamen in Anglia & Scotia res ex voto & sententia Papæ fluxerunt, Angliâ magis magisque in vero Dei cultu stabilitâ: Scotiæ quin etiam Solio impolito Rege Jacobo, qui Pontificiam religionem & authoritatem omnem sustulit: In Gallia verò ex voto fluxerunt magis, ubi post decretum Caroli IX. ut scilicet Nobilibus in arcibus & sedibus suis populoque in Templis suburbanis, sacra liberè peragere integrum sit; Pius furoris sui satellites nactus Guisios, cœdibus horribilibus cuncta implevit; & Regem ipsum ad asperiora incitatum, contra Ludovicum Condæum, Principem optimum, pecunia copiisque adjuvit, etiam distrahendi facultates Ecclesiasticas eum in finem copia eidem facta.
units.tr: CXCII. What disturbances did that impious man not stir up in Spain, especially in the Spanish Netherlands, France, England and Scotland, to root out and utterly destroy the purer religion? Abundant witnesses to this history lie everywhere. He sent Nicolas Morton, an Englishman, to England to thwart the efforts of Queen Elizabeth to establish the Evangelical religion. Indeed, he did not hesitate to curse the Queen herself as a heretic with an issued bull, to strip her of all authority over the kingdom so far as he could, and to release her subjects from their oath of fidelity and obedience. The bull which John Felton, with incredible boldness, nailed to the doors of the Bishop in London, Humphrey (on the practice of the Roman Curia, p. 81) and Bullinger, deliberately, called to account. In Scotland, with the same Pope and Lotharen inciting, the King was removed by Queen Mary and Bothwell. Yet affairs in England and Scotland did not turn out according to the wish and judgment of the Pope: England became ever more firmly established in the true worship of God, and in Scotland, King James, who abolished the Papal religion and all its authority, was even placed on the throne. In France, however, things turned out more to his liking, where, after the decree of Charles IX, that the nobles might freely celebrate sacred rites in their castles and homes, and the people in the suburban churches, Pius, having found in the Guises the satellites of his madness, filled everything with horrible slaughter. He also incited the King himself to harsher measures against Louis of Condé, an excellent prince, and aided him with money and troops, and to this end the ecclesiastical revenues were placed at his disposal for dispersing them.

units.la: CXCIII. Impii etiam hujus artibus & consiliis inter Regem Hispaniæ Philippum II. & subditos Belgas tragœdia funestissima suscitata est. Ejus causa fuit fœdus sacrum, Pio incentore, Bajonæ Philippum inter Hispaniæ & Carolum IX. Galliæ Reges, Liga sancta titulo initum, de religione Pontificia juxta Tridentini Concilii decreta, per omnes ditiones suas asserenda. Hinc statim in Belgio leges promulgatæ sunt rigidæ: ut Edicta Caroli V. contra receptæ religionis Pontificiæ hostes strictè observentur; Quæsitores fidei admittantur, & si necessitas postulaverit, brachio Seculari juventur ; denique Concilium Tridentinum cuncti religiosè observent. Quo edicto perculsi Belgæ, simul quòd novorum Episcoporum Pontifici addictissimorum jugum sibi imponi, aliaque dira contra fas legum publicarum adversus se jam pridem supplices facti Gubernatrici Margarithæ Parmensi rigorem deprecantur, & in Hispaniam ad Regem Legatos idem tentaturos destinant. Sed adeò nihil subditorum preces & lachrymæ profecerunt, ut ipsi quoque Legati, qui venerant obsequium memoraturi, si nullo novo onere tentarentur ; Regiorúmque ministrorum tyrannidem deprecaturi, vel delusi turpiter, vel crudeliter & contra jus gentium occisi fuerint, utut evocante & jubente ipso Rege ad eam legationem à suis protrusi essent. Missusque mox cum ingentibus militum copiis in Belgium Ferdinandus Toletanus Albæ Dux, lutum illud sanguine maceratum (quo nomine olim Tiberium venisse Suetonius in ejus vita cap. 57. author est) accepto etiam à Pio Pontifice galero & gladio Pontificiis precibus sacrato ; Concilium sanguinis instituit, Comites clarissimos, Egmontium & Hornanum capite plexit, denique Proceres Belgas ad Duodecim virile illud Concilium vocavit, ut Regii Procuratoris accusationibus satisfacerent. Albanus ille, hominis monstrum, sine fronte jactabat, octodecim (alii duplo majorem numerum notant) millia Belgarum, & sexcentos se carnifici tantùm contrucidandos dedisse. Sicut autem fieri amat, ut qui nimis emungit, sanguinem elicit. Prov. XXX. 33. ita fortissimi in Belgio libertatis vindices luculento, & in omnia Secula victuro exemplo demonstrârunt, gravissimos esse morsus irritatæ necessitatis : & ut leni ac miti imperio habitos fidelissimos permanere ; sic crudelitatem atque terrorem infirma esse charitatis vincula. Nam justa tantùm ira ac desperatione ad fortitudinem erecti (uti ferè solet plus impetûs, major constantia penes miseros esse) cæteroquin omnibus modis inferiores, pro patria & libertate præter jus fásque oppressa, tam strenuè felicitérque pugnárunt, ut potentissimus hostis post quingentorum sexaginta quatuor millionum (hanc summam ipsemet moriturus filio apud Meteranum lib. XIX. pag. 878. confessus est) impensam, tot ingentium exercituum, &, quod caput est, tot nobilissimarum Provinciarum jacturam, demum in ipsum Holandiæ meditullium, pacem ultro delatum venerit. Et qui à Carolo Comite Barlamontio, in sermone ad Gubernatricem, Gallica voce, Gheusii, seu mendici vocati sunt, opulentissimi, & potentissimi Regis vires ita attriverunt, ut piam justámque causam præsentissimo Numine defensam fuisse, cordato nemini amplius obscurum esse possit.
units.tr: CXCIII. Through the arts and counsels of this same impious man, a most deadly tragedy was also stirred up between Philip II, King of Spain, and his Belgian subjects. Its cause was the sacred league, made at Bayonne under the title of the Holy League by Philip, King of Spain, and Charles IX, King of France, at Pius's instigation, to maintain the Papal religion in all their dominions according to the decrees of the Council of Trent. Immediately afterwards, strict laws were promulgated in the Netherlands: that the edicts of Charles V against the enemies of the received Papal religion be strictly observed; that inquisitors of the faith be admitted; and that, if necessity should require, they be aided by the secular arm; and finally that all should religiously observe the Council of Trent. The Belgians were alarmed by this edict, and at the same time, because a yoke of new Bishops, most devoted to the Pope, was being imposed on them, and because of other dreadful measures contrary to the law of the land, they came as suppliants to Margaret of Parma, the Regent, and begged for moderation. They also resolved to send envoys to the King in Spain to attempt the same. But the prayers and tears of the subjects achieved so little that the envoys themselves, who had come to offer submission, and to plead against the tyranny of the royal ministers, if no new burden were laid on them, were either shamefully deceived, or cruelly killed, against the law of nations, although they had been summoned and sent to that embassy by the King himself. Soon Ferdinand of Toledo, Duke of Alba, was sent into Belgium with huge bodies of troops, having received from Pope Pius also a hat and a sword consecrated at Papal entreaty, that mud (for which name Suetonius, in his life of Tiberius, chap. 57, says Tiberius was once known) soaked in blood. He established the Council of Blood, beheaded the most illustrious counts, Egmont and Horn, and finally summoned the Belgian nobles before that infamous Council of Twelve, so that they might answer the accusations of the Royal Prosecutor. That Alba, a monster of a man, boasted without shame that he had handed over eighteen thousand (others note twice that number) Belgians, and six hundred, to be butchered by the executioner alone. But, as it commonly happens, he who blows his nose too hard draws blood (Prov. 30:33). So the most valiant defenders of liberty in Belgium showed, by a brilliant example that will live for all ages, that the bites of provoked necessity are most severe; and that men who had been held in gentle and mild rule remain most faithful, while cruelty and terror are weak bonds of charity. For men raised to courage only by just anger and despair (as usually happens, the wretched have more impetus and greater constancy), otherwise weaker in every way, fought so vigorously and so happily for their country and liberty, oppressed beyond law and right, that the most powerful enemy, after expending five hundred and sixty-four million (a sum he himself confessed to his son on his deathbed, in Meteranus book XIX, p. 878), and so many huge armies, and, what is the main thing, so much loss of the most noble provinces, at last came of his own accord to offer peace in the very heart of Holland. And those whom Count Charles Barlaymont, in a speech to the Regent in French, called Gueux (Gheusii), or beggars, so wore down the strength of the most wealthy and powerful King that no sensible person can any longer doubt that their pious and just cause was defended by the most present Divine Power.

units.la: CXIV. Illud verò crudelitatis numeros omnes implet, quòd eodem Impio suasore, Carolus Infans Hispaniæ, viginti duorum annorum juvenis, Belgis favere, creditus, in vincula à patre raptus, & propinato haustóque incautè veneno extinctus est: quódque etiam Regina ipsa Isabella, Philippi conjux, quòd pacis studiosior & amantior, quam in rem Papæ fuerit, visa; etiam secretiora consilia sanguinaria adversus Euangelicos Bajonæ Philippum inter & Galliæ Regem conclusa communicâsset, eidem fato succubuit. Ob quæ facinora, quasi gloriosa, Pontifex ille Philippo Regi auream rosam & gladium dono misit. Certè, Jesuita licet, Famianus Strada de Bello Belg. Dec. 1. lib. VII. p. m. 377. & 380. vim utrique illatam esse, non dissimulat. Et favorem erga Belgas Carolo perniciem attulisse, his ib. p. 377. verbis testatur: Hinc Caroli patrocinium studiumque in eos, quos patri offensos ejectósque sciret: in Belgas præcipuè, quorum Legatos Marchionem Bergensem atque Montinium solicitè complexus clam evocare ad se, tueríque eorum causam videbatur ardentiús, quàm par erat; pollicitus iis, iturum sese in BelBelgium ad componendos Provinciarum motus. Imò religionis gratia sublatum esse à Rege filium unicum, idem Rex testatus est, quando, referente eodem Strada, pag. 381. misso ad Archiepiscopum Rostanum, Pontificium Nuntium, Concilii Castellani Præside, eundem edocuit, rei illius causam non esse aliam, quam quod Religionis populorumque conservationem sanguini suo præhabere voluerit; coactúmque propterea se filium unicum sibi, ea ratione propemodum sacrificare, ne quibus affluebat à Deo beneficiis, nimis quàm ingrate responderet. Exemplum isthoc est exercitæ Bullæ Pauli IV. de pœnis hæreticorum, eorúmque qui iis favere creduntur; etiamsi, inquiebat ille, Imperiali vel Regali dignitate & excellentia præfulgerent.
units.tr: CXIV. Yet this deed fills up every measure of cruelty. By the same wicked adviser, Charles, Infante of Spain, a young man of twenty-two, who was believed to favour the Netherlanders, was seized by his father and cast into chains, and when he had been given poison to drink, carelessly swallowed, he was killed. Queen Isabella, the wife of Philip, was overtaken by the same fate, because she was seen to be more devoted to peace than suited the Pope's purposes, and because she had revealed to the Euangelici the bloody secret plans agreed at Bayonne between Philip and the King of France. For these crimes, which were thought glorious, that Pontiff sent King Philip a golden rose and a sword as a gift. Certainly, although he is a Jesuit, Famianus Strada, de Bello Belg. Dec. 1. lib. VII. p. m. 377 and 380, does not deny that violence was done to both. And he bears witness, in these words, ib. p. 377, that Charles's favour and zeal for the Netherlanders brought ruin upon him: Hence Charles's patronage and zeal towards those whom he knew to have been offended and driven out by his father; above all towards the Netherlanders, whose envoys, the Marquis of Bergen and Montigny, he eagerly embraced, secretly summoning them to himself and seeming to defend their cause more warmly than was right; he promised them that he would go to the Netherlands to settle the disturbances of the provinces. Indeed, the same king testified that his only son was removed on account of religion, when, as the same Strada reports, p. 381, he sent word to Archbishop Rostan, the Pope's nuncio and president of the Castilian council, and informed him that the cause of that affair was nothing other than that he had wished to put the preservation of the religion and of the peoples before his own blood; and that he had therefore been compelled to sacrifice his only son to him, in a manner, lest he should answer too ungratefully the benefits God lavished upon him. This is an example of the practice of the bull of Paul IV concerning the punishments of heretics and of those who are believed to favour them, even if, he said, they shone with imperial or royal dignity and eminence.

units.la: CXCV. Gregorii XIII. Bononiensis, qui antehac Hugonis Bon-Compagni nomine venit, juris humani consultissimi, at Divini ignarissimi, in Papatum succedentis initia ferales Eoæ illæ Parisienses S. Bartholomæi nomine non tam celebres, quàm ad omnem posteritatis memoriam infames, foedárunt. Nam eo Bartholomæi die A. M. D. LXXII. (cujus anni die XIII. May Gregorius Papatum adiit) & paucis aliquot sequentibus Catharina Medicea, Regis matre, germana Jezabele; & Duce Guisio incentoribus, neque inscio ipso Rege, tantum Christiani Evangelici sanguinis, ab iis, qui Christianissimi perhiberi volunt, effusum est, ut passim ejus rivuli vicorum alveos inundarent. Quin imò tandiu in viros fortissimos, in Regni Proceres, in florem utriusque sexus innocentissimum pulcherrimúmque, in multitudinem promiscuam, ab Orci emissariis sævitum est, quoad publica & nobilissima flumina repleta cadaveribus, & atrata sanguine conspecta sunt; ita ut accolis etiam longissimè distitis usus aquæ ad potum, aliásque res necessarias, nec non esus piscium humana carne saginatorum, magna cum execratione crudelitatis inauditæ carnificinæ, aliquantisper exosus & inutilis fuerit. Summa paucis illis diebus cœsorum, quod Rex ipse in Responsione ad Legatum Pontificis, teste in vita Gregorii XIII. Cicarella, fassus est, ad septuaginta millia, vel, ut alii colligebant, ad plus quàm centum millia Christianorum excurrit. Auxitque infamiam facinoris, quòd Rex crudelitatis notam, quam ne Thetys quidem universis undis suis abluerit, perjurii macula cumulavit.
