Finally the Pontiff severely annuls and rescinds all the acts of the clergy in the matter of the Regalia, in these words: Therefore, by these present letters, with the authority handed to us by Almighty God, we disapprove, rescind and quash whatever was done in your assembly in the matter of the Regalia, together with everything that followed from it, and whatever may be attempted in future; and we declare these things null for ever, although, being manifestly void in themselves, they would not need such quashing and declaration. We hope, however, that you yourselves, considering the matter better, will by a swift retraction consult your conscience and the esteem of the Gallican clergy; and we trust that, as such men have not been lacking until now, so in future there will not be lacking those who, following the example of the good Shepherd, are ready to lay down their lives for their sheep and for the testament of their fathers. Finally he declares and concludes his purpose for the future in these words: We, indeed, as the duty of our office requires, are ready, with God helping by his grace, to sacrifice the sacrifice of justice and to defend the rights and liberty of the Church of God and the authority and dignity of this Holy See, presuming nothing of ourselves but everything of God, who strengthens us and works all things in us, and who bade Peter come to him over the waters. For the figure of this world passes away, and the Day of the Lord draws near. So let us act, venerable brothers and beloved sons, that when the Supreme Shepherd, the Father of the household and the Prince of Shepherds, shall wish to demand an account from his servants, he may not require from our hands the blood of the ruined and torn Church which he acquired for himself. Meanwhile we impart to you all the Apostolic blessing, to which we wish the heavenly one to be added, with the inward affection of paternal love. At Rome, at St Peter's, under the Fisherman's ring, 2 April 1682, in the sixth year of our pontificate. It has not displeased us to give the words of this Bull, or Monitory, in full, so that the insolent arrogance of this Pontiff, by which he concedes little to his predecessors; his violent zeal (for the Archbishop of Toulouse is also said to have reproached him with this in a letter written to the Pope), a zeal not so much for his altars as for his hearths; and finally the remarkable artifice by which, under the veil of a holier discipline, faith, the danger of overturning the foundation of the Hierarchy and the testament of his Fathers (established certainly not by God the Father but by Hildebrands and Bonifaces for themselves and their fathers), he hides and covers his insatiable desires, for which, in the prophecy of Malachy of the Archbishop of Armagh, published already in the twelfth century, he is called by the name Insatiable Beast, may be seen more clearly by all. Whether the impostor clergy of France will change their mind and opinion and join their efforts to the authority of the Apostolic See, or not, the turning days will show.

units.la: CCCXLV. Cæterùm dissidium isthoc Regem inter & Pontificem funestissimum Reformatæ per Galliam Ecclesiæ accidisse, tristis experientia iterum docuit. Nunquam enim majoribus cum angustiis conflictata est, quàm eo ipso tempore, quo dissidium illud exarsit, arsitque maximè. Accedit quòd ipsa Cleri Gallicani Congregatio constituto transactóque Regaliæ negotio, ad consilia extirpandæ religionis in Regno universo Euangelicæ animum convertit; Concilii Arelatensis primi exemplum prætexens, utpote cujus Patres peracta re, cujus consiciendæ causa præsertim convenerant, ad cætera deinde animum intenderint, quæ Christianæ Reipublicæ commodis profutura esse intelligerent. Cùm verò in his tribus capitibus omnino pax & virtus Ecclesiæ tanquam solidis firmamentis contineatur, fide, moribus, disciplina. na ; in iisque stabiliendis iidem Concilii Arelatensis Patres operam collocaverint ; atque in iis fides præcipua sit, nihilque ad eam propugnandam plus adjumenti afferat, quàm si hæreses veritatis luce, & charitatis ardore schismata superentur, opera pretium esse, ita in Encyclicis suis ad universos Episcopos Galliæ Cal. Julii A.M.D. C.LXXXII. exaratis literis Congregatio loquitur, existimavimus, hæresin Calvinianam statim aggredi, eámque artem schismatis potiorem & in primis validam impugnare. Ad hoc excitatos inclinatósque se asserunt, tum charitate Christi, ex cujus Ecclesia una duæ sint à schismaticis factæ, tum Innocentii XI. vita moribus, sic ad veteris atque austerioris disciplinæ formam compositis, ut cum eo sentire Fidei suæ Adversariis recusandum non sit, cujus facta etiam imitari sibi, si verum loqui velint, optandum fateantur : tum Ludovici Magni quotidianis adversus Ecclesiam meritis, imò potiùs Regiæ fortitudinis, Christianæque pietatis miraculis, qui quot urbes hæreticas intra Galliæ fines ad pristinam avitámque fidem reduxerit, totidem Ecclesiæ Parenti, Filius natu æquè ac virtutibus major, incruentas victorias peperit. His, inquiunt, exemplis commoti, ac tantum non suspecti nobismetipsis negligentiæ in fungendo munere Pastorali, ad hæresin impugnandam nos accinximus. Quibus verò armis bellum isthoc cernere instituunt? Una, inquiunt, charitate, una Christi Domini pace, non objiciendo terrores, non certando contumeliis ; sed hortationibus, votis, precibus compellando adversarios, atque ad concordiam adducendos, eò quòd Christianæ societati, quæ cum iis intercedat, & Catholicæ matris affectui magis aptum & congruum fore duxerint, de gremio pacis Apostolicæ fugientes paternis monitis revocari. Quare, inquiunt, monemus cohortamurmúrque toto pondere charitatis inclinantes ad reconciliationem pacis, ut revertantur ad nos. Percunctamur iterum atque iterum, cur abscesserint, quare Catholicam unitatem repudiaverint: significamus quàm proclive futurum sit, plaga obducta semel persanari cætera, quæ medicina egere videbuntur; atque adeò pollicemur, si ex animo respiscant, à nobis esse, vel cum Matris Ecclesiæ quasi quodam incommodo recipiendos. Ne verò inde Reformati sumant occasionem sibi ac suis blandiendi spe inani suturae inter semetipsos dissociationis, quòd exorta sint nuperrimè Romanam inter & Gallicanam Ecclesiam nonnulla dissidia: admonent, primùm non de fidei doctrina, non de morum institutis, verùm de alternantis pro tempore disciplinæ rationibus aliquot, se cum Ministris Summi Pontificis, salva pace fraternæ charitatis contendere: deinde posse à Catholicis hominibus adversus Catholicos citra noxæ periculum, dum id more Christiano ac modo fiat, intra viscera Ecclesiæ, neque scisso utero disputari: ac postremo illam ipsam contentionem, quam fuscæperunt, & ipsis fugiendi exemplo suo scismatis, & sibi insectandi ejusdem causam esse oportere, quia in eam necessitatem adducti, ut querelis interdum apud Romanum Pontificem deferendis, Regni juribus interdum, vel Ecclesiæ suæ vindicandis privilegiis agerent, ea moderatione, reverentia, religione in re quavis disceptanda cernendáque usi fuerint, ut ne minimam quidem suspicionem charitatis læsæ moverint, nedum ut simultati locum ullum fecerint, aut divortio occasionem dederint. Atque hanc sui consilii de revocandis ad concordiam Schismaticis totam rationem esse, eámque ad Ecclesiæ Africanæ imitationem expressam, confirmant.
units.tr: CCCXLV. Moreover, the sad experience of the past has again shown that this quarrel between the King and the Pontiff was most disastrous for the Reformed Church throughout France. Indeed, the Church was never troubled by greater distress than at the very time when this quarrel broke out and burned most fiercely. In addition, the Congregation of the French Clergy itself, once the matter of the royal rights had been settled and concluded, turned its mind to plans for wiping out the Evangelical religion throughout the whole kingdom. It pleaded the example of the First Council of Arles, whose Fathers, once the business for which they had chiefly gathered was finished, turned their attention to other matters that they understood would benefit the Christian commonwealth. Since all peace and strength of the Church rest on these three heads, as on solid foundations (faith, morals and discipline), and since the same Fathers of the Council of Arles devoted their efforts to securing them, and since faith is the chief of these, and nothing contributes more to defending it than when heresies are overcome by the light of truth and schisms by the warmth of charity, the Congregation says in its Encyclical letters to all the Bishops of France, dated 1 July 1682: we have judged it worthwhile to attack at once the Calvinist heresy and to assail that art of schism, the more powerful and in the first place the more effective. They claim to have been roused and inclined to this by two things: first, the charity of Christ, from whose Church two parts have been made by the schismatics; and second, the life and morals of Innocent XI, which have been so shaped to the form of the old and stricter discipline that his opponents in the faith must not refuse to agree with him, whose deeds they also confess they would wish to imitate, if they are willing to speak the truth. They were moved also by the daily services of Louis the Great to the Church, or rather by the marvels of royal courage and Christian piety; for as many heretical cities as he has brought back within the borders of France to their former and ancestral faith, so many bloodless victories has he, greater as son by birth than by virtues, won for the Parent Church. Moved by these examples, they say, and not a little suspicious of our own negligence in discharging the pastoral office, we have girded ourselves to attack the heresy. But with what weapons do they propose to wage this war? With charity alone, they say, and with the peace of Christ the Lord alone: not by casting terrors, not by contending in insults, but by exhorting, praying and beseeching the adversaries and bringing them to concord; because they judged that those who have fled from the bosom of apostolic peace should be called back by fatherly admonitions, as this would be more fitting and suitable to the bond of Christian fellowship that exists between them and to the affection of the Catholic mother. Therefore, they say, we advise and exhort them, and bending with the full weight of charity towards reconciliation and peace, we ask that they return to us. We ask again and again why they have departed and why they have rejected Catholic unity. We point out how easy it will be, once the wound is closed, to heal the rest, which may seem to need remedy; and so we promise that if they repent from the heart, they are to be received by us, or rather by Mother Church, with a certain indulgence. But lest the Reformed take from this an occasion to flatter themselves and their own people with the empty hope of a future split among themselves, because of some recent disagreements between the Roman and the Gallican Church, they warn, first, that the French Clergy contends with the Ministers of the Supreme Pontiff, saving the peace of brotherly charity, not over the doctrine of faith or the institutions of morals, but only over some matters of discipline, which change with the times; second, that it is possible for Catholics to dispute among themselves, without danger of harm, provided this is done in a Christian way and manner, within the bowels of the Church and without tearing the womb; and last, that the very dispute which they have taken up ought, by their own example, to be a reason for the schismatics to flee and for them to pursue it, because they were brought to such a necessity that they had to act, sometimes by bringing complaints before the Roman Pontiff, sometimes by vindicating the rights of the Kingdom or the privileges of their own Church, and they used such moderation, reverence and scruple in handling and examining any matter whatever that they did not raise even the smallest suspicion of injured charity, much less give any place to enmity or occasion for divorce. They affirm that this whole reasoning of their plan, of calling the schismatics back to concord, is expressed on the model of the African Church.

units.la: CCCXLVI. Quis verò heic lectis perpensisque Cir- cularium literarum illarum tot artibus lenocinisque non judicium autobthoris.
units.tr: CCCXLVI. Who, then, having read and weighed those circular letters with so many of their arts and enticements, would not be wholly astonished at the author's judgment?

units.la: obstupescat totus? Etenim hæreses veritatis luce, schismata charitatis ardore superari, sapienter quidem Episcopi decernunt. Qua verò luce veritatis tot capita fidei, morum & disciplinæ cum iis controversa hactenus hæreseos unquam convicerunt? superârunt? Prostant bella Jehovæ à viris Dei bellata, quorum exitus abundè demonstrat, qua parte veritatis lux radiet. Neque novellæ illæ Methodi sedecim numero, ab Episcopis nisi fallor ad convertendos ad Papatum orthodoxos præscriptæ, & à Methodistis recentioribus variis emendicatæ, veritatis luce quenquam illustrare poterunt, cùm mera sophismata, & adversus invictum Dei verbum machinas carnalis sapientiæ, atque ludibria contineant. Quo dein charitatis ardore superare schisma contenderunt? Etenim si charitatis arma illa sunt, quibus à longo jam tempore adversus Reformatas Ecclesias decernunt, non utique docendo, instituendo, Cœlestis veritatis manifestatione omnium conscientiis sese veluti coram Deo commendando, insinuando; sed terrores terroribus cumulando, libertatis irrevocabilibus pactis concessæ nervos omnes concidendo, miserorum fortunas affligendo, Templa Regiis pactis concessa evertendo, impuberes seducendo, certamina emortualia decumbentium infestando, denique subdolis & erubescendis planè artibus, qualibus nunquam certè Christus, nunquam Apostoli, nunquam Episcopi, nunquam Imperatores Christiani veteres usi sunt, qualiúmque forte Gentiles ipsos olim puduisset; columbinam simplicitatem fidelium oppugnando, næ charitatis illo bello præclarè defunctos confitebimur. Quo charitatis ardore deinceps schisma aggressuri, superaturi sint, tempus, atque utinam non etiam profundissima tot fidelium suspiria & lachrymæ docebunt. Mirum præterea supra modum, quòd lectis jam Romani Pontificis literis Monitoriis, in animum venire Patribus illis potuit, ut suum non cum Ministris Pontificis, sed cum ipso Pontifice dissidium tantopere sibi extenuandum putaverint. De alternantis pro tempore disciplinae rationibus aliquot agi, ipsemet Pontifex diserte negavit, atque alio consilia relaxandi canonum disciplinam pro temporum necessitate, pertinere, denique, per abusum Regalia non solum everti disciplinam Ecclesiae, sed etiam fidei ipsius integritatem in discrimen vocari; disciplinae & Hierarchiae Ecclesiae fundamentum everti, gravibus adeo, sonantibusque verbis pertendit. Neque arbitrabimur nos, an ne minimam quidem laesae charitatis suspicionem moverint, nedum simultati cum Pontifice locum ullum fecerint, aut divortio occasionem dederint. Aliter tamen censere Pontificem, Monitoriae ejus literae, quarum initio statim testatur, Episcopos Clerumque Galliae, qui corona olim & gaudium fuerint Apostolicae Sedis, ita se erga illam in praesens gerere, ut cogatur ipse multis cum lachrymis usurpare Propheticum illud: Filii matris meae pugnaverunt adversus me; manifeste arguunt. Saltem majori jure Ecclesias nostras a Romano Pontifice dissidere, quando ejus potissimum culpa omnis religio & fides in Ecclesia depravata & lethaliter vulnerata est, atque ille, ut emendaret tot fidei, morum, disciplinae corruptelas, nulla ἀπόδειξις πνεύματος demonstratione Spiritus, precibus monitisque nullis flecti & adduci potuit, quin potius exasperatus etiam magis adversus demonstrantes, orantes, monentes anathemata vibravit, ferro flammaque immaniter saeviit: quam quo Ecclesiae Gallicanae Clerus a Romano Pontifice in re, quam parvi momenti esse censet, pertinaciter dissidet, dubitamus nulli. Verissime enim jam olim S. Nazianzenus Orat. 1. de pace pronuntiavit, ἐπὶ χρείων ἐμπαθῶς ὁμοιότης ἢ ὑπὲρ διστροφῆς βεβαίως βεἰας ἀλήθειαις contentionem pietatis causa susceптam concordia assectibus obnoxia potiorem esse.
units.tr: Indeed, the bishops wisely decree that heresies are overcome by the light of truth and schisms by the fire of charity. But by what light of truth have so many articles of faith, morals and discipline, long controverted with those men, ever convicted or overcome heresy? The wars of Jehovah, waged by the men of God, still stand, and their outcome amply shows on which side the light of truth shines. Nor can those new methods, sixteen in number, prescribed by the bishops for bringing the orthodox back to Papacy (unless I am mistaken), and begged together by various recent Methodists, illuminate anyone with the light of truth, since they contain nothing but mere sophisms, the machinery and mockeries of carnal wisdom against the unconquered Word of God. With what ardour of charity do they then mean to overcome the schism? For if those are the weapons of charity with which they have for a long time been fighting against the Reformed Churches, then it is not by teaching, instructing, and commending and insinuating themselves into everyone's conscience as before God through the manifestation of heavenly truth. Instead, they pile terror upon terror, cut down all the sinews of the liberty granted by irrevocable pacts, afflict the fortunes of the wretched, overturn temples conceded by royal pacts, seduce minors, harass the dying struggles of the sick, and, finally, use sly and frankly shameful arts, such as Christ never used, the Apostles never used, bishops never used, nor Christian emperors of old, and such as the Gentiles themselves might once have been ashamed of. They assail the dove-like simplicity of the faithful. We shall confess that they have acquitted themselves splendidly in that war of charity. With what ardour of charity they will next attack and overcome the schism, time will teach, and would that the deep sighs and tears of so many faithful did not also teach it. Moreover, it is exceedingly strange that, after the Roman Pontiff's monitory letters had been read, it could occur to those fathers that they should so greatly minimise their dissent, not with the ministers of the Pontiff, but with the Pontiff himself. The Pontiff expressly denied that various systems of discipline, changing with the times, were under discussion, and he insisted, in weighty and resounding words, that by abuse the Regalia not only overturn the discipline of the Church, but also put the integrity of the faith itself in peril, and that the foundation of the discipline and hierarchy of the Church is overturned. We shall not decide whether they "have moved not even the slightest suspicion of injured charity, much less given any occasion for enmity with the Pontiff or for divorce." Yet that the Pontiff thinks otherwise, his monitory letters plainly argue, in which he testifies at the very outset that the bishops and clergy of France, who once were the crown and joy of the Apostolic See, now so conduct themselves towards it that he is himself compelled, with many tears, to use that prophetic saying: "The sons of my mother fought against me." At least with greater right do our Churches dissent from the Roman Pontiff, since through his fault above all religion and faith in the Church has been corrupted and mortally wounded. And he, to correct so many corruptions of faith, morals and discipline, with no demonstration of the Spirit [ἀπόδειξις πνεύματος], could not be moved or persuaded by prayers or admonitions. Rather, exasperated all the more against those who demonstrated, prayed and admonished, he hurled anathemas and raged savagely with fire and sword. We doubt that anyone will deny that the Gallican clergy stubbornly dissent from the Roman Pontiff on a matter they judge of small importance. For Saint Gregory Nazianzen most truly pronounced long ago, in his first Oration on Peace, that contention undertaken for the sake of piety is better than a concord liable to passions [ἐπὶ χρείων ἐμπαθῶς ὁμοιότης ἢ ὑπὲρ διστροφῆς βεβαίως βεἰας ἀλήθειαις].

units.la: CCCXLVII. Circularibus illis ad Episcopos Galliæ literis junctæ erant aliæ, monitionis scilicet ad schismaticos exemplaria, quæ ut curent continuè nota fieri omnibus & singulis Calvinianæ Sectæ consistoriis, injunctæ iisdem est.
units.tr: CCCXLVII. Along with those circular letters to the bishops of France there were others, namely copies of the admonition to the schismatics, which the bishops were enjoined to see are continually made known to every single consistory of the Calvinist sect.

units.la: Prostant & illæ literæ, his verbis inscriptæ subscriptæque: Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, & Clerus Gallicanus omnis, auctoritate Regia Parisiis congregatus. Fratribus Secessionis Calvinianæ correctionem, reditum, concordiam exoptant. Exordium literarum gemitum Ecclesiæ universæ Christi ob secessionem illam sic pandit: Ingemiscit jam diu, Fratres, universa Christi Ecclesia, & maximo cum dolore plena Sanctæ ac Sinceræ pietatis Parens Vos ab utero, ab uberibus, à gremio suo voluntaria secessione abstractos, & in solitudine adhuc errantes videt. Numquid enim poterit Mater oblivisci Filiorum uteri sui? aut Ecclesia non meminisse charitatis erga Vos, male memores quidem, at Filios tamen suos, quos erroris contagio à veritate Catholica, & Calviniana defectionis tempestas à veteris Fidei Sanctitate abstraxit, à Capite Christianæ unitatis avulsit. Hinc est, Fratres, quòd illa ingemiscit, ac divisa sua viscera gravissimè pariter atque amantissimè conqueritur. Quærit Filios amissos, vocat ut perdix, ut Gallina congregare satagit, ut aquila provocat ad volandum, & maternis anxia doloribus conatur vos, Filioli, iterum parturire, donec verè & Catholicè in Vobis reformetur Christus.
units.tr: Those letters too survive, inscribed and subscribed with these words: "The archbishops, bishops, and the whole Gallican clergy, assembled at Paris by royal authority, wish correction, return and concord to the brethren of the Calvinist secession." The opening of the letter sets out the groaning of the whole Church of Christ over that secession in this way: "Long has the whole Church of Christ groaned, brethren, and full of the greatest grief, the Parent of holy and sincere piety sees you, torn away by voluntary secession from her womb, her breasts and her lap, still wandering in the wilderness. For can a mother forget the children of her womb? Or can the Church fail to remember her charity towards you, who are indeed ill-minded, yet still her sons, whom the contagion of error has torn from Catholic truth, and the storm of Calvinian defection has torn from the holiness of the old faith, and has wrenched from the Head of Christian unity? Hence it is, brethren, that she groans and laments her divided bowels most heavily and most lovingly alike. She seeks her lost sons, calls them as the partridge does, strives to gather them as the hen does, challenges them to fly as the eagle does, and anxious with maternal pains she tries to bring you, little sons, once more to birth, until Christ is truly and Catholically formed in you."

units.la: Tum rationem sibi reddi secessionis suæ à Papatu severè postulat his verbis: Nos adeò Clerus omnis Gallicanus, quos Spiritus S. posuit regere Ecclesiam, in qua nati estis, & qui hæreditate non interrupta eandem Fidem, eandem Cathedram tenemus, quam Sancti Pontifices, qui Christianam Religionem Galliis intulerunt; convenimus Vos, & qua legatione pro Christo defungimur, tanquam Deo exhortante per nos quærimus à vobis, cur schisma ma feceritis? Enimverò, ut se habent res vestræ, velitis nolitis, vos estis Fratres nostri ; quos olim unus omnium nostrûm Pater, qui in Cælis est, in adoptionem filiorum receperat, & quos una Mater Ecclesia in spem æternæ hæreditatis suscitulerat. Imò & ille ipse, qui Vos primus fascinavit non obedire veritatis Euangelio; Professionis nostræ Antesignamus, nonne antea nobiscum vivebat frater unanimis? non in eadem versari domo, non iisdem escis spiritalibus vesci, non mutua Christianæ nobiscum fraternitatis exequi solebat officia? Excusate, si potestis, apud Patrem, apud Matrem, apud Fratres, fugæ tam flagitiosæ, tam abruptæ ac præcipitis infamiam. Divisionem Christi, rescissionem Sacramentorum Christi, bellum impium in membra Christi, criminationes in conjugem Christi, negationem promissionum Christi excusate, abluite, si potestis; & quoniam non potestis, oraculo Prophetico vos fatemini obnoxios: Filius malus justum se dicit, exitum autem suum abluere non potest. Quorsum itaque, Fratres, in radice cum orbe toto non mansistis? Cur vota ac desideria Fidelium cum ipsis altaribus confregistis? cur conscidistis precibus viam? Illuc ascensus ad Deum fuit, cur ne more consueto ad Deum fieret oratio, scalam tollere de lapide & sacrilega manu subducere laborâstis? Cæteri adhuc Sectarii hoc moliti erant, non ut altare Christi subverteretur, sed ut adversus altare Christi & suum ipsi qualecunque extollerent. Vos ne quid superesset sacrificii Christiani, inauditum ad hæc tempora facinus, ausi estis diruere altaria Domini virtutum, in quibus Passer Christus elegerat sibi domum, & Turtur Ecclesia nidum sibi, ubi poneret pullos suos. At hæc prostrema, & quodcunque deinceps aut bellorum contra Ecclesiam, aut errorum contra antiquum dogma consecutum est, schismaticus furor effecit; nec tam vestræ voluntati, quàm schismatis ingenio volumus esse tribuendum. Hoc adversus Vos nominatim expostulamus, hoc ex vobis quærimus indesinenter, cur schisma feceritis? Ad hoc nisi responderitis, quantumcunque in aliis dicendo aut scribendo contendatis, superflua loquimini. Tum causam secessionis petitam à moribus hominum, quibuscum vivere sanctiores viri, & legum severiores amatores, nec honestum ad famam, nec salubre ad conscientiam duxerint, diluere multis conati, sic Fratres hos ad reditum invitant: Quid jam superest, Fratres, nisi ut isti Spiritus S. consilio vestri causa precamur: Beati pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur. Et per viscera misericordiæ, quæ lacerāstis hactenus, per Ecclesiæ Matris uterum, quem rupistis; per charitatem Fratrum, quam toties violastis, per Sacramenta Dei, quæ contempsistis; per Altaria Dei, quæ confregistis; per quicquid Sanctum ac Divinum, aut in Cælo, aut in terris colitur, Vos fraternis animis ad correctionem, ad reditum, ad concordiam hortamur. Imò quid iam superest omnino, nisi ut obliti schismatis, & memores uberum revertamini ad propria, ubi tot mercenarii abundant panibus, dum in terra deserta, invia & inaquosa, ne micas quidem ad sustentandam utcunque famem vestram spiritualem colligitis? Ecquid verò conjectamini aut resistitis? Itáne verò in Filiorum nomine erubescitis, inter quos primogenitus Ludovicus Ecclesiæ Matri Optimæ nova erigit quotidie trophæa? hoc uno sanè, vestra obstante pertinacia, non satis felix, quòd tametsi pro tuendo nomine Christiano multa in dies religiosè ac piè constituat, è suorum numero subditorum, qui à sacris patriis defecerunt sponte, & ad ritus alienos convolárunt, Religionis transfugas, veteris militiæ desertores, etiamnum videat in suscepto errore permanentes: isque adeò Christianissimus Princeps, qui, nobis audientibus ajebat nuper, tanto studio cupere se dispersas disjectásque partes ad Ecclesiæ unitatem revocari, ut id mereri duceret gloriosum, vel Regii sui sanguinis effusione, atque etiam illius invictissimi brachii diminutione, quo tot bella feliciter confecisset. Vósne igitur, Fratres, Augustissimo Principi, Regi vestro, plurimorum ac potentissimorum hostium Debellatori, fortissimarum urbium Expugnatori, maximarum Provin-ciatiarum Dominatori, omni genere triumphorum insigni, eam palmam invidebitis, quam cæteris omnibus anteponat? Cæterùm dum vos ita compellamus, & ad pacis consilia hortamur, ne dicatis: Nolite nos quærere: nam hoc dicit iniquitas, qua divisi sumus, non charitas, qua Christiani sumus. Meminerit is, ita esse mandatum nobis à Spiritu veritatis & Pacis per Prophetam, ut qui se negant esse Fratres nostros, iis dicere non desinamus; Vos estis Fratres nostri. At quod tempus offerri nobis opportunius potest Vos ad Romanam communionem revocandi, quàm quo Romanam Ecclesiam gubernat Innocentius Pontifex, cujus vita & mores ad antiquioris & severioris disciplinæ formam exacti perfectum sanctitatis exemplar orbi exhibent Christiano? Ut ad eum se adjungere virtutis omnis cultorem eximium maximæ virtutis opus ad salutem perinde ut ad gloriam in Vobis futurum sit. Subjunctis novis corhortationibus, tandem Epistola in comminationes non obscuras definit: Quòd si inquiunt illi, facere adhortantibus nobis pertinaci animo renuitis; Si nec precibus vinci, nec flecti charitate, nec monitis adduci ad concordiam vultis; Angeli quidem pacis amare flebunt; nec tamen vos continuò, ut fieri par esset erga nimium pervicaces, relinquemus vobis: sed per sepes & spinas oves Christi quærere non desinemus: & cùm effecerimus omnia, propter quæ mentes vestræ nobis reconciliari debuerint, pax nostra demum, vobis eam respuentibus, tam officiosè, tam sincerè oblatam, revertetur ad nos, nec amplius requiret Deus animas vestras de manu nostra; & quemadmodum error hic vester novissimus erit pejor prioribus, sic erunt novissima vestra pejora prioribus. Veruntamen meliora speramus, Fratres, & saluti vestræ viciniora.
units.tr: Then he sharply demands an account of their secession from the Papacy, in these words: We, the whole Gallican clergy, whom the Holy Spirit has set to rule the Church in which you were born, and who hold by uninterrupted inheritance the same faith and the same chair that the holy bishops held, who brought the Christian religion into Gaul, meet with you. Discharging the embassy we bear for Christ, and as though God were exhorting you through us, we ask you: why have you made a schism? For, however things stand between you and us, whether you will or no, you are our brothers, whom our one Father in heaven once received into the adoption of sons, and whom our one Mother the Church raised up to the hope of an everlasting inheritance. Indeed, was not he himself, who first bewitched you so that you would not obey the Gospel of truth, the standard-bearer of our profession? Did he not once live with us as a united brother, dwell in the same house, feed on the same spiritual food, and perform the mutual duties of Christian brotherhood with us? If you can, make your excuses before the Father, before the Mother, before the brothers, for the infamy of so shameful, so sudden and headlong a flight. Excuse and cleanse, if you can, the division of Christ, the tearing of Christ's sacraments, the impious war against the members of Christ, the accusations against the spouse of Christ, the denial of the promises of Christ. And since you cannot, you confess yourselves liable to the prophetic saying: "The evil son says he is righteous, but he cannot cleanse his own outgoing." Why then, brothers, did you not remain in the root together with the whole world? Why did you break the prayers and desires of the faithful together with the altars themselves? Why did you cut off the way with prayers? There was an ascent to God by that route. Why did you labour, with a sacrilegious hand, to remove the ladder from the stone, so that prayer might not be made to God in its usual manner? The other sectaries up to now were aiming at this, not that the altar of Christ should be overturned, but that they might raise up their own, whatever it was, against the altar of Christ. You dared, so that nothing of Christian sacrifice might remain, a crime unheard of until these times: to pull down the altars of the Lord of hosts, in which Christ the sparrow had chosen a house for himself, and the Church the turtle-dove a nest, where she might place her young. But these last disasters, and whatever has since followed, whether wars against the Church or errors against the ancient doctrine, the schismatic frenzy has brought about. We wish that this be attributed not so much to your will as to the nature of schism. This we demand of you by name, this we ask of you without ceasing: why have you made a schism? Unless you answer this, however much you contend in speaking or writing about other matters, you are talking to no purpose. Then, having tried at length to refute the reason for the secession, which was drawn from the conduct of the men with whom holier men and lovers of stricter laws thought it neither honourable for their reputation nor wholesome for their conscience to live, they invite these brothers back in this way: What, brothers, now remains, except that we pray, for your sake, by the counsel of the Holy Spirit: "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God." And by the bowels of mercy, which you have hitherto torn; by the womb of Mother Church, which you have broken; by the brotherly love, which you have so often violated; by the sacraments of God, which you have despised; by the altars of God, which you have broken; by whatever is holy and divine, worshipped either in heaven or on earth, we exhort you with brotherly hearts to correction, to return, to concord. Indeed, what now remains at all, except that, forgetting the schism and mindful of the breasts, you return to your own home, where so many hired workers abound with bread, while in a desert, pathless and waterless land you gather not even crumbs to sustain your spiritual hunger in any way? Do you indeed consider or resist? Do you blush in the name of sons, among whom the firstborn Louis raises new trophies every day for the best Mother the Church? Truly this one thing, because of your stubbornness, is not sufficiently happy: although on behalf of defending the Christian name he devoutly and piously establishes many things each day, yet he sees among the number of his subjects those who have of their own accord fallen away from the sacred rites of their fathers and flocked to foreign rites, deserters from the faith, deserters from the old army, still persisting in the error they have embraced. And yet this most Christian Prince, who lately said in our hearing that he so eagerly desired the scattered and dispersed parts to be recalled to the unity of the Church that he thought it a glorious thing to merit this, even by the shedding of his royal blood and even by the loss of that most invincible arm with which he had so successfully finished so many wars. Will you then, brothers, begrudge the most august Prince, your King, the conqueror of very many and very powerful enemies, the storm-breaker of the strongest cities, the lord of the greatest provinces, distinguished by every kind of triumph, that palm which he prefers above all others? Moreover, while we thus address you and exhort you to the counsels of peace, do not say: "Do not seek us," for this is what iniquity says, by which we are divided, not charity, by which we are Christians. Let him remember that it has been commanded to us by the Spirit of truth and of peace, through the prophet, that we should never cease to say to those who deny that they are our brothers: "You are our brothers." But what more opportune time can be offered to us to recall you to the Roman communion than this, when Innocent rules the Roman Church as Pontiff, whose life and morals, conformed to the form of the older and stricter discipline, present to the Christian world a perfect example of holiness? That you may join yourselves to him as an outstanding cultivator of every virtue, so that the greatest work of virtue may be in you, for your salvation no less than for your glory. After adding fresh exhortations, the letter at last ends in threats that are not obscure: But if, they say, you are unwilling, with obstinate minds, to do what we urge; if you will not be conquered by prayers, nor bent by charity, nor brought to concord by admonitions, the angels of peace will indeed weep bitterly. Nor, however, shall we then leave you altogether, as would be fitting towards those who are too obstinate, but we shall not cease to seek the sheep of Christ through hedges and thorns; and when we have done all things for which your minds ought to have been reconciled to us, our peace, offered so dutifully and so sincerely, if you reject it, will at last return to us, and God will no longer require your souls at our hand. And just as this your latest error will be worse than the earlier ones, so your last things will be worse than the first. Nevertheless, brothers, we hope for better things, and things nearer to your salvation.

units.la: CCCXLVIII. Operæ pretium duxi pleraque E- pistolæ illius verba, in quibus favum stillant labia זרח Ex- traneæ, & lenius est oleo palatum ejus; sed אחריתה novissi- mum ejus, amarum sicut absinthium, acutum veluti gladius biceps
units.tr: CCCXLVIII. I have thought it worth setting out most of the words of that letter, in which the lips of the Strange Woman [זרה] drip honey and her mouth is smoother than oil; but her end [אחריתה] is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword.

units.la: Fucus earum-dem detectus. (Prov. v. 34.) repræsentare ἀλλοφυλίω, ne posteritatem lateat, qua contentione, quo fuco, qua φιλοδολόγων ψευδο-λογίας hypocrisi falsiloquorum, quibúsve illecebris artibúsque negotium isthoc gestum sit. Enimverò post rationem secessionis, non à vera Christi fideliúmque Ecclesia, sed ab inhærente sociatáque ad tempus eidem Papali factione, cui non magis quàm Donatistis olim, universæ Christi Ecclesiæ nomen congruit; institutæ, non ob mores duntaxat, uti Clerus falsò persuadere conatur, sed ob religionem, fidem, cultúmque omnem, tyrannide affectata in conscientiam, superstitione & idolomania, denique erroribus capitalibus cum verbi Divini veritate hostiliter pugnantibus, miserè corruptum, lethalíque tabe & veneno infectum imbutúmque; toties verè, graviter, seriò ipsius verbi Divini, immoti veritatis principii, non μύθων στοφισμάτων fabularum arte confictarum authoritate, redditam, tot Sanctorum Martyrum sanguine obsignatam: post stabilitum authoritate Regia in tot Regni locis religionis Reformatæ exercitium liberum: post tot Templa contra fas Edictorum diruta, tot calamitates miseris inflictas; quin & ipso persecutionum ardentium æstu, inquirere denuo in causam schismatis, quid, inquam, hoc aliud est, quàm in re seria ludere, vel, si intentionem inquirentium spectamus, πῶς κεφάλῃ ϑανάτῳ crambe bis posita mors? Liceat de χρηστολόγοις blandiloquis & benedicentibus ejusmodi illa Gregorii M. Moral. xxxiii. 36. usurpare: Assumunt Agni speciem, ut Draconis exerceant operationem. Quomodo verò diviserunt Christum, qui solùm Christum optârunt; non desiderantes cognoscere aliud, quàm Christum crucifixum? Quomodo Sacramenta Christi rescinderunt, qui à Christo non instituta respuerunt? Quomodo bellum impium im membra Christi gesserunt, qui cum Christo ejúsque que veris membris omnibus vera fide & charitate indivulsi cohærent? Quomodo Sponsam Christi criminati sunt, qui eandem uni viro Christo, castam virginem adjungere, omni studio curáque laborárunt? Quomodo negárunt promissionem Christi, qui sola ea freti non timuerunt hactenus, quid sibi caro faceret? Quomodo excisi sunt à radice, qui fide in solum Christum, radicem Jesse, ῥιζωθέντες τῇ χρηστότητι permanentes in benignitate ejus, consistunt? Quomodo confregerunt altare verum, Christum, qui altaria, vota desideria hominum, à vero altari Christo, & fiducia in eodem solo collocanda, abstrahentia verbi Divini authoritate freti removerunt? Quomodo precibus viam conscciderunt, quibus solus Jesus Christus justus Paracletus ad Deum via, veritas & vita est? Quomodo sustulerunt scalam de lapide, qui uni Lapidi in Sione fundato pretioso, angulari summo, adeóque ab imo ad summum usque penetranti, pertingenti, Lapidis illius, cujus in Cœlum usque porrecta scala est, antitypo soli, superstructi confidentésque non erubescunt? Quomodo sustulerunt sacrificium Christianum, qui altaria lignea fictitiarum virtutum Domini contra altare nostrum Christum, qui super omnes Cœlos ascendit, ut impleret omnia, erecta & in quibus nec passer Christus, nec turtur Ecclesia unquam sibi pullisve suis nidum fixere, pensi amplius non habent? Quomodo denique moverunt bellum Ecclesiæ, errores contra antiquum dogma feminârunt, qui pro antiquo dogmate non diligentes animas suas usque ad mortem, Archiepiscopis interea, Episcopis, totóque Clero Gallicano inveterati erroris sui pertinacia, & dominantium in partes abreptorum consensu tuto, assueta sibi pompa deliciisque solitis diffluente, ac de cœtero adversus innocuam plebem Christi ad flammam ferrúmque sine fine ne & modo conclamante; tot mala, vivicomburia, lanienas inauditas, vitæ discrimina, fortunarum incendia sustinuerunt; quandoque etiam adversus Henoticos religionis prætextu dominationi inhiantes, hæredem Regni, se religionémque vindicantes strenuè defensitárunt? Quam igitur causam expostulandi adversus innocentes oppressos, toties vim Cleri conscientiis eorum dominantis injustam passos, habuerunt? Quin potiùs Cleri Gallicani Pontificii est reddere rationem schismatis, divortii, secessionis perniciosissimæ omnium à Christo ad Papam, ἀντιχειστον vicarium Christi sese venditantem sine tabulis juris Divini, imò adversus authoritatem earundem, efferentémque se adversus omne id, quod Deus est & dicitur: à lege Christi, ad legem Papæ: à vivis aquis limpidísque fontibus verbi Divini, ad olidas cisternas traditionum humanarum, eorúmque incertarum planè & fluxæ fidei; à sacrificio Christi cruento, ad incruentum Missaticum; à Christi intercessione & invocatione, ad intercessionem & invocationem Sanctorum, sive verorum, sive fictitiorum; à justitia Christi, Euangelica, in qua sola Deus acquiescit, ad justitiam propriam, humanam, qua freti olim Judæi justitiam Divinam amiserunt; à cultu unius soliúsque Dei ad cultum hominum, auri, argenti, ligni, lapidum, ossium, aliarúmque rerum Divinitatis expertium, ut infinita ejusmodi, ob quæ cum Pontificia communione, si fidem, conscientiámque suam salvam vellent nostri, nulla iis συμφωνησις, συγκαταθεσις, nullum consortium commerciúmque, communio nulla esse potuit, silentio præteream. Cùm verò à Christo, ejúsque Ecclesia vera & Catholica nunquam Reformati in Gallia discessionem fecerint, sed Reformatione sua scorias duntaxat, sordésque ab auro & argento, lapidibúsque pretiosis cœlestis doctrinæ, paleas à tritico, vile à pretioso feperaverint, non iis utique ad communionem Papatus, sed Clero potiùs ad Christum verámque & Catholicam ejus, à qua devius errat, Ecclesiam, cum qua Reformatæ Ecclesiæ Galliæ conjunctissimæ sunt, revertendum fuerit, juxta consilium Dei falutberrimum, quod his verbis Jerem. xv. 19. consignatum legimus: Propterea sic dixit Jehova: Si conversus fueris, tunc convertam Te, & coram me stabis. Et si eduxeris pretiosum à vili, tanquam os meum eris. Convertentur ipsi ad te, & tu non converteris ad ipsos. Religio-igitur sit Vobis, o Fideles, Sanctificati, Asserti semel & illuminati à Spiritu Dei, o inops, imbellis, moesta לחיית Congregatiomi (ita nonnulli Psal. lxxix. 19. interpretantur) tradita Turtur, quæ, amisso, vel abscondente potiùs se ad tempus Compare tuo, apud Te & Deum Tuum solum plorabunda ingemiscis; religio, inquam, sit Vobis audire voces & lenocinia Extraneæ, ad amores suos pellicientis, adhortante vos graviter Spiritu Dei per Sapientissimum Mortalium Prov. v. 20. 21. Ut quid delectaberis, Fili mi, cum Aliena, & amplecteris sinum Extraneæ? Quando coram oculis Jehovæ sunt viæ viri, & omnes semitas ejus ponderat. Iniquitates suæ capient ipsum Impium, funibus peccati sui tenebitur. Ipse morietur, eò quòd non audivit eruditionem: & propter multitudinem stultitiæ suæ errabit.
units.tr: The mask of these same people is exposed. (Prov. v. 34.) I must set forth the foreign woman [ἀλλοφυλίω], so that posterity may not be ignorant by what contention, by what mask, by what hypocrisy of lying words of the lovers of falsehood [φιλοδολόγων ψευδολογίας], and by what enticements and arts this business was carried out. Indeed, what reason for the secession is there? It was not made from the true Church of Christ and the faithful, but from a faction clinging to the Papacy and allied to it for a time, to which the name of the whole Church of Christ fits no better than it once fitted the Donatists. It was founded not merely, as the clergy try falsely to persuade us, on morals, but on religion, faith and all worship: on a tyranny that laid hold of conscience, on superstition and idolatry, and finally on capital errors that fight hostilely against the truth of the Divine Word, and so it was miserably corrupted, infected and steeped in deadly rot and poison. Again and again, truly, gravely and seriously, the authority of the Divine Word itself, the unmoving principle of truth, not tales invented by the art of fables [μύθων στοφισμάτων], was restored; it was sealed by the blood of so many holy martyrs; after the free exercise of the Reformed religion was established by royal authority in so many places of the kingdom; after so many temples were demolished in defiance of right and edicts, and so many calamities were inflicted on the wretched; and even in the very heat of burning persecutions, they now inquire again into the cause of the schism. What, I ask, is this but to play at a serious matter, or, if we look at the intention of the inquirers, a cabbage served twice, death to the head [πῶς κεφάλῃ ϑανάτῳ]? Let me borrow from Gregory the Great, Moralia xxxiii. 36, those words about such flatterers and blessers: They take on the appearance of the Lamb, so that they may carry out the work of the Dragon. But how did they divide Christ, who desired only Christ and did not wish to know anything other than Christ crucified? How did they rescind the sacraments of Christ, who rejected what Christ did not institute? How did they wage impious war against the members of Christ, who cling inseparably to Christ and to all his true members in true faith and charity? How did they accuse the Bride of Christ, who have laboured with all zeal to join her, a chaste virgin, to one husband, Christ? How did they deny the promise of Christ, who, relying on that alone, have hitherto not feared what flesh might do to them? How have they been cut off from the root, who stand by faith in Christ alone, the root of Jesse, rooted in the kindness [ῥιζωθέντες τῇ χρηστότητι], remaining in the goodness of him? How did they break the true altar, Christ, who, relying on the authority of the Divine Word, removed the altars, vows and desires of men, which ought to be placed in the true altar Christ and in trust in him alone? How did they cut off the way of prayer, in which Jesus Christ alone, the righteous Advocate, is the way, the truth and the life to God? How did they take away the ladder from the stone, they who, not blushing, build on that one precious stone laid in Zion, the chief corner stone, which reaches and penetrates from bottom to top, the antitype of that stone on which a ladder stretches up to heaven? How did they take away the Christian sacrifice, they who now have no concern for the wooden altars of fictitious virtues erected against our altar, Christ, who ascended above all the heavens that he might fill all things, and where neither the sparrow Christ nor the turtle-dove Church ever fixed a nest for herself or her young? Finally, how did they make war on the Church, sowing errors against the ancient doctrine, they who, not loving their souls unto death for the ancient doctrine, meanwhile endured, with the obstinacy of their long-standing error and with the consent of the dominant factions, the archbishops, bishops and the whole Gallican clergy, who, safe and flowing in their accustomed pomp and usual delights, cried out without end for flame and sword against the innocent people of Christ; they endured so many evils, burnings alive, unheard-of butcheries, dangers to life, fires to fortunes; and at times, against the Henotics who gaped for domination under the pretext of religion, they vigorously defended themselves, claiming the heir of the kingdom and religion? What cause then did they have for complaint against the innocent oppressed, who so often suffered the unjust violence of the clergy's dominion over their consciences? Rather, it is for the Gallican Papist clergy to give an account of the schism, the divorce, the most pernicious secession of all from Christ to the Pope, who boasts himself the vicar [ἀντιχειστον] of Christ without the tables of Divine law, indeed against their authority, lifting himself up against everything that is God and is called God: from the law of Christ to the law of the Pope; from the living, limpid fountains of the Divine Word to the stinking cisterns of human traditions, and their uncertain and utterly fleeting faith; from the bloody sacrifice of Christ to the unbloody Mass; from the intercession and invocation of Christ to the intercession and invocation of saints, whether real or fictitious; from the Gospel righteousness of Christ, in which alone God rests, to our own human righteousness, relying on which the Jews once lost the divine righteousness; from the worship of the one and only God to the worship of men, of gold, silver, wood, stones, bones and other things devoid of divinity. I pass over in silence the countless such things, because of which, if our people wished to keep their faith and conscience safe, there could be no agreement [συμφωνησις], assent [συγκαταθεσις], no fellowship or dealings, no communion at all with Papal communion. But since the Reformed in France never made a secession from Christ and his true and Catholic Church, but by their Reformation only purged the dross and filth from gold and silver, and the stones of heavenly doctrine, the chaff from the wheat, the base from the precious, it was in no way for them to return to communion with the Papacy; rather the clergy ought to return to Christ and his true and Catholic Church, from which they wander astray, with which the Reformed Churches of France are most closely joined, according to the most wholesome counsel of God, which we read sealed in these words of Jeremiah xv. 19: Therefore thus said the LORD: If you return, then I will bring you back, and you shall stand before me. And if you bring forth the precious from the vile, you shall be as my mouth. They shall turn to you, but you shall not turn to them. Let it be your duty, O faithful, sanctified, once asserted and enlightened by the Spirit of God, O poor, unwarlike, sorrowful congregation (so some interpret Ps. lxxix. 19), the turtle-dove given up, who, having lost your mate, or rather hiding him for a time, mourn and groan before you and your God alone; it should be your duty, I say, to hear the voices and enticements of the Strange Woman, who lures you to her loves, while the Spirit of God earnestly urges you through the wisest of mortals, Prov. v. 20–21: Why will you delight, my son, in the stranger, and embrace the bosom of the foreign woman? For the ways of a man are before the eyes of the LORD, and he weighs all his paths. The iniquities of the wicked will take him, and he will be held fast in the cords of his sin. He shall die because he did not receive instruction, and because of the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.

units.la: CCCXLIX. Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν δι' ταῦτα. Produximus enim, uti institutum nostrum ferebat, Ecclesiæ Romanæ historiam ad nostra usque tempora, quæ ob ejusdem adversus veram Ecclesiam Christi odium inveteratum & ἀκαταλλάκτον, crescentem in dies saevitiam, magnámque insidiarum, moliminum, persecutionum tum aperte crudelium, tum occultè graviúsque ignis instar, qui erumpere non valens periculosius interiora appetit, saevientium. & ima viscera Ecclesiæ arrodentium, molem עת רעה tempus malum Amos. v. 13. & Καιρὸς χαλεπὸς tempora dissicilia 2 Timoth. iii. 1. dixeris merito. Exiverunt pridem, exeúntque quotidie ex portis Ecclesiæ hujus seductores Spiritus ad Reges terræ & habitabilis totius, ut eos congregent ad prœlium diei illius magnæ Dei Omnipotentis in locum Harmageddon Hebraicè dictum. Ecce, ita interea Filius Dei ex Cœlo fideles suos alloquitur, venio sicut fur. Beatus qui vigilat, & custodit vestimenta sua, ne nudus ambulet, & videant turpitudinem ejus, Apoc. xvi. 14–17.
units.tr: CCCXLIX. And so much for these matters [Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν δι' ταῦτα]. For, as our plan required, we have brought the history of the Church of Rome down to our own times. Because of that Church's long-standing and irreconcilable hatred of the true Church of Christ, and its raging cruelty growing day by day, and its great mass of plots, machinations and persecutions, some openly cruel, some hidden and more grievous, like a fire that, unable to break out, eats more dangerously into the inner parts and gnaws at the very vitals of the Church, you may rightly call it an evil time [עת רעה] (Amos v. 13) and perilous times [Καιρὸς χαλεπὸς] (2 Tim. iii. 1). Seducing spirits have long gone out, and go out every day, from the gates of this Church, to the kings of the earth and of the whole inhabited world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty, into the place called Harmagedon in Hebrew. Meanwhile the Son of God speaks to his faithful from heaven: Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he who watches and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and men see his shame, Apoc. xvi. 14–17.

units.la: CCCL. Tu verò ROMA,
units.tr: CCCL. But you, ROME,

units.la: Spurcum cadaver pristinæ venustatis, Imago turpis puritatis antiquæ. Nec Roma Romæ compos, sed tamen Roma, Sed Roma, quæ præstare non potes Romam, Sed quæ foveris fraude, quæ foves fraudem. Vrbs prurienti quæ obsoletior scorto, Et obsoleti more pruriens scorti, Quæ pene victa fæce prostitutarum Te prostituta vincis, & tuum facta es Tibi Lupanar in tuo lupanari. Vale pudoris urbs inanis & recti, Tui pudoris nominisque decoctrix, Turpis litura non merentium rerum, Ocelle quondam, nunc lacuna Fortunæ Negotiosa mater otiosarum. Vale nefanda, constuprata, corrupta, Incesta cœlibum Quiritium manceps!
units.tr: Foul corpse of your former beauty, image of the ugly purity of old. You are not Rome in your right mind, and yet you are still Rome, but Rome that cannot make Rome great, a Rome that you have been fostered by fraud and that fosters fraud. City, more worn out than a whore and lustful in the manner of a worn-out whore, who, nearly beaten by the dregs of prostitutes, outdo them by prostituting yourself, and have become a brothel to yourself in your own brothel. Farewell, city empty of modesty and of right, destroyer of your own modesty and name, ugly blot upon deserving things, once a darling, now the pit of Fortune, busy mother of the idle. Farewell, unspeakable, debauched, corrupted, incestuous dealer in the celibate Quirites!

units.la: Tu omnium in Christiano Orbe malorum causa es, quorum tibi coram Deo forti, justo, Zelote reddenda erit quandoque ratio. Propter te mactantur, affliguntur, vexantur tot millia hominum Christum Salvatorem suum ve-rè rè & purè colentium. Tibi omnis ille sanguis innocentissimorum effusus est. Tibi omnis suscepta vexatio, patrata persecutio est. Non alia tot persecutionum, tot infictorum malorum causa, ac ne prætextus quidem alius est, quàm quòd Christiani tuam illam, nullo jure, nullo titulo hactenus in fidem & conscientiam eorum usurpatam, Apostolicam videlicet, authoritatem agnoscere sicut non potuerunt, ita noluerunt. Homines tu quidem fallere potuisti, & poteris, quousque justè sanctéque permiserit Dominus. Sed disposita jam fata tua sunt. DEUS destruet Te in finem, evellet te, & emigrare te faciet de tabernaculo tuo, & radicem tuam de terra viventium. Arguet te, & statuet se contra faciem tuam. De Te, & Tibi dicta noveris ferientia illa oracula: Et vidi mulierem sedentem super bestiam coccineam, plenam nominibus blasphemiæ, habentem capita septem, & capita decem. Et mulier erat circumdata purpura, & coccino, & inaurato auro, lapide pretioso, & margaritis, habens poculum aureum in manu sua, plenum abominatione & immunditia fornicationis ejus. Et in fronte nomen ejus scriptum: Mysterium: Babylon illa magna, mater fornicationum & abominationum terræ. Cecidit, cecidit Babylon illa Magna: quæ à vino iræ fornicationis suæ potavit omnes gentes. Justus es Domine, qui es, & qui eras Sanctus, qui hæc judicâsti; quia sanguinem Sanctorum & Prophetarum effuderunt, & sanguine potâsti eos. digni enim sunt. Babylon magna venit in memoriam ante Deum, ut detur illi calix vini indignationis iræ ejus. Quæ Tibi soli examuíssim & παροιμίας convenire, deinceps, νῦν ἡ̃ς παλάμα manifestum faciemus. At clamant interea animæ decollatorum afflictorumque omnium propter testimonium Jesu, & propter verbum Dei, subtus altare Dei: USQUE QUO DOMINE, SANCTE ET VERAX, NON JUDICAS ET NON VINDICAS SANGUINEM NOSTRUM Ecclesia triumphantis mul tantisque ardentia vota.
units.tr: You are the cause of all the evils in the Christian world, for which you will one day have to give account before God, who is strong, just, and jealous. Because of you so many thousands of men who truly and purely worship Christ as their Saviour are slaughtered, afflicted and harassed. All that innocent blood has been shed for you. All the persecution undertaken and carried out has been for you. There is no other cause and no other pretext for so many persecutions and so many inflicted evils than that Christians have not been able, and have not been willing, to acknowledge that authority of yours, which, though you have usurped it over their faith and conscience until now, has no right and no title, namely the authority of the Apostles. You indeed have been able to deceive men, and will be able to do so, for as long as the Lord justly and holily permits. But your fates are already decided. God will destroy you utterly, will pluck you up, and will make you depart from your tent, and your root from the land of the living. He will convict you, and will set himself against your face. Know that those striking oracles are spoken about you and to you: "And I saw a woman sitting upon a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns. And the woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, and decked with gold, precious stone and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand, full of abominations and the filthiness of her fornication. And upon her forehead a name was written: Mystery, Babylon the Great, the mother of harlots and abominations of the earth. Fallen, fallen is Babylon the Great, which made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication. Just art thou, O Lord, who art and wast holy, who hast judged these things, for they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and thou hast given them blood to drink; for they are worthy. Babylon the Great came into remembrance before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath." Which things we shall make plain, in what follows, to fit you alone exactly, as the proverb says [παροιμίας], now [νῦν ἡς παλάμα]. Meanwhile the souls of those beheaded and afflicted for the testimony of Jesus and for the word of God cry out beneath the altar of God: "How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood?" These are the ardent and many prayers of the Church triumphant.

units.la: STRUM DE iis, QUI HABITANT IN TERRA. Et qui talia testatus est, dixit: ETIAM, VENIO CITO. AMEN. suspirantibus omnibus, qui adventum ejus diligunt: ETIAM VENI, DOMINE JESU. Tibi Patri, Filio & Spiritui S. ob abyssos judiciorum & gratiarum divitiarumque Tuarum, sit Magnificentia & Robur, Gloria, & Victoria, & Honor in Secula Seculorum!
units.tr: ... CONCERNING THOSE WHO DWELL ON THE EARTH. And he who testified these things said: "Surely I come quickly. Amen." All who love his coming sighing: "Even so, come, Lord Jesus." To you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, for the depths of your judgments and the riches of your graces, be magnificence and strength, glory, victory and honour, for ever and ever!

units.la: INvadendis occupandisque Imperiis, juris sæpe color initio quæri solet: stabilita verò fundataque semel tyrannide, vetera illa initia quantum potest obruuntur, sex tantum Regia nudè, & veluti ὀὐηγμοῖς obtenditur, in contemptores legibus Majestatis perduellionumque vindicatur. Itaque simpliciter magis & ingenuè, quàm cautè Paulus III. cum de summa ipsius potestate aliquando inter familiares mentio incideret, ridere illos solitus erat, ut scholasticos & rerum rudes, qui à Christo eam tam anxiè repeterent, cujus se possessionem vel solam, optimum & firmissimum titulum habere dicebat, quam viribus opibusque summis, civitatibus munitissimis, & potentissimorum Principum sibi conjurantium auxilio tueri ac defendere posset. Prudentius etiam Italorum pars maxima, quæ Pontificem Romanum, non uti Deum aliquem, aut Dei vicarium ob fulmina illa, quibus jam pene totus inermis est; sed ut Principem viris, armis, urbibus castellis, fœderibusque potentissimum reveretur & observat. Nos verò, quos ille ut puerulos sola vanæ religionis larva perterret, quibusque ut venalitiis mancipiis pro arbitrio abutitur, scire aliquando par est, quo jure, quare injuria tam duro inclementique Domino serviamus: non ut tanquam spartaci bellum aliquod servile moveamus, sed ut ingenuinati, & quorum majores servitutem illam non servierunt, vindicibus tamen idoneis vel tertia assertione semel amissam libertatem & strenuè recuperemus, & fortiter retineamus conservemusque. Natales porrò nostros, vel ab ejusdem Domini familia, aliqua saltem ex parte repetere licet, ex qua est hoc quidem mancipium, sed frugi admodum & manumissione dignissimum: cujus etiam hac in re fidem herus infidelissimus per alligatos obruere conatus est. Nos tabulas quasi ex naufragio, aut potius ex rogo vispellionum manibus extortas omnibus reddimus. Quarum fidem & vindicum satis perspecta integritas, & auctoris stylus, & loci ipsius, unde dolo malo detractæ sunt, vel sola inspectio sic afferunt, ut de ea nemo bonus juste dubitare possit. Reliquum est, ut hoc beneficio prudenter & serio utamur fruamurque, ne si nos ob pretium participandum iterum quodammodo venire patiamur, non eadem posthac spes libertatis, affulgeat, & perpetua servitute dignissima etiam gravioribus flagris mancipia premamur.
units.tr: When men set out to invade and seize empires, they usually look first for some colour of right. But once tyranny is established and secure, its old beginnings are buried as far as possible. Royal authority is then displayed bare, as it were as a pretext [ὀὐηγμοῖς], and those who despise it are punished under the laws of majesty and treason. So Paul III, when his supreme power was once mentioned among his intimates, used to laugh at those who, as scholastic men ignorant of affairs, sought so anxiously to derive it from Christ. He said that his possession of it was in itself the best and firmest title, and that he could guard and defend it with his greatest forces and wealth, his strongest cities, and the aid of the most powerful princes allied with him. He spoke simply and frankly rather than cautiously. Moreover, the greater part of the Italians are wiser. They do not revere the Roman Pontiff as some god or vicar of God because of those thunderbolts, by which he is now almost wholly unarmed. They revere and observe him as a prince most powerful in men, arms, cities, castles and alliances. But we, whom he frightens like little children with the mere mask of empty religion, and whom he abuses at will like bought slaves, ought to know at some point by what right and for what reason we serve so harsh and merciless a master, and by what injustice. We should do this not so that we may stir up some servile war like Spartacus, but so that we, who are freeborn and whose ancestors did not serve that servitude, may with suitable avengers however, by a third assertion, vigorously recover the liberty once lost, and firmly hold, keep and preserve it. Moreover, we may trace our origins, at least in part, back to the household of that same Lord. From it indeed this slave comes, though a very thrifty one and most worthy of manumission. His most faithless master has tried to crush his loyalty in this matter too, by chains. We give back to all the records, as it were wrested from a shipwreck, or rather from the pyre, out of the hands of scoundrels. Their genuineness, the sufficiently proven integrity of the avengers, the author's style, and the very place from which they were removed by malice, by the mere inspection of them alone, attest them so clearly that no good man can justly doubt them. It remains that we use and enjoy this benefit prudently and seriously. If we allow ourselves, for the sake of sharing the price, to be sold again in some way, the same hope of liberty will no longer shine upon us, and we, most deserving of perpetual servitude, will be oppressed with heavier whips.
