units.tr: XCVI. XCVII.

units.la: 1155. Hadriano IV. P. equum conscendenti Fridericus I. Imp. stape-
units.tr: 1155. Hadrian IV, as he was mounting a horse, orders Frederick I, Emperor, to hold the stirrup.

units.la: dem tenere jubetur; qui opus servile renuens, ab osculo Papae arce-
units.tr: He refuses the servile task and is kept from the Pope's kiss until he does what was commanded.

units.la: tur, donec imperata faceret. Inde Romae 18. Jun. coronatur. §.
units.tr: Then at Rome on 18 June he is crowned. §.

units.la: XCIV.
units.tr: XCIV.

units.la: 1157. Hadrianum inter & Fridericum Imp. contentio oritur de Imperio
units.tr: 1157. A dispute arises between Hadrian and Emperor Frederick over whether the Roman Empire is a fief of the Pope.

units.la: R. an Papae feudum sit. Ita pertenderat Papa, Lotharii Imp. histo-
units.tr: The Pope maintained that it was, citing a picture of Lothar the Emperor painted in the Lateran palace.

units.la: riam in palatio Lateranensi pictam prætexens. Picturam deleri Imp.
units.tr: When the Emperor asked that the picture be removed,

units.la: cum petisset, neque delevit eam Papa, & scripsit insuper, Papam ei
units.tr: the Pope did not remove it, and he further wrote that the Pope had conferred on him the insignia of the imperial crown.

units.la: insigne Imperialis coronae contulisse. Contumelia irritatus Imperator
units.tr: Angered by the insult, the Emperor marches into Italy with an army.

units.la: cum exercitu in Italiam tendit. Papa metuens sibi pacem exorat; at
units.tr: The Pope, fearing for himself, begs for peace; but soon, urged on by the Cardinals, he excommunicates the Emperor, who was demanding his rights in Italy more firmly, above all at Rome. ibid.

units.la: mox, hortantibus Cardinalibus, eundem constantius jus suum in Ita-
units.tr: Under the same Pope Hadrian, the name of the Waldenses became famous.

units.la: lia, Romae imprimis requirentem, excommunicat. ibid.
units.tr: Already they had separate assemblies at Lyons, Toulouse and in Narbonese Gaul, having suffered persecutions from the Popes. §. XCIX. C.

units.la: Clarescit, eodem Pontifice Hadriano Waldensium nomen. Lug-
units.tr: 1159. Alexander III, having overcome the Antipopes, seizes the Papacy. §. XCIV.

units.la: duni, Tholosae & in Gallia Narbonensi segreges jam coetus habue-
units.tr: duni, at Toulouse and in Narbonese Gaul, already had separate assemblies, suffering persecution from the Popes.

units.la: rant, Pontificum persecutiones passi. §. XCIX. C.
units.tr: ...had suffered persecution at the hands of the Pontiffs. §. XCIX. C.

units.la: 1159. Alexander III. superatis Antipapis Papatum rapit. §. XCIV. Idem Henricum Regem Angliae, quòd necis Thomae Bequeti Cantuariensis conscius esset, virgis caedi jubet. ibid.
units.tr: 1159. Alexander III, having overcome the antipopes, seizes the papacy. §. XCIV. The same man orders Henry, King of England, to be beaten with rods, because he had been privy to the murder of Thomas Becket of Canterbury. ibid.

units.la: Cum Friderico Barbarossa Venetiis pacem pangit. Ubi Imperatoris prostrati collo calcato his verbis Papa insultat: Supra aspidem & basiliscum ambulabis, &c. ibid.
units.tr: Clement III excommunicates the Danish priests who retained their wives, and terrifies Philip, King of France, with anathema. ibid.

units.la: Waldenses ab Alexandro ad Concilium Lateranense citati, eorum declinant. Unde bello, caedibus, lanienis per bullas cruciatas expositi, per Europam dispersi, in Bohemia cumprimis sedem figunt. ibid.
units.tr: Celestine III crowns Henry VI as Emperor. As soon as the Emperor, adoring the Pope, bowed down, the Pope raised his foot and knocked the crown from his head, signifying that it is in his power to give and to take away empire. ibid.

units.la: Clemens III. P. Danos Sacerdotes conjugatos retinentes excommunicat: Philippum Galliae Regem anathemate terret. ibid.
units.tr: Clement III, Pope, excommunicates the Danish priests who keep their wives, and terrifies Philip, King of France, with anathema. ibid.

units.la: Coelestinus III. P. Henricum VI. Imp. coronat. Eique mox Papam adoranti, pede elevato coronam capite decutit, significans, in sua potestate esse, dare & auferre imperium. ibid.
units.tr: Pope Celestine III crowned Emperor Henry VI, and when the Emperor afterwards came to adore the Pope, the Pope raised his foot and knocked the crown from his head, signifying that it was in his power to give and to take away the empire. ibid.

units.la: SECULUM DECIMUM TERTIUM.
units.tr: THE THIRTEENTH CENTURY.

units.la: §. CI. —— CXVI.
SEculi hujus faciem miseram praesagit Joachimus Abbas. Et de Ecclesiae R. perversitate graviter Scriptores coaevi quiritantur. §. CI.
units.tr: Joachim the Abbot foretells the wretched face of this century, and contemporary writers bitterly complain of the perversity of the Roman Church. §. CI.

units.la: Innocentius III. Philippo Imp. adversus Othonem certanti de Imperio, postquam diu vehementer restitit, cumque excommunicavit; tandem utrumque reconciliat. §. CII.
units.tr: Innocent III fought with Philip the Emperor against Otto over the Empire. After resisting for a long time, he excommunicated Philip too, but at last he reconciled both. §. CII.

units.la: Waldenses, quibus praecipui Galliae Proceres jam adhaeserant, mirè se diffundunt. Cum iis Innocentius Carmanii colloquium instituit. Cùm non satisfieret Proceribus, manentes in sententia horrendam tempestatem, classicum canentibus Monachis, Dominico inprimis, subeunt. Dispersi denuo passim nidulantur. §. CV.
units.tr: The Waldenses, to whom the principal nobles of France had already attached themselves, spread widely. Innocent held a colloquy with them at Carmanium. When the nobles were not satisfied and the Waldenses held to their opinion, they underwent a dreadful storm, with the monks, the Dominicans above all, sounding the trumpet. Scattered again, they nested here and there. §. CV.

units.la: Idem Angliae Regem Johannem, & Regnum, quòd Langtonum Cantuariensi Archiepiscopatui obtrudi non paterentur, interdicto subjicit; & cruciatam adversus illud militiam concitat. ibid.
units.tr: The same Innocent placed King John and the kingdom of England under an interdict, because they would not allow Langton to be forced on the archbishopric of Canterbury, and he stirred up a crusade against them. ibid.

units.la: Rex Angliae Johannes à Pontifice ad angustias redactus, Regnum suum feudum Pontificis & vectigale facit, promissa solutione denarii Petri, & quotannis mille marcarum Sterlinorum. ibid.
units.tr: King John of England, reduced to straits by the Pope, made his kingdom a fief and tributary of the Pope, with the promised payment of Peter's penny and a thousand marks sterling a year. ibid.

units.la: Innocentius Romae in Laterano Concilium celebrat, & transsubstantiationem ante à Lanfranco introductam, nec non auricularem confessionem quotannis semel edendam definit; Ordinésque Monachorum Mendicantium, Dominicanorum inprimis & Franciscanorum, rum, qui Ecclesiam Romanam adversus Waldenses fortiter defendere coeperant, confirmat. §. CIII.
units.tr: Innocent celebrated a council at Rome in the Lateran. He defined transubstantiation, first introduced by Lanfranc, and also that auricular confession should be made once a year. He confirmed the orders of the mendicant monks, the Dominicans and Franciscans especially, who had begun to defend the Roman Church vigorously against the Waldenses. §. CIII.

units.la: 1222. Fridericus II. Imp. in Italia multipliciter a Papa Honorio III. injuriis afficitur. In Germaniam concedens, Principibus Germanis injurias illas, & evertendi Imperii R. conatus queritur. §. CV.
units.tr: 1222. Frederick II, Emperor, was treated with many injuries in Italy by Pope Honorius III. Going into Germany, he complained to the German princes of those injuries and of the attempts to overthrow the Roman Empire. §. CV.

units.la: 1223. Fridericus Romam tendit, ubi Johannes Brennensis, Rex Hierosolymitanus, eum Papae reconciliat, ea conditione, ut Fridericus ducta uxore sua haeres Regni Hierosolymitani infidelibus eripiendi, declaretur. ibid.
units.tr: 1223. Frederick went to Rome, where John of Brienne, King of Jerusalem, reconciled him with the Pope, on condition that Frederick, once he had married John's daughter, should be declared heir to the kingdom of Jerusalem, to be wrested from the infidels. ibid.

units.la: 1227. Friderico expeditionem in Palaestinam tardius suscipienti, Gregorius IX. amoto Imperatore Siciliae inhians, indignatus, eundem excommunicat, totamque Italiam Guelforum Papae, & Gibellinorum, Imperatori adhaerentium factionibus miscet. ibid.
units.tr: 1227. Gregory IX was angry that Frederick undertook the expedition to Palestine too slowly. Longing to remove the Emperor from Sicily, he excommunicated him and threw all Italy into confusion with the factions of the Guelfs, who adhered to the Pope, and the Ghibellines, who adhered to the Emperor. ibid.

units.la: 1228. Fridericus, excommunicatus licet, in Palaestinam tendit. Adversus eum Papa Johannem Socerum, Hospitalarios, ipsumque Sultanum accendit. Sultanus Papae insidias Friderico, Hierosolyma capta, detegit. unde induciis cum eo pactis Italiam Fridericus repetit, & utcunque Pontifici conciliatur. ibid.
units.tr: 1228. Frederick, although excommunicated, went to Palestine. The Pope stirred up against him his father-in-law John, the Hospitallers, and the Sultan himself. The Sultan, after Jerusalem had been taken, revealed the Pope's plots against Frederick. Therefore Frederick made a truce with the Sultan, returned to Italy, and somehow was reconciled to the Pontiff. ibid.

units.la: 1239. Fridericus Saracenis Sardiniam eripit. Eam occupatam Papa pro sua repetit, & abnuentem Fridericum excommunicat. Fridericus cum exercitu Romam tendit, cui cruciatam militiam opposuit quam Imp. vicit & orco mactavit. ibid.
units.tr: 1239. Frederick wrested Sardinia from the Saracens. When it was occupied, the Pope claimed it for himself and excommunicated Frederick, who refused to give it up. Frederick marched with an army to Rome. Against him the Pope set a crusade, which the Emperor defeated and sent down to the underworld. ibid.

units.la: 1240. Gregorius P. a Friderico in angustias redactus, cum eo inducias ad Concilium generale usque pangit. sed mox induciae rumpuntur, Papa pecunias undique corrogante, &c., bullis per Albertum Boham huc illuc missis, adversus Imp. conspirante. ibid.
units.tr: 1240. Pope Gregory, reduced to straits by Frederick, made a truce with him until a General Council. But soon the truces were broken, the Pope collecting money on all sides, and bulls were sent here and there through Albert of Bohemia, who conspired against the Emperor. ibid.

units.la: 1241. Concilium Romae a Gregerio in causa Friderici indicitur. Episcopi eo non terrestri, uti Imp. petierat, sed maritimo itinere, classe viginti sex navium instructi, properant, & a Friderici filio Conrado victi, pars submersi, pars capti detentique sunt ibid. Denuo excommunicatus Fridericus, ab Eberhardo Salisburgensi Archiepiscopo Ratisbonae in Comitiis, oratione adversus Papam habita pathetica, absolvitur. §. CVIII.
units.tr: 1241. Gregory called a council at Rome in the cause of Frederick. The bishops hastened there, not by the land route, as the Emperor had asked, but by sea, equipped with a fleet of twenty-six ships. Defeated by Frederick's son Conrad, some were sunk and some captured and detained. ibid. Frederick was excommunicated again, but was absolved by Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg, at Regensburg in the Diet, after a moving speech against the Pope. §. CVIII.

units.la: 1243. Innocentius IV. Gregorii successor Friderici excommunicationem confirmat; & in Gallia Angliaque turbas gravissimas excitat. §. CV.
units.tr: 1243. Innocent IV, successor of Gregory, confirmed the excommunication of Frederick, and in Gaul and England he stirred up the gravest disturbances. §. CV.

units.la: 1245. Idem Concilio Lugduni indicto Caesarem Imperio abdicat, eique Henricum Thuringiae Landgravium surrogat. Imperator Italiam petit, Papamque magnas in angustias redigit. ibid. Henricus Imp. Pontificius, post vulnus Ulmæ acceptum, Ifenaci moritur cui Pontificii Wilhelmum Comitem Hollandiæ sufficiunt. ibid.
units.tr: 1245. Innocent, having called a council at Lyons, deposed the Emperor from the Empire and substituted Henry, Landgrave of Thuringia, in his place. The Emperor went to Italy and reduced the Pope to great straits. ibid. Henry, the Pope's Emperor, died at Eisenach after a wound received at Ulm, and the Papists put up William, Count of Holland, in his place. ibid.

units.la: Innocentius Petrum de Vinea, fidelem hactenus Fridérico, pretio conducit, ut Imperatorem veneno tollat. Patratus facinus proditurde Vinea, & captus, oculisque privatus in carcere moritur. ibid.
units.tr: Innocent hired Peter de Vinea, hitherto faithful to Frederick, for a price, to kill the Emperor with poison. The deed was planned, but de Vinea betrayed it. He was captured, blinded, and died in prison. ibid.

units.la: Fridericus in arce Florentina Apuliæ morbo correptus moritur. ibid. Princeps longè præstantissimus, neque aliam ob causam Pontificibus adeò exosus, quàm quòd rara virtute præditus, præter morem Impp. in Italia habitans, observâsse Pontificum perversa studia & molimina visus esset. §. CVI.
units.tr: Frederick, seized by illness, died in the fortress of Florence in Apulia. ibid. He was by far the most outstanding prince, and the Popes hated him for no other reason than that, endowed with rare virtue and living in Italy contrary to the custom of emperors, he seemed to have seen through the perverse pursuits and schemes of the Popes. §. CVI.

units.la: Alexander IV. P. Guilhelmi de S. Amore tractatum, cui titulus erat: de periculis novissimorum temporum; quo Monachorum Ordines perstringuntur, & à Franciscanis excogitatum Evangelium æternum, quo Evangelium Christi abrogatur, & novum Spiritus S. revelatur; describitur; comburit. §. CIX. CX. CXI. Æternum porro Evangelium isthoc, blasphemiis horrendis refertum, nudum Papatum sequentium temporum repræsentabat. §. CXII.
units.tr: Pope Alexander IV condemned the treatise of William of St. Amour entitled On the Perils of the Last Times, in which the orders of monks are assailed. He also burned the Eternal Gospel devised by the Franciscans, by which the Gospel of Christ is abrogated and a new revelation of the Holy Spirit is proclaimed. §. CIX. CX. CXI. This Eternal Gospel, filled with horrible blasphemies, represented the naked Papacy of the following times. §. CXII.

units.la: Idem Papa cum Manfredo, Friderici notho, Apuliæ & Siciliæ Rege, bellum gerit, eíque Edmundum, Regis Angliæ filium substituit. §. CXIII.
units.tr: The same Pope waged war with Manfred, Frederick's bastard son and King of Apulia and Sicily, and put Edmund, son of the King of England, in his place. §. CXIII.

units.la: Eidem in Gallia Simoniam exercenti, Ludovicus Rex Sanctionem Pragmaticam, vetantem, ne Rege inscio pecuniæ ex Regno Romam deportentur, opponit. ibid.
units.tr: Louis, the King, opposed the same Pope, who was practising simony in Gaul, with the Pragmatic Sanction, which forbade money to be carried from the kingdom to Rome without the King's knowledge. ibid.

units.la: Flagellantium sectam recens exortam Alexander confirmat. ibid.
units.tr: Alexander confirmed the recently arisen sect of the Flagellants. ibid.

units.la: Urbanus IV. Thomæ Aquinatis instinctu festum corporis Christi instituit. ibid.
units.tr: Urban IV, at the instigation of Thomas Aquinas, instituted the feast of Corpus Christi. ibid.

units.la: Idem Carolum Andegavensem Regem Siciliæ creat, dummodo Manfredum Regno pellat. ibid.
units.tr: The same Urban made Charles of Anjou King of Sicily, provided he drove Manfred out of the kingdom. ibid.

units.la: Carolus Andegav. Manfredum prope Beneventum prælio superat, & interficit. Conradinus Friderici II. ex Conrado nepos Regni Siciliæ hæreditatem adituros à Clemente IV. P. cum injuria repellitur. ibid.
units.tr: Charles of Anjou defeated Manfred in battle near Benevento and killed him. Conradin, grandson of Frederick II through Conrad, who was about to take up the inheritance of the kingdom of Sicily, was unjustly repelled by Clement IV. ibid.

units.la: Conradinus à Carolo ad lacum Fuscinum prælio victus, una cum Friderico Austriæ Duce, Clementis P. consilio, sævè decollatur, eadémque opera Friderici Barb. progenies, totáque stirps Suevica extinguitur, & vacua Regna pro arbitrio Papæ dispensantur. ibid.
units.tr: Conradin was defeated by Charles in battle at Lake Fucino. Together with Frederick, Duke of Austria, he was cruelly beheaded on the counsel of Pope Clement. By the same work the line of Frederick Barbarossa and the whole Swabian stock was extinguished, and the vacant kingdoms were distributed at the Pope's pleasure. ibid.

units.la: Rodolphus I. Imp. Francofurti electus, & à Gregorio X. Romam ad coronationem invitatus, eò venire, terrentibus vestigiis, renuit, nuit, & Papæ, ut electionem ratam haberet, Romandiolam donavit. ibid.
units.tr: Rudolf I, elected Emperor at Frankfurt and invited by Gregory X to Rome for his coronation, refused to go there, his steps faltering with fear. In order to have the Pope ratify his election, he gave him Romagna. ibid.

units.la: Gregorius idem Concilio Lugduni celebrato, leges in electione Papæ à Cardinalibus observandas sancit. ibid.
units.tr: The same Gregory, at the Council of Lyons, enacted laws to be observed by the cardinals in the election of a Pope. ibid.

units.la: Aderant in eodem Concilio Michaelis Palæologi Imp. Const. Legati, obedientiam promittentes Papæ, si adversario suo Carolo Andeg. resisteret. Certis conditionibus Papa pacisci tur. Sed mox negotiatio evanuit. ibid.
units.tr: At the same Council were present the legates of Michael Palaeologus, Emperor at Constantinople, promising obedience to the Pope if he would resist his adversary Charles of Anjou. The Pope struck a bargain on certain conditions, but soon the negotiation fell through. ibid.

units.la: Siculi cum Petro Aragoniæ Rege, à Nicolao III. adversus Carolum concitato, conspirantes, d. 30. Martii vespere, campanæ pulsu, Gallos in Sicilia omnes duarum horarum spatio crudeliter occidunt, Conradini nefarie cæsi sanguinem ulciscente Deo. ibid.
units.tr: The Sicilians, conspiring with Peter, King of Aragon, who had been stirred up against Charles by Nicholas III, on the evening of 30 March, at the sound of a bell, cruelly killed all the Frenchmen in Sicily within the space of two hours, God avenging the blood of Conradin, which had been wickedly shed. ibid.

units.la: Martinus IV. P. Petrum Aragoniæ Regem excommunicat, & Regnum Carolo Valesio donat. ibid.
units.tr: Martin IV excommunicated Peter, King of Aragon, and gave the kingdom to Charles of Valois. ibid.

units.la: Nicolaus IV. P. Mainardum Tiroli Comitem, quòd Tridentino Episcopo restituisset, excommunicat, qui gravi sermone Antichristos effœminatos pulsat. § CXIV.
units.tr: Nicholas IV excommunicated Meinhard, Count of Tyrol, because he had restored the territory to the Bishop of Trent. In a grave sermon he assailed the effeminate Antichrists. §. CXIV.

units.la: Cœlestino V. P. Papatum ob simplicitatem resignanti, Bonifacius VIII. succedens, Gibelinis, seu fidis Imperii civibus gravem se gerere incipit. §. CXV.
units.tr: Boniface VIII, succeeding Celestine V, who resigned the Papacy out of simplicity, began to behave harshly toward the Ghibellines, that is, the citizens loyal to the Empire. §. CXV.

units.la: Bonifacius coronatus & accinctus prodiens in publicum, proclamat: Ego sum Cæsar & Papa. Alberti electionem ægrè tandem approbat. §. CXIX.
units.tr: Boniface, appearing in public crowned and girded with the sword, proclaimed: I am Caesar and Pope. He approved Albert's election only with difficulty, in the end. §. CXIX.

units.la: SECULUM DECIMUM QUARTUM. §. CXVI. — CXXXIX.
units.tr: Fourteenth Century. §. CXVI. — CXXXIX.

units.la: BONIFACIUS VIII. annum Jubilæum hoc anno agendum decernit, in quo plenissimam omnium peccatorum remissionem Romam venientibus, promittit. Primo die in Pontificalibus populo apparens, Apostolicam illi Benedictionem precatus est. Altero Imperiali habitu, gladio nudo prælato, sedens promulgavit: Ecce duo gladii. Inauguratio hæc fuit Cæsareo Papatus, seu potestatis utriusque supremæ, quem Papa jam adeptus & bulla etiam, Unam Sanctam &c. testificatus fuerat. §. CXVI. CXVII. Deinceps Clemens VI. jubilæum ad annum quinquagesimum, Bonifacius IX. ad trigesimum tertium, Sixtus IV. ad vicesimum quintum reduxit. §. CXVIII.
units.tr: Boniface VIII decreed that a jubilee should be celebrated that year, and promised the fullest remission of all sins to those who came to Rome. On the first day he appeared before the people in pontifical vestments and prayed for them the apostolic blessing. On the second, dressed in imperial robes, with a bare sword carried before him, he sat and proclaimed: Behold, two swords. This inauguration was the Caesarean papacy, or supreme power over both swords, which the Pope had already gained and had also attested in the bull Unam Sanctam etc. CXVI. CXVII. Afterwards Clement VI reduced the jubilee to fifty years, Boniface IX to thirty-three, and Sixtus IV to twenty-five. CXVIII.

units.la: Eodem die, quo Jubilæum isthoc Bonifacius celebravit, etiam TurTurcicum Imperium Ottomannus auspicatus est. §. CXVI.
units.tr: On the same day on which Boniface celebrated this jubilee, the Ottoman also began the Turkish empire. CXVI.

units.la: Bonifacius Philippum Pulchrum in Palæstinam proficisci sub anathemate jubet. Legatus ejus Episcopus Apamceensis duriora verba prolocutus à Rege in carcerem compingitur. Papa Legatum liberari præcipit. Cunctante Rege, Papa bulla declarat, Regnum Franciæ Papæ feudum esse. Bullam cùm Rex comburi jussisset, & Episcopos investivisset, vicissim Regem Papa excommunicavit. Tandem Bonifacius à Rege captus, in carcere moritur. §. CXX.
units.tr: Boniface ordered Philip the Fair to set out for Palestine under anathema. His legate, the bishop of Pamiers, spoke rather harsh words and was thrown into prison by the king. The Pope ordered the legate freed. When the king hesitated, the Pope declared by bull that the kingdom of France was a fief of the Papacy. When the king had ordered the bull burned and had invested bishops, the Pope in turn excommunicated the king. Finally Boniface was seized by the king and died in prison. CXX.

units.la: Robertus Gallus Papam idolum, serpentem, Antichristum vocat. §. CXXI. Idem facientes Fratricelli persecutionem patiuntur. §. CXXII.
units.tr: Robert the Gaul called the Pope an idol, a serpent, and Antichrist. CXXI. The Fraticelli, doing the same, suffered persecution. CXXII.

units.la: Clemens V. P. lectus sedem Avenione in Gallia figit; ubi septuaginta duos posthac annos integros, Roma relicta, & per Cardinales tres cum Senatoria potestate gubernata; Pontifices commorantur. §. CXXIII.
units.tr: Clement V, elected Pope, fixed his seat at Avignon in Gaul. From then on the popes remained there for seventy-two full years, with Rome abandoned and governed by three cardinals with senatorial power. CXXIII.

units.la: Idem Papa Durando Mimatensi præcipit, ut de reformanda ecclesia consilium scriberet. Scriptum graviter licet, in nervum non erupit. ibid.
units.tr: The same Pope ordered Durand of Mende to write a plan for reforming the Church. The writing, though weighty, did not strike at the heart of the matter. ibid.

units.la: Henricus VII. Imp. à Bernhardo Politiano Monacho hostia intoxicata necatur. §. CXXV.
units.tr: Henry VII, emperor, was killed by a poisoned host given to him by Bernhard Politian, a monk. CXXV.

units.la: Concilio Viennæ celebrato, Clemens idem edita Decretali, cujus initium, Pastoralis, se supra Imperatores longè extollit; Minorum religionem confirmat, & Templariorum ordinem abrogat. §. CXXIV.
units.tr: At the council held at Vienne, Clement, having issued a decretal whose opening words are Pastoralis, raised himself far above the emperors. He confirmed the religion of the Minorites and abolished the order of the Templars. CXXIV.

units.la: Johannes XXIII. se ipsum Pontificem eligit; negans, animas defunctorum fidelium ante finem mundi beata visione Dei frui. Extravagantes idem edidit, in quibus Papam Soli, Imperatorem lunæ confert. §. CXXVII.
units.tr: John XXIII elected himself pope, denying that the souls of the faithful departed enjoy the blessed vision of God before the end of the world. He also published the Extravagantes, in which he likens the Pope to the sun and the emperor to the moon. CXXVII.

units.la: Dantes Aligerius edito libro, cui titulus Monarchia potestatem Papæ oppugnat. §. CXXVI.
units.tr: Dante Alighieri, having published a book entitled Monarchia, attacked the power of the Pope. CXXVI.

units.la: Idem bulla bestiali Ludovico Bavaro Imperio interdicit; §. CXXX. cui ex Ratisbonensibus Comitiis masculè Ludovicus respondet; Antichristi nomine eum insigniens. §. CXXXI.
units.tr: The same Pope, by a brutal bull, placed Louis of Bavaria under interdict from the empire. CXXX. To this Louis replied boldly from the Diet of Regensburg, branding him with the name of Antichrist. CXXXI.

units.la: Johannes P. hæreseos damnat eos, qui Christum pauperem fuisse, & nihil ipsum & Apostolos proprii habuisse asserrent. §. CXXIX.
units.tr: John XXII condemned as heresy those who asserted that Christ was poor and that he and the apostles had nothing of their own. CXXIX.

units.la: Grave dissidium inter Ludovicum Bavarum Imp. & Johannem XXIII. P. oritur. Papa Ludovicum, qui renitente eo imperaverat, Imperii invasorem: Ludovicus Papam hæresiarcham vocaverat. Ludovicus Ratisbonæ re cum Imperii Principibus communicata, libertatem Imperii asserere statuit. §. CXXVIII.
units.tr: A grave dispute arose between Louis of Bavaria, emperor, and John XXII. The Pope had called Louis, who had ruled against his will, an invader of the empire, and Louis had called the Pope a heresiarch. Louis, having consulted with the princes of the empire at Regensburg, resolved to assert the liberty of the empire. CXXVIII.

units.la: Ludovicus à Romanis accersitus in Italiam iter instituit, Papa reclamante, & Ludovicum excommunicante, quin & exercitum adversus eum instruente. ibid.
units.tr: Louis, summoned by the Romans, set out on his journey into Italy, while the Pope protested, excommunicated him, and even raised an army against him. ibid.

units.la: Ludovicum eruditis scriptis strenuè Wilhelmus Occam, Marsilius Patavinus, Michael Cœsenas, aliique tutantur. ibid. & §. CXXXIII.
units.tr: Louis was vigorously defended by learned writings of William of Occam, Marsilius of Padua, Michael of Cesena, and others. ibid. & CXXXIII.

units.la: Ludovicus Romam intrat, coroatur per Castellanum cum conjuge, & Episcoporum quorundam consensu novum Pontificem elegit, Petrum de Corbonaria ex familia Columnensium; Nicolai V. nomen assumentem. §. CXXVIII.
units.tr: Louis entered Rome and was crowned by the Castellan, together with his wife. With the consent of some bishops he elected a new pontiff, Peter of Corvara, from the family of the Colonna, who took the name Nicholas V. CXXVIII.

units.la: Papa Avinione iterum Ludovicum excommunicat, hæreticum & schismaticum proclamat. ibid.
units.tr: The Pope at Avignon again excommunicated Louis and proclaimed him a heretic and schismatic. ibid.

units.la: Johanni Benedictus XII. succedit, & simultates cum Ludovico hostiliter continuat. §. CXXXII.
units.tr: Benedict XII succeeded John and continued his hostile quarrels with Louis. CXXXII.

units.la: Ludovicus à Benedicto diris ut exsolveretur, frustra expetens, ad generale Concilium provocat. ibid.
units.tr: Louis, having vainly sought from Benedict to be freed from the dreadful curses, appealed to a general council. ibid.

units.la: Comitiis Francofurti habitis, Principes Imperii decernunt, solennitates Papæ in coronando Imperatore esse adventitias, nomina sine re, & à quolibet Episcopo administrari posse; nec vacante Imperio jus ejus ad Papam, sed ad Palatinum & Saxonem revolvi; denique Concilium generale Papæ judicio anteferendum esse. ibid.
units.tr: At the diet held at Frankfurt, the princes of the empire decreed that the solemnities of the Pope in crowning an emperor were incidental, names without substance, and could be administered by any bishop. They also decreed that, while the empire was vacant, the right to it did not revert to the Pope but to the Count Palatine and the Duke of Saxony. Finally, they decreed that a general council was to be preferred to the judgment of the Pope. ibid.

units.la: Clemens VI. P. Benedicti successor Ludovicum excommunicatione solvit, conditionibus durissimis quas, suadentibus Principibus, & Theologis Parisiensibus, ceu iniquas Imp. repudiat. ibid.
units.tr: Clement VI, Benedict's successor, released Louis from excommunication on very harsh conditions, which Louis, at the urging of the princes and the Parisian theologians, rejected as unjust. ibid.

units.la: Clemens idem Ludovicum in die Cœnæ Domini dirissimè execratur, Principibúsque Imperii, ut alium eligant, præcipit. Principes nonnulli Rhenfii Carolum IV. Johannis Regis Bohemiæ filium, Regem Romanorum eligunt. Reliqui Principes mox Spiræ electionem rescindunt. ibid.
units.tr: The same Clement, on Maundy Thursday, most dreadfully cursed Louis and ordered the princes of the empire to elect another. Some Rhenish princes elected Charles IV, son of John, King of Bohemia, as King of the Romans. The remaining princes soon annulled the election at Speyer. ibid.

units.la: Ludovicus veneno potatus, cum vomitu, & mox venatione illud ejicere tentaslet, ursum ingentem impetendo, ex equo præceps ruit, & mox moritur. ibid.
units.tr: Louis, having been given poison, vomited it up, and soon afterwards, trying to expel it by hunting, attacked a huge bear, fell headlong from his horse, and died shortly after. ibid.

units.la: Ludovico post varios discordibus consiliis electos succedens tandem Carolus IV. primo vere Romam proficiscitur, ibidémque à Legato Innocentii VI. P. Cardinale Hostiensi, coronatur, non sine dedecore, pedes urbem ingressus, promitténsque, nunquam Italiam se repetiturum; adéoque Majestatem Imperii R. turpiter prodens. §. CXXXIV. Vixerat ea ætate Franciscus Petrarcha, Seculi sui lumen, qui ignominiosa Caroli coronatione motus, graviter cum increpuit, & Romanam etiam Curiam graphicè depinxit. §. CXXXV.
units.tr: Louis was succeeded, after various discordant counsels had chosen several candidates, by Charles IV, who at last set out for Rome in the spring. There he was crowned by the legate of Innocent VI, the Cardinal of Ostia, not without disgrace: he entered the city on foot, promising never to return to Italy, and so shamefully betrayed the majesty of the Roman Empire. CXXXIV. In that age lived Francis Petrarch, the light of his century, who, moved by the shameful coronation of Charles, rebuked him sharply and also depicted the Roman Curia vividly. §. CXXXV.

units.la: Innocentio VI. Pontifice claret Johannes Wiclefus, Oxoniensis, qui Papæ ceu Antichristi, tum hierarchiam, tum doctrinam, voce calamóque, fortissimè oppugnavit, asseclas multos magnósque primùm in Anglia, mox etiam exul in Bohemia nactus. § CXXXVII.
units.tr: Under Innocent VI there flourished John Wycliffe of Oxford, who with voice and pen most vigorously attacked the Pope as Antichrist, both his hierarchy and his doctrine. He won many great followers, first in England and then, in exile, in Bohemia. § CXXXVII.

units.la: Gregorius XI. P. Catharinæ Senensis & Brigittæ somniis potissimùm inductus, Avenione relicta Romam intrat, cùm sedes Pontificia annis ferè septuaginta duobus in Galliis fuisset. §. CXXXVIII.
units.tr: Gregory XI, moved chiefly by the dreams of Catherine of Siena and Bridget, left Avignon and entered Rome, the papal seat having been in Gaul for nearly seventy-two years. §. CXXXVIII.

units.la: Catharina Senensis & Brigitta revelationibus suis prolatis, graviter in Romanam curiam invehuntur, & Ecclesiæ reformationem urgent. §. CXXXVI.
units.tr: Catherine of Siena and Bridget, having published their revelations, inveighed severely against the Roman curia and urged the reformation of the Church. §. CXXXVI.

units.la: Gregorio XI. succedit Urbanus VI. Cardinales Galli invitos se ejus electioni consensisse questi, Fundos abeunt, ibíque Papam Gallum, Robertum Gebennensem, seu Clementem VII. eligunt, qui Avenione annis sedecim sedit. Ortum hinc est schisma gravissimum omnium, Pontifices Avenionenses & Romanos inter, quod quadraginta annis durans, in Concilio demum Constantiensi extinctum est. §. CXXXVIII.
units.tr: Gregory XI was succeeded by Urban VI. The French cardinals, complaining that they had consented to his election against their will, went off to Fondi, and there elected the Frenchman Robert of Geneva, or Clement VII, as pope; he sat at Avignon for sixteen years. From this arose the most grievous schism of all, between the Avignon and Roman popes. It lasted forty years and was finally ended at the Council of Constance. §. CXXXVIII.

units.la: Bonifacius IX. P. juxta prædecessoris Urbani VI. sanctionem, jubilæum celebrans, argentariam messem facit, & post dicennium etiam novum indicit; bullis indulgentiarum addens, eas ratas fore porrigentibus Ecclesiæ R. adjutrices manus. Annatas eitam seu reditus unius anni Sacerdotii alicujus in tota Europa vacantis, reddendas Pontifici R. severè sancit: ibid.
units.tr: Boniface IX, following the sanction of his predecessor Urban VI, celebrated the jubilee and made a harvest of silver. Afterwards, after ten years, he also declared a new one. He added to the bulls of indulgences the assurance that they would be ratified for those who offered helping hands to the Roman Church. He also severely decreed that the annates, that is, the revenue of one year from any priesthood vacant anywhere in Europe, be paid to the Roman Pontiff: ibid.

units.la: Johannis Huffi doctrina in Bohemia latè spargi incipit, adeò ut Augustæ Vindelicorum Huffitæ inquiri, plurélque comburi coeperint. §.CXXXVII.
units.tr: The teaching of John Hus began to spread widely in Bohemia, so that at Augsburg the Hussites began to be sought out, and many were burned. §. CXXXVII.

units.la: Avenione in locum Clementis VII. succedit Petrus Luna, seu Benedictus XIII. qui jurans se abiturum Papatu, si Ecclesiæ ad tollendum schisma videretur, sequente anno, ut id faceret, rogatus, negavit, Petri naviculam deserendam esse. §. CXXXIX.
units.tr: At Avignon, Peter de Luna, or Benedict XIII, succeeded Clement VII. Swearing that he would abandon the papacy if it seemed to the Church that this would end the schism, he was asked to do so the following year, and refused, saying that the little boat of Peter must not be deserted. §. CXXXIX.

units.la: SECVLVM DECIMVM QVINTVM.
units.tr: THE FIFTEENTH CENTURY.

units.la: §. CXXXIX. — CXLIX.
units.tr: §. CXXXIX. — CXLIX.

units.la: INnocentio VII. Romæ succedit Gregorius XII. Errerius dictus, Juràrat summa execratione, se Papatum depositurum, siquidem Antipapa idem faceret. quod tamen postea in Concilio Pisano facere renuit. §. CXXXIX.
units.tr: Gregory XII, called Errerius, succeeds Innocent VII at Rome. He swore with the utmost execration that he would give up the papacy, provided the antipope did the same. Later, however, at the Council of Pisa, he refused to do so. §. CXXXIX.

units.la: Cardinales in Concilio Pisano abolendi schismatis gratia, Pontificem utrumque, Benedictum & Gregorium deponunt; & Alexandrum V. eligunt. Renuente utroque Papatum deserere, tres sunt Antipapæ, & Ecclesia Romana triceps. ibid.
units.tr: At the Council of Pisa the cardinals, for the sake of abolishing the schism, deposed both pontiffs, Benedict and Gregory, and elected Alexander V. Since both refused to give up the papacy, there were three antipopes, and the Roman Church was three-headed. ibid.

units.la: Alexandro V. mortuo succedit Balthassar Cossa, seu Johannes XXIII. juxta alios XXIV. ibid.
units.tr: After Alexander V died, Balthasar Cossa succeeded, as John XXIII, or, according to others, XXIV. ibid.

units.la: Huslus causam suam Romæ per Legatos agit, & excommunicatur. §. CXLIX.
units.tr: Hus pleads his cause at Rome through legates, and is excommunicated. §. CXLIX.

units.la: Johannes Romæ Synodum celebrat, coronaturus Sigismundum, & Ecclesiam tranquillaturus. In prima Sessione post Missam bubo, ferale omen, apparuit, nec nisi fustibus interemptus discessit. §. CXXXIX.
units.tr: John holds a synod at Rome, intending to crown Sigismund and to calm the Church. In the first session, after Mass, an owl, a deadly omen, appeared, and it left only when it had been killed with clubs. §. CXXXIX.

units.la: Nicolaus Clemangis Ecclesiam Romanam Babylonem, meretricem &c. appellat. Gerson Ecclesiam sine Papa esse posse sustinet, & ruinam ominatur. Alii, Theodoricus de Nyem, Joh. Oldocastel, Theodoricus Urias, Huslius inprimis, & Hieronymus Prag. &c. Ecclesiam R. graviter oppugnant. §. CXLVII. CXLVIII.
units.tr: Nicolas Clemangis calls the Roman Church Babylon, a harlot, and so on. Gerson maintains that the Church can exist without a Pope, and he foretells its ruin. Others, Theodoric of Niem, John Oldcastle, Theodoric Uria, and above all Hus, and Jerome of Prague, and others, severely assail the Roman Church. §. CXLVII. CXLVIII.

units.la: Sigismundi Imp. labore incredibili cogitur Concilium Constantiense, schismatis abolendi, & Ecclesiæ reformandæ causa. Eodem 3. Nov. Joh. Huss accessit. Geritúrque res tota suffragiis quinque nationum. §. CXL.
units.tr: Through the incredible labour of the Emperor Sigismund, the Council of Constance is convened for the sake of abolishing the schism and reforming the Church. On 3 November John Hus arrived. The whole business is conducted by the votes of the five nations. §. CXL.

units.la: Johannes P. causæ diffidens Concilio se subducit; & ex fuga retractus, gravissimorúmque scelerum convictus Papatu abdicatur, & in carcerem rapitur. Gregorius P. Arimini, ne idem sibi accideret, per legatos suos sese in Concilio abdicat. ibid.
units.tr: Pope John, distrusting his cause, withdraws from the Council; and, being dragged back from his flight and convicted of the gravest crimes, he is deprived of the papacy and hauled off to prison. Gregory XII, at Rimini, lest the same befall him, abdicates in the Council through his legates. ibid.

units.la: Johannus Huss damnatus in Concilio, contra datam fidem, comburitur. §. CXLVIII. Idem fatum sequente anno Hieronymus Prag. subiit. ibid.
units.tr: John Hus, condemned by the Council contrary to the safe-conduct he had been promised, is burned. §. CXLVIII. The following year Jerome of Prague suffered the same fate. ibid.

units.la: Concilium Const. decernit, Laicis sub una specie Eucharistiam distribuendam; Bohemis protestantibus, Huslium & Hieronymum in Martyrum numerum referentibus. Unde bellum Hussiticum oritur, per annos novendecim multis cladibus extractum. §. CXL. CXLVIII.
units.tr: The Council of Constance decrees that the Eucharist is to be distributed to the laity under one kind only. The Bohemian protestants, counting Hus and Jerome among the martyrs, object. Hence the Hussite war arises, dragged out over nineteen years with many disasters. §. CXL. CXLVIII.

units.la: Urgetur in Concilio Reformatio Ecclesiæ. Dissidentibus Patribus, priùs abdicatis jam tribus Antipapis, novus Papa Martinus V. eligitur. §. CXL.
units.tr: Reformation of the Church is pressed in the Council. The Fathers disagree; since the three antipopes had already abdicated, a new Pope, Martin V, is elected. §. CXL.

units.la: Petrus de Aliaco reformationis capita digerit, causas in primis, ob quas Papa corripi & deponi possit, consignat. Sed res omnis post electionem Papæ in fumum abiit. ibid. & §. CXLVII.
units.tr: Peter of Ailly sets out the heads of reform, and in particular records the causes on account of which a Pope may be rebuked and deposed. But the whole business vanished into smoke after the election of the Pope. ibid. and §. CXLVII.

units.la: Martinus V. à reformatione abhorrens, invito Sigismundo Constantia discedit. Atque ita Concilium, re infecta finitur. §. CXL.
units.tr: Martin V, shrinking from reform, leaves Constance against the wishes of Sigismund. And so the Council ended with nothing accomplished. §. CXL.

units.la: Martino V. succedit Eugenius IV. qui statim, Sigismundo consentiente, Basileæ Concilium inchoat, & Ecclesiæ reformandæ studium præ se fert. §. CXLI.
units.tr: Eugene IV succeeds Martin V. With Sigismund's consent he at once opens a Council at Basel, and professes a zeal for reforming the Church. §. CXLI.

units.la: Bohemi Basileensi Concilio se sistentes, & rationem fidei suæ exponentes, certis conditionibus communionem sub utraque specie impetrant. ibid.
units.tr: The Bohemians present themselves to the Council at Basel, set out the account of their faith, and on certain conditions obtain communion under both kinds. ibid.

units.la: Eugenius intellecto, disputari in Concilio, an Papa Concilio subsit; illud, Basilea relicta, Ferrariam atque inde Florentiam transfert, invitis Concilii Præsidibus. Ne igitur Concilium Basileense dissolveretur, Sigismundus ipse Basileam venit. ibid.
units.tr: Eugene, understanding that the Council was debating whether the Pope is subject to the Council, leaves Basel and transfers the assembly to Ferrara, and from there to Florence, against the wishes of the Council's presidents. Therefore, so that the Council of Basel would not be dissolved, Sigismund himself came to Basel. ibid.

units.la: Eugenius à Concilio ob lupinam tyrannidem deponitur, lecto in ejus locum Amedæo Sabaudo, Felicis V. nomine insigni; ab eodemque Concilio simul statuitur, reformandam esse Ecclesiam in capite & membris, & Concilio Papam subesse. ibid.
units.tr: Eugene is deposed by the Council for wolfish tyranny, and Amadeus of Savoy is chosen in his place, under the notable name Felix V. The same Council also decrees that the Church must be reformed in head and members, and that the Pope is subject to the Council. ibid.

units.la: Pragmatica sanctio, quam statuerant in Concilio Basileensi Patres communi consensu, in qua capita, quibus Ecclesiastica dignitas conservari posset, digesta & Pontifici beneficiorum Regni collationes, appellationes item ad Romanam Curiam ademptæ erant; Lutetiæ à Rege Galliæ post Concilium in Biturigibus celebratum, publicatur, quam deinceps Pontifices, seu hæreticam oppugnarunt. §. CXLVII.
units.tr: The Pragmatic Sanction, which the Fathers had established at the Council of Basel by common consent, in which were set out the heads by which ecclesiastical dignity could be preserved, and by which the Pontiff's conferral of benefices in the kingdom was curtailed, and appeals to the Roman Curia were likewise abolished, was published at Paris by the King of France after the Council held at Bourges. The Pontiffs afterwards attacked it, even as heretical. §. CXLVII.

units.la: Florentiæ Concilium ab Eugenio celebratur, præsente Johanne Palæologo Imp. Constantinop. Josepho Patriarcha, aliisque Græcis, unionem offerentibus, & auxilia adversus Turcas expetentibus. Transactio lubrica, repugnante Michaele Ephesino Episcopo fit, & à Græcis post rescinditur. §. CXLI.
units.tr: The Council at Florence is held by Eugene, in the presence of John Palaeologus, Emperor of Constantinople, Joseph the Patriarch, and other Greeks, who offer union and seek aid against the Turks. The agreement was shaky, made over the opposition of Michael, Bishop of Ephesus, and was afterwards rescinded by the Greeks. §. CXLI.

units.la: Typographia à Johanne Gutenbergio, aurifice Argentinensi, Moguntiï profertur, eáque non parum procedente tempore Antichristi revelatio juvatur. §. CXLIV.
units.tr: Printing is brought forth at Mainz by John Gutenberg, a goldsmith of Strasbourg; and as time advances it greatly helps the revelation of Antichrist. §. CXLIV.

units.la: 1444. Ludovicus Delphinus, Caroli VII. Filius, Concilium Basileense, Eugenio incitante, dissoluturus, Basileam obsidet, & Helvetiis paucis exercitum ejus vastum fundentibus, obsidionem solvit. §. CXLI.
units.tr: 1444. Louis the Dauphin, son of Charles VII, intending at Eugene's urging to dissolve the Council of Basel, besieges Basel. When the few Swiss routed his vast army, he lifted the siege. §. CXLI.

units.la: 1447. Eugenio succedit Nicolaus V. fautor literarum insignis. Cui Friderici III. Imp. intercessione Felix V. cessit, dignitate Cardinalis contentus. Ejus opera literæ in Europa renatæ, literatíque passim aucti sunt. §. CXLIII.
units.tr: 1447. Nicholas V succeeds Eugene, a distinguished patron of letters. Through the intercession of the Emperor Frederick III, Felix V yielded to him, content with the dignity of cardinal. Through his efforts letters were reborn in Europe, and men of learning were everywhere advanced. §. CXLIII.

units.la: 1453. Constantinus Imp. à Nicolao auxilia implorat contra Muhammedem Constantinopolin maximo exercitu aggressum; neque impetrat quicquam. Inde Constantinopolis d. 29. Maii capitur, Constantinus in fuga occiditur, totumque Orientale Imperium Ottomannico imperio cedit. §. CXLII.
units.tr: 1453. Constantine the Emperor implores help from Nicholas against Muhammad, who attacked Constantinople with a huge army, and he obtains nothing. Constantinople was then taken on 29 May, Constantine was killed in flight, and the whole Eastern Empire passed to the Ottoman empire. §. CXLII.

units.la: 1458. Æneas Sylvius, Pii II. nomine Papa creatur; Concilii Basileensis antehac scriba, cujus etiam adversus Pontificiam potestatem acta probaverat. At Papa jam, improbavit, eadem, & Pontificiæ potestatis fimbrias dilatavit si quis alius. §. CXLIV.
units.tr: 1458. Aeneas Sylvius is created Pope under the name Pius II. He had formerly been secretary of the Council of Basel, and had approved its acts against papal power. But now as Pope he disapproved of the same acts, and extended the fringes of papal power more than anyone else. §. CXLIV.

units.la: 1459. Sigismundus Dux Austriæ, quòd Cardinalem Cusanum in vincula conjecisset, à Pio P. excommunicatus, ad Concilium, & à Concilio ad Christum provocat. §. CXLVII.
units.tr: 1459. Sigismund, Duke of Austria, because he had thrown Cardinal Cusanus into chains, is excommunicated by Pius II, and appeals from the Pope to a Council, and from the Council to Christ. §. CXLVII.

units.la: 1460. Gregorius Heimburgius Sigismundi Cancellarius ejusque defensor, à Pio eodem excommunicatus, masculè respondet, & Synagogam Romanam graviter perstringit. ibid.
units.tr: 1460. Gregory Heimburg, chancellor of Sigismund and his defender, excommunicated by the same Pius, replies manfully and lashes the Roman synagogue severely. ibid.

units.la: 1464. Pio II. succedit Paulus II. qui Cardinales veste Coccinea, & rubenti petaso insignivit, & montes pietatis instituit. §. CXLVI.
units.tr: 1464. Paul II succeeds Pius II. He decorated the cardinals with scarlet robes and red hats, and established the monts de piété. §. CXLVI.

units.la: 1471. Paulo succedit Sixtus IV. literatus satis, sed flagitiosissimus idem, fundator lupanaris Romani nobilis, in quo singula scorta hebdomatim singulos ei Julios penfitârunt; Helvetiis etiam fœdere sibi unitis pudenda bulla illudit. ibid.
units.tr: 1471. Sixtus IV succeeds Paul. He was sufficiently learned, but equally most shameless, the founder of the famous Roman brothel, in which individual prostitutes paid him individual Julii every week. He also mocked the Swiss, though they were united to him by treaty, with a shameful bull. ibid.

units.la: 1479. Johannes de Wesalia Wormatiensis Concionator; & Wes- selus Groningensis Papæ tyrannidem & abusus strenuè oppugnant. §. CXLVII.
units.tr: 1479. John of Wesel, preacher at Worms, and Wessel of Groningen vigorously attack the tyranny and abuses of the Pope. §. CXLVII.

units.la: 1484. Sixtum excipit Johannes Baptista Cybo, ex antiqua Græcorum familia, dictus Innocentius VIII. sedecim ante Pontificatum liberorum Pater. ibid.
units.tr: 1484. Sixtus is succeeded by John Baptist Cybo, of an ancient Greek family, called Innocent VIII, who before his pontificate was the father of sixteen children. ibid.

units.la: 1492. Alexander VI. cui Borgiæ cognomen, Papa creatur, homo ad exitium Italiæ natus, qui Divina & humana omnia venum expo- suit; ditiones noviter detectas Hispaniæ inter & Lusitaniæ Reges partitus est; & cum Lucretia filia notha furtivam consuetudinem habuit. ibid. Eodem Pontifice Guicciardinus, Baptista Mantuanus, Sannazarius, Savanarola, alii Pontificum scelera deexerunt, Antichristianismum traduxerunt. §. CXLVII. CXLVIII.
units.tr: 1492. Alexander VI, surnamed Borgia, is created Pope, a man born for the ruin of Italy, who put all things divine and human up for sale. He divided newly discovered lands between the kings of Spain and Portugal, and he had a secret liaison with his illegitimate daughter Lucretia. ibid. Under this same Pontiff, Guicciardini, Baptista Mantuanus, Sannazaro, Savonarola, and others denounced the crimes of the Popes and exposed Antichristianism. §. CXLVII. CXLVIII.

units.la: SECULUM DECIMUM SEXTUM.
units.tr: THE SIXTEENTH CENTURY.

units.la: §. CXLIX. — CCVIII.
units.tr: §. CXLIX. — CCVIII.

units.la: ALexander veneno a filio Borgia Cardinalibus nonnullis praeparat o, & ministri incuria parenti propinato, extinctus Pium III. & hoc post 26. dies mortuo, ex fratre nepotem Julium II. successorem habet. Totum terrarum orbem bellis hic involvit, & S. Petri patrimonium absolutione casuum reservatorum auxit. §. CXLIX.
units.tr: Alexander, poisoned by his son Borgia, had prepared poison for some cardinals. But through the carelessness of a servant it was given to his own father, and he died. Pius III died twenty-six days later, and Julius II, a nephew of Alexander through his brother, succeeded him. Julius involved the whole world in wars, and by the absolution of reserved cases he increased the patrimony of St Peter. §. CXLIX.

units.la: Cardinales quatuor Gallicarum partium, Imp. Maximiliano, & Rege Galliae consentientibus, Concilium Pisis convocant, & Julium Papam indignum sede Pontificia pronuntiant. ibid.
units.tr: Four cardinals of the French party, with the consent of Emperor Maximilian and the King of France, convened a council at Pisa and declared Pope Julius unworthy of the papal see. ibid.

units.la: Julius contra Concilium Romae ad Lateranum celebrat, & Cardinales hos dignitatibus privat. ibid.
units.tr: Julius held a council at the Lateran in Rome against this council and deprived these cardinals of their dignities. ibid.

units.la: Idem Ludovicum XII. Galliae Regem excommunicat. Hic cusae monetae verba haec inscripsit: Perdam Babylonem. §. CL.
units.tr: The same Julius excommunicated Louis XII, King of France. On the coin he struck, Louis inscribed these words: I will destroy Babylon. §. CL.

units.la: Budaeus Pragmaticam sanctionem strenuè defendit. ibid.
units.tr: Budaeus vigorously defended the Pragmatic Sanction. ibid.

units.la: Faber Stapulensis, Picus Mirandulanus Papatum oppugnant; & Sebastianus Brand Ecclesiae reformationem instare praesagit. ibid.
units.tr: Faber Stapulensis and Pico della Mirandola attacked the papacy. Sebastian Brant foretold that a reformation of the Church was at hand. ibid.

units.la: Julius, Vaticanum aedificare aggressus moritur, excipiente Johanne Medices, seu Leone X. homine Epicuraeo, sub quo Concilium Lateranense Pisanum extinguit. §. CLI. CLII.
units.tr: Julius began to build the Vatican and died. He was succeeded by Giovanni de' Medici, or Leo X, a man of Epicurean character, under whom the Lateran council was brought to an end and the Council of Pisa was extinguished. §. CLI. CLII.

units.la: Leo Helvetios contra Gallos Mediolano inhiantes in Italiam inducit. Qui Novariae obsessi, erumpentes, instructissimum exercitum Gallorum vincunt. §. CLI.
units.tr: Leo brought the Swiss into Italy against the French, who were coveting Milan. Besieged at Novara, the Swiss broke out and defeated a very well-equipped French army. §. CLI.

units.la: Leo idem a Maximiliano Imp. ad Franciscum Regem Galliae deficit, eique Imperii Constantinopolitani coronam confert. Multa deinceps adversus Maximilianum, & Successorem ejus Carolum V. improbè machinatus est. ibid.
units.tr: The same Leo deserted Emperor Maximilian for Francis, King of France, and conferred on him the crown of the Empire of Constantinople. Afterwards he schemed wickedly for a long time against Maximilian and his successor, Charles V. ibid.

units.la: Idem sublata Sanctione Pragmatica, Concordata cum Rege Francisco agitat, de nominatione Episcoporum & Abbatum. ibid.
units.tr: The same Leo, having set aside the Pragmatic Sanction, negotiated a concordat with King Francis concerning the nomination of bishops and abbots. ibid.

units.la: Leo missis per omnia Regna literis indulgentias pollicetur, interventu pecuniae, falsis etiam praetextibus usus. Lutherus ea de re adversus Tecelium indulgentiarum praeconem, scribit ad Moguntinum, & themata Witebergae indulgentiis opponit. Zwinglius quoque
units.tr: Leo sent letters to all kingdoms promising indulgences in return for money, and he used false pretexts as well. On this matter Luther wrote against Tetzel, the hawker of indulgences, wrote to the Archbishop of Mainz, and set forth theses at Wittenberg against indulgences. Zwingli also

units.la: d que de corruptione Ecclesiae cum Cardinale Sedunensi disputat, & Evangelium praedicare incipit. Occasio haec fuit Reformationis Ecclesiasticae mox insecutae. §. CLII. CLIII.
units.tr: disputed about the corruption of the Church with the Cardinal of Sion, and began to preach the Gospel. This occasion was the beginning of the ecclesiastical Reformation that soon followed. §. CLII. CLIII.

units.la: Reformationis vero necessitatem arguunt graves de corruptione Ecclesiae Romanae querelae, eo tempore, si unquam alias ingeminatae. §. CLVI. CLVII.
units.tr: Grave complaints about the corruption of the Roman Church, louder than at any other time, proved the necessity of reformation. §. CLVI. CLVII.

units.la: Lutherus Romam citatus, eo venire detrectat. Evocatur igitur Augustam Vindelicorum ad Cajetanum, cum quo de indulgentiis & Coena Domini disputans, ad Papam provocat. ibid.
units.tr: Luther, summoned to Rome, refused to go there. He was therefore called to Augsburg before Cajetan, and there, disputing with him about indulgences and the Lord's Supper, he appealed to the Pope. ibid.

units.la: Zwinglius Tiguri Evangelium praedicans, Samsoni indulgentiarum institutori omnibus viribus resistit, & de eo ad Hugonem Const. Episcopum scribit. §. CLII.
units.tr: Zwingli, preaching the Gospel at Zurich, resisted with all his strength Samson, the promoter of indulgences, and wrote about him to Hugo, Bishop of Constance. §. CLII.

units.la: Lutherus Lipsiae cum Eccio de primatu Papae & purgatorio disputat. ibid.
units.tr: Luther disputed at Leipzig with Eck about the primacy of the Pope and purgatory. ibid.

units.la: Lutherus a Leone excommunicatus ad Concilium provocat; & Pontificiis libros ejus comburentibus, ipse vicissim Wittebergae jus Canonicum comburit; librum de captivitate Babylonica scribit, & paulo post duos Papatus nervos, vota Monastica, & Missas privatas, incidit. ibid.
units.tr: Luther, excommunicated by Leo, appealed to a council. When the Papists burned his books, he in turn burned the canon law at Wittenberg. He wrote the book on the Babylonian captivity, and soon after attacked two pillars of the papacy, monastic vows and private masses. ibid.

units.la: Wormatiae in Comitiis, salvo conductu Caroli, comparet Lutherus, & assistente ipsi Schurfio J.C. coram Imperio & Ordinibus magna constantia de doctrina sua respondet. Proscriptus in arce Warnburgensi decem menses delitescit, & denuo a Leone excommunicatur. ibid.
units.tr: At Worms, at the diet, under Charles's safe-conduct, Luther appeared and, with the jurist Schurff assisting him, answered with great constancy before the Empire and the estates concerning his doctrine. Outlawed, he lay hidden for ten months in the castle of Wartburg, and was again excommunicated by Leo. ibid.

units.la: Leoni succedit Hadrianus Ultrajectinus, Praeceptor Caroli, qui homo ingenuus reformationis in capite & membris necessitatem agnoscit; reformationem molitur, sed mancam mutilamque. §. CLVIII. CLXI.
units.tr: Leo was succeeded by Adrian of Utrecht, Charles's tutor, a frank man who acknowledged the need for reformation in head and members. He undertook a reformation, but an incomplete and maimed one. §. CLVIII. CLXI.

units.la: Ordines Imperii Norinbergae centum Gravamina, quibus Germania a Pontifice onerata sit, consignant, eademque ad Papam perscribunt, petentes ut Concilium generale indicat. §. CLIX.
units.tr: The estates of the Empire at Nuremberg drew up a hundred grievances by which Germany was burdened by the Pope, and sent them to the Pope, asking that a general council be convened. §. CLIX.

units.la: Lutherus, abrogata Missa, formulam communionis Sacrae, & praeconii Evangelici Witebergensibus ordinat, & S. Biblia in vernaculam linguam convertere incipit. §. CLII.
units.tr: Luther, having abolished the Mass, drew up for the Wittenbergers a form of the sacred communion and of evangelical preaching, and began to translate the Holy Bible into the vernacular language. §. CLII.

units.la: Glisccente contra Zwinglium offensione, Senatus Tigurinus Synodum indicit, in qua Jacobus Faber, Episcopi Constantiensis vicarius, Tigurinorum rogatu comparet. Finita disputatione cum solidi nihil objectum Zwinglio, & ad singula responsum ab eodem solide constitisset, Senatus contusconsulto edito mandatur, ut omissis traditionibus purum putum Dei verbum praedicetur. ibid.
units.tr: As offence against Zwingli grew, the Senate of Zurich called a synod, at which James Faber, vicar of the Bishop of Constance, appeared at the request of the Zurichers. When the disputation was over, nothing solid had been objected to Zwingli, and he had answered each point solidly. By a decree the Senate ordered that, with traditions set aside, the pure Word of God be preached. ibid.

units.la: Hadriano P. non sine veneni suspicione defuncto, surrogatur Clemens VII. cui Antipapa Urbanus VI. obnititur. §. CLXIII. CLXIV.
units.tr: Adrian P. died, not without suspicion of poison, and Clement VII was put in his place. Against him the antipope Urban VI made a stand. §. CLXIII. CLXIV.

units.la: In Germaniae multis locis Ecclesiae reformantur, Doctoribusque ut purum Dei verbum praedicent, injungitur. Tiguri quoque Missa abrogata Templa ab imaginibus & statuis purgantur; nequicquam Cantonibus reliquis reclamantibus. ibid. & §. CLXII.
units.tr: The Churches were reformed in many places in Germany, and the preachers were ordered to preach the pure Word of God. At Zurich too the Mass was abolished, and the churches were cleansed of images and statues, though the other cantons protested in vain. ibid. & §. CLXII.

units.la: Clemens P. Campegium Norinbergam mittit, & reformationem offert. quam cum fucatam esse intellexisset Ordines, ad Concilium provocant, & interea Evangelium pure & modeste ut doceatur, decernunt. Post conventum Ferdinandus, Campegius, Episcopique plures seorsim convenientes Wormatiense edictum, quo Lutherus damnatus erat, urgent, Missae abrogationem prohibent. §. CLXIII.
units.tr: Pope Clement sent Campeggio to Nuremberg and offered a reformation. When the estates perceived that it was a sham, they appealed to a council, and meanwhile decreed that the Gospel be taught purely and modestly. After the diet, Ferdinand, Campeggio and several bishops, meeting privately, pressed the Edict of Worms, by which Luther had been condemned, and forbade the abolition of the Mass. §. CLXIII.

units.la: Cantones Helvetiae novem Pontificii, una cum Valesiis, Lucernae conveniunt, Reformationis ipsi quoque articulos condunt, temporum suorum calamitatem Sacerdotum iniquitati imputant, nundinationes foedas prohibent, & Curtisanos, quos Romanos nebulones vocant, coercent. §. CLIX.
units.tr: The nine Papist cantons of Switzerland met at Lucerne together with the Valais. They also drew up articles of reformation, blamed the calamities of their times on the wickedness of the priests, forbade shameful trading in offices, and restrained the Curtisans, whom they call Roman scoundrels. §. CLIX.

units.la: Spirae Ordines Imperii conveniunt, ubi Principibus Pontificiis edictum Wormatiense urgentibus, reliquis eise opponentibus, Ferdinandus itarem moderatur, ut promisso Concilio omnes acquieverint. §. CLXIII.
units.tr: The estates of the Empire met at Speyer. There, while the Papist princes pressed the Edict of Worms and the others opposed it, Ferdinand moderated the matter so that all would acquiesce in the promised council. §. CLXIII.

units.la: Cantones Helvetiae duodecim Badae institua disputatione, sanciunt, ne veterem religionem quisquam deserat, utque futuri Concilii authoritatem omnes sequantur. ibid.
units.tr: The twelve cantons of Switzerland, at Baden, after a disputation was instituted, decreed that no one should abandon the old religion, and that all should abide by the authority of the future council. ibid.

units.la: In Suecia Gustavus visitationem Ecclesiarum instituit, abusus Pontificios, & potestatem Politicam Episcoporum, frustra tergiversantium, abolet. §. CLXII.
units.tr: In Sweden Gustavus instituted a visitation of the Churches and abolished the Papist abuses and the political power of the bishops, who vainly tried to evade it. §. CLXII.

units.la: Clemens P. cum Gallo adversus Caesarem foedus init. Unde Borbonius ex Galliis ejectus, cum Fronspergio, Caesaris nomine Romam capiunt, Romam spoliant, & Papam in mole Hadriani obsident. §. CLXIII. CLXIV.
units.tr: Pope Clement made an alliance with the French King against Caesar. Whereupon Bourbon, expelled from France, together with Frundsberg, in Caesar's name, took Rome, plundered Rome, and besieged the Pope in the Mole of Hadrian. §. CLXIII. CLXIV.

units.la: Bernates, cum disputationis Badensis acta iis communicata non essent, aliam Bernae disputationem instituunt, in qua bona causa vincit, & post Ecclesia reformatur. §. CLXII.
units.tr: The men of Bern, since the acts of the Baden disputation had not been communicated to them, instituted another disputation at Bern. In it the good cause won, and afterwards the Church was reformed. §. CLXII.

units.la: Johannes Saxoniae Elector, & Philippus Hassiae Landgravius bellum parant adversus Pontificios, qui jam ante fœdus contra Evangelicos iniverant. Interponentibus se Palatino & Trevirensi pax constituitur. §. CLXIII.
units.tr: John, Elector of Saxony, and Philip, Landgrave of Hesse, prepared war against the Papists, who had already before this made a league against the evangelicals. With the Palatine and the Archbishop of Trier interposing themselves, peace was established. §. CLXIII.

units.la: Spiræ Comitia Ordinum Imperii celebrantur, & à Pontificiis Wormatiense contra Novatores decretum urgetur; protestantibus Saxone & Hassio. unde Evangelicis Protestantium nomen. ibid.
units.tr: The diet of the estates of the Empire was held at Speyer, and the Papists pressed the Worms decree against the innovators. The Saxon and the Hessian protested, and from this the evangelicals received the name Protestants. ibid.

units.la: Cæsar Pontifici reconciliatus, Bononiæ coronatur, postquam verbis conceptis jurâsset, se Pontificiæ potestatis defensorem fore. Cum eodem P. de Concilio convocando prius egerat. Papa à Concilio abhorrente, Carolus promisit, se ad tollendum schisma primo leniori-bus remediis, & iis non succedentibus armis usurum. Inde conventus Augustanus indicitur, in quo Confessio Augustana Imperatori & Ordinibus prælegitur. Concludit Carolus, Protestantibus omnia inintegrum restituenda esse, dato deliberandi usque ad d. 15. Apr. sequentis anni, spatio. Interim Cæsar cum fœderatis vim parat. §. CLXIV.
units.tr: Caesar, reconciled to the Pope, was crowned at Bologna, after he had sworn in set words that he would be the defender of papal power. He had earlier negotiated with the same Pope about convening a council. As the Pope shrank from a council, Charles promised that to remove the schism he would use milder remedies first, and if these did not succeed, arms. Then the diet of Augsburg was called, at which the Augsburg Confession was read before the Emperor and the estates. Charles decided that everything must be restored to the Protestants as it was before, with time to deliberate until 15 April of the following year. Meanwhile Caesar prepared force with his allies. §. CLXIV.

units.la: Tigurini à quinque Pagis graviter offensi, annonæ comeatu iisdem interdicunt. Qui ad extremas angustias redacti, silentio conductis copiis, signa opinione Tigurinorum citius proferunt, & imparatos confusosque vincunt. Zwinglius castrensis præco in eo prælio cœditur. & mox religionis pax concluditur. ibid.
units.tr: The men of Zurich, gravely offended by the five rural cantons, cut off their supply of food and provisions. Reduced to the utmost straits, the cantons, keeping their troops secret, unfurled their standards sooner than the Zurichers expected, and defeated them, unprepared and in confusion. Zwingli, serving as army chaplain, was killed in that battle, and soon a peace concerning religion was concluded. ibid.

units.la: Imminente à Turca bello, Suinfurti pax religionis Germaniæ ad futurum usque Concilium conceditur. ibid.
units.tr: With war threatened by the Turk, a peace concerning religion in Germany was granted at Schweinfurt until the future council. ibid.

units.la: Papa denuo, deserto Cæsare, Massiliæ fœdus init cum Francisco Galliæ Rege, cujus filio neptim suam Catharinam Medicæam despondet. Ex eo tempore Franciscus in Maxentium quendam efferatus, diris supplicis adversus Evangelicos sæviit. ibid.
units.tr: The Pope again, deserting Caesar, made a league at Marseille with Francis, King of France, to whose son he betrothed his niece Catherine de' Medici. From that time Francis, enraged against a certain Maxentius, raged with dire punishments against the evangelicals. ibid.

units.la: Clementi succedit Paulus III. Farnesius, cujus vitam & mores spurcos liber Italicus depingit. §. CLXV.
units.tr: Clement was succeeded by Paul III Farnese, whose life and filthy morals an Italian book portrays. §. CLXV.

units.la: Jesuitarum Societas, authore Ignatio Lojola, à Paulo P. approbatur. §. CLXIX. CLXX. Capucini sub eodem caput exerunt. Hi junctis viribus Papatum ruentem sustinere conantur. §. CLXXI.
units.tr: The Society of Jesuits, founded by Ignatius Loyola, was approved by Pope Paul. §. CLXIX. CLXX. Under the same pope the Capuchins raised their heads. These, with their united strength, tried to sustain the collapsing papacy. §. CLXXI.

units.la: Paulus Concilium indicit Mantuæ, & statim Vicentiam transfert. Sed deprecantibus Venetis res non succedit. §. CLXVI.
units.tr: Paul summons a council to meet at Mantua, but at once transfers it to Vicenza. Yet, the Venetians objecting, the matter does not succeed. §. CLXVI.

units.la: Christianus Daniæ Rex puriorem in toto Regno religionem instituit. §. CLXII.
units.tr: Christian, King of Denmark, establishes a purer religion throughout his whole kingdom. §. CLXII.

units.la: Jussu Pauli P. à delegatis Cardinalibus & Præsulibus consilium de emendanda Ecclesia conscribitur, & Pontifici exhibetur. In consilio eo Ecclesiæ morbi & ulcera ingenuè satis deteguntur. Sed res tota successum nullum sortita est. §. CLXVII. Con-
units.tr: By order of Pope Paul, a plan for amending the Church is drawn up by the delegated Cardinals and Prelates and presented to the Pontiff. In that plan the diseases and ulcers of the Church are laid bare with considerable frankness. But the whole affair had no success. §. CLXVII. Con-

units.la: Concilium Tridentinum ante indictum, protestantibus licet Evangelicis contra illud, utpote Pontificis libidini inserviens, celebrari die 13. Dec. incipit. §. CLXXII. Reformatio in eo plane frivola tentatur. §. CLXXIII. CLXXIV.
units.tr: The Council of Trent begins to be held on 13 December, having been announced beforehand; the Evangelical Protestants object to it, as serving the Pontiff's lust. A reformation is attempted in it, which is quite trivial. §. CLXXII. CLXXIII. CLXXIV.

units.la: Sub initium Concilii hujus Cornelius Musslus, Episcopus Bitontinus, & Caranza, Ecclesiae Romanae corruptionem, habitis orationibus, graphice depingunt. §. CLXXV.
units.tr: At the beginning of this Council, Cornelius Musslus, Bishop of Bitonto, and Caranza vividly depict, in their speeches, the corruption of the Roman Church. §. CLXXV.

units.la: Fridericus Palatinus Elector Ecclesias suas, abrogata Missa, reformat. §. CLXII.
units.tr: Frederick, Elector Palatine, reforms his churches, the Mass having been abolished. §. CLXII.

units.la: Carolus Imp. à Paulo P. incitatus diro bello cum Protestantibus Principibus, Smalcaldico foedere junctis, decernit in quo superiore acie Fridericum Electorem Saxoniae Mulbergaevi, & Philippum Hassiae Landgravium, ad Salinas Saxonicas, fraude capit. §. CLXIV.
units.tr: The Emperor Charles, spurred on by Paul, decrees a dire war against the Protestant Princes joined in the Smalkaldic League, in which, in the battle at Mühlberg, he captures by treachery Frederick, Elector of Saxony, and Philip, Landgrave of Hesse, at the Saxon Salt-works. §. CLXIV.

units.la: Eduardus VI. Angliae Rex, profligata Pontificia doctrina, religionem mutat. Eadem occasione Scotia quoque puriorem religionem amplectitur. §. CLXIII.
units.tr: Edward VI, King of England, having overthrown Papal doctrine, changes the religion. On the same occasion Scotland also embraces a purer religion. §. CLXIII.

units.la: Caroli jussu, cum Concilium Tridentinum Protestantes abnuerent, liber conscribitur de religione in Germania observanda Interim, dum Concilium legitime instituatur. Irascitur propterea Carolo Paulus P. nec Protestantes plerique librum probant. ibid.
units.tr: At Charles's command, since the Protestants refused the Council of Trent, a book is written on the religion to be observed in Germany, the Interim, until a council is lawfully convened. For this reason Pope Paul is angry with Charles, and most Protestants do not approve the book. ibid.

units.la: Julius III. ante Mariam de Mohte dictus, Paulo post diutinam Cardinalium dissensionem succedit, Sardanapalus insignis. §. CLXXVI. Petente Caesare, Concilium Bononia Tridentum revocat. §. CLXXVII.
units.tr: Julius III, called before Mary de Monte, succeeds Paul after a long dispute among the Cardinals, a notable Sardanapalus. §. CLXXVI. At the Emperor's request, he recalls the Council from Bologna to Trent. §. CLXXVII.

units.la: Mauritius, Elector Saxoniae, foedere cum Rege Galliarum aliisque inito, Socerum Philippum Landgravium à captivitate iniqua, & Germaniam à servitute liberaturus, Carolum bello petit, & victor simul Socerum liberat, simul Passavienssi transactione religionis Pacem impetrat. Hoc igitur bello purior religio ab oppressione Pontificia liberata, & ringente licet Pontifice, Pax perpetua Ecclesiae impetrata est. §. CLXXVIII.
units.tr: Maurice, Elector of Saxony, having entered into an alliance with the King of France and others, intending to free his father-in-law, Philip, Landgrave, from unjust captivity and Germany from slavery, attacks Charles in war; and, victorious, at the same time frees his father-in-law and obtains a lasting peace for the Church through the Treaty of Passau concerning religion. Thus, in this war, the purer religion was freed from Papal oppression, and, although the Pontiff was raging, a perpetual peace was obtained for the Church. §. CLXXVIII.

units.la: Eduardus Angliae Rex lento veneno e medio tollitur, succedente Maria, quae Pontificiam religionem restituit, & dirum in modum adversus Evangelicos saevit. §. CLXXIX.
units.tr: Edward, King of England, is removed from the midst by a slow poison; Mary succeeds him, who restores the Papal religion and rages in a dreadful manner against the Evangelicals. §. CLXXIX.

units.la: Julio III. P. succedit Marcellus: atque huic post dies 22. Paulus IV. Carafa, erga Principes summos, Carolum, Ferdinandum & Philippum Draconicum animum gerens. §. CLXXX. CLXXXI.
units.tr: Julius III is succeeded by Marcellus, and after twenty-two days by Paul IV, Carafa, who bore a draconian spirit towards the chief princes, Charles, Ferdinand and Philip. §. CLXXX. CLXXXI.

units.la: Pax Religionis in Conventu Passavienssi promissa, in Augustanis Comitiis solenniter confirmatur. §. CLXXXVIII.
units.tr: The peace of religion promised at the Diet of Passau is solemnly confirmed at the Diet of Augsburg. §. CLXXXVIII.

units.tr: Paul IV establishes at Rome a congregation of Cardinals and Prelates

units.la: tuit, de Reformanda Ecclesia consultaturam. irrito plane successu.
units.tr: to deliberate on reforming the Church, with a plainly fruitless outcome.

units.tr: supporters, by which he also subjects to punishment those who shine

units.la: Idem tribunal Inquisitionis Romæ erigit. ibid.
units.tr: The same man sets up the tribunal of the Inquisition at Rome. ibid.

units.tr: Mary, Queen of England, dies, and her successor Elizabeth abolishes

units.tr: Pius revives the Council of Trent, already dead for ten years, and in a new manner

units.la: suscitat, eique novo exemplo quinque Legatos præficit. §. C L XXXV.
units.tr: sets five Legates over it. §. C L XXXV.

units.tr: During it, the Emperor Ferdinand, in a letter written to the Pontiff, complains of the manner in which the Council is being held, and sends a volume of demands to the Council;

units.la: cilii celebrati modo queritur, & postulatorum volumen ad Concilium

units.la: In Galliis bellum civile primum movetur, Pontificiorum Duce
units.tr: In France the first civil war breaks out, with Francis Guise leading the Papists and Louis de Condé the Reformed.

units.la: Francisco Guisio; Reformatorum Ludovico Condæo. cadente Gui-
units.tr: Guise falls, and by the peace granted by the Queen for religion, it is permitted to nobles

units.la: sio, & pace religiosa à Regina concessa, eatenus, ut liceat nobilibus

Concilium Tridentinum 3. Dec. finitur, & à Pontificiis nonnul-
units.tr: The Council of Trent ended on 3 December, and was accepted by some of the Papists, but by the Protestants all together was rejected as a conventicle.

units.la: lis recipitur, aliis, Protestantibus verò universis, ceu Conciliabu-
units.tr: In the Netherlands the nobles made suppliant petitions to Margaret the Regent for freedom of religion. Shortly afterwards riots broke out there, and statues were thrown down. §. 193.

units.la: lum profanorum hominum rejicitur. §. C L XXXVII. C L XXXVIII.
units.tr: becomes worse by the day, and persecutes the faithful. §. C X C.

units.la: Post Concilium Tridentinum Ecclesia Romana, abstersò pudore
units.tr: Pius V, succeeding Pius IV, despairs of his own salvation and promotes the execution of the Council of Trent. §. C X C I.

units.la: omni, deterior in dies evadit, & fideles persequitur. §. C X C.
units.tr: In Belgium the nobles make supplication to Margaret, the Governess, for freedom of religion. Soon afterwards seditions break out there, and statues are cast down. §. C X C III.

units.la: Pio IV. Succedens Pius V. de salute sua desperat, & Concilii
units.tr: There the army of the Reformed Churches is routed by Alba,

units.la: Tridentini executionem promovet. §. C X C I.
units.tr: and the captured Egmont, Horn and other knights are soon put to the sword. ibid.

units.la: In Belgio Proceres Margarethæ Gubernatrici pro libertate religio-
units.tr: At the same place the army of the Reformed Churches was routed by Alva, and the captured Egmont, Horne, and other knights were soon put to death by the axe. Ibid.

units.la: nis supplices fiunt. Paulò post ibidem seditiones exoriuntur, & statuæ
units.tr: ...nis become suppliants. Shortly afterwards, riots break out there and statues are thrown down.
