units.tr: are thrown down. §. CXCIII.

units.la: Ibidem Reformatarum Ecclesiarum exercitus ab Albano funditur,
units.tr: There too the army of the Reformed Churches is routed by Alba,

units.la: & capti Egmondanus, Hornanus, aliíque Equites mox securi per-
units.tr: and the captured Egmondanus, Hornanus, and other knights were soon put to death by the axe.

units.la: cutiuntur. ibid.
units.tr: are beheaded shortly afterwards. Ibid.

units.la: Moritur Claudius Espencæus, Theologus Parisiensis insignis, qui Romanam Curiam graphicè depinxit. §. CCXXI.
units.tr: Claudius Espencaeus, a distinguished Parisian theologian who vividly portrayed the Roman Curia, dies. §. CCXXI.

units.la: Pius V. Elisabetham Angliæ Reginam anathemate ferit, ejúsque consilia per Nicolaum Marianum in Angliam missum infringere conatur. Excommunicationis sententia sequente anno à Feltono Londini ad fores Episcopi affigitur, qui scelus suspendio luit. §. CXCII. In Gallia Condæus captus contra fidem datam occiditur; & Amiralius arma circumfert, donec sequente anno mense Augusto pax fieret, & pristina religionis libertas restitueretur. ibid.
units.tr: Pius V. struck Elizabeth, Queen of England, with anathema, and tried to thwart her plans by means of Nicolaus Marianus, whom he sent into England. The sentence of excommunication was posted the following year at London, on the gates of the Bishop's house, by Felton, who paid for the crime with the gallows. In France Condé was taken captive and killed, contrary to the faith that had been pledged; and the Admiral took up arms and carried them about until, in August of the following year, peace was made and the former liberty of religion was restored. ibid.

units.la: Pio V. succedit Gregorius XIII. cujus initia horribilis laniena Parisiensis, applaudente ipso, modis inauditis Bartholomæi die, conscio Rege Carolo IX. Reformatæ religionis Principes in una velut muscipula, uti loquebatur, capturo; patrata fœdat. §. CXCV. CXCVI. CXCVII.
units.tr: Henry III, King of France, kills the Guises, who had planned to thrust him into a monastery, surrounding them with snares. He himself too, for this reason, is devoted to curses by Sixtus in the following year, and is struck by the monk Jacques Clément with a poisoned and long knife, and dies; the Pontiff praises the parricide beyond measure. §. CC. CCI.

units.la: Gregorius Papa formulam Calendarii novi ad Comitia Augustana mittit, eámque in Imperio recipi petit. Approbatur verò à Cæsare Rodolpho, aliisque Pontificiis: à Protestantibus contra rejicitur. §. CXCVIII.
units.tr: Sixtus V, nourishing some monstrous plan against the Spaniards, whose power in Italy he regarded with suspicion, was about to take the side of Henry IV and Elizabeth, both excommunicated, but is secretly killed by a Franciscan monk; after him Urban VII, and after ten days Gregory XIV, succeeds. §. CCIII. CCIV.

units.la: Idem seminaria instituit, Jesuitas fovet, Hiberniam Elisabethæ subtrahere conatur. ibid.
units.tr: The same pope founded seminaries, fostered the Jesuits, and tried to wrest Ireland away from Elizabeth. Ibid.

units.la: Wilhelmus Araufionensis, libertatem religionis in Belgio defendens, à quodam sicario, à Parmensi immisso, globo sclopeti trajectus moritur. §. CXCIII.
units.tr: William of Orange, defending freedom of religion in the Netherlands, was struck by a ball from a musket and died, shot by a certain assassin sent by the Parmese. §. CXCIII.

units.la: Gregorium XIII. excipit Sixtus V. lacrymas cruentas, crudelitatis signum, fundere suetus. Is Regem Navarræ & Condæum, ut inhabiles Regno, statim excommunicat, & ditiones eorundem prædæ exponit, Guisio aliisque exercitu comparato urbes occupantibus, & decretum de una religione Pontificia conservanda, promulgantibus. §. CXCIX.
units.tr: Gregory XIII was succeeded by Sixtus V, who was accustomed to shed bloody tears, a sign of cruelty. He at once excommunicated the King of Navarre and Condé, as unfit to reign, and exposed their dominions to plunder, while Guise and others raised an army to occupy cities and promulgated a decree that the one Papist religion must be maintained. §. CXCIX.

units.la: Classis ingens Hispanica, navibus 125. instructa, cum classe Parmensi, trecentarum navium jungenda, Angliam occupatura, benedictione Sixti P. consecrata, non sine Divino miraculo dissipata magnam partem perit, & conatus ingens, clade Senacheribiana, in nihilum recidit. §. CCIX.
units.tr: The mighty Spanish fleet, equipped with 125 ships, was to be joined with the Parmese fleet of three hundred ships and was to occupy England. It was consecrated with the blessing of Pope Sixtus, but not without a divine miracle it was scattered, and for the most part perished; and this huge attempt, with a Sennacherib-like disaster, came to nothing. §. CCIX.

units.la: Henricus III. Rex Galliæ Guisios, qui consilia de ipso in Monasterium trudendo ceperant, insidiis circumventos trucidat: qui & ipse propterea sequente anno à Sixto P. diris devotus, à Monacho Jacobo Clemente, venenato & oblongo cultello ictus, occiditur; parricidium laudante Pontifice supra modum. §. CC. CCI.
units.tr: Henry III, King of France, has the Guises, who had plotted to thrust him into a monastery, ambushed and slaughtered. In the following year he himself, devoted to destruction by Sixtus V, was struck down by the monk Jacques Clément with a poisoned, elongated knife and killed; the Pontiff praised the parricide beyond measure. §. CC. CCI.

units.la: Sixtus V. monstri quidpiam alens contra Hispanos, quorum suspectam in Italia potentiam habuit, Henrici IV. & Elisabethæ, excommunicati utriusque, partibus accessurus, à Monacho Franciscano clanculum occiditur; cui Urbanus VII. & huic post decem dies Gregorius XIV. succedit. §. CCIII. CCIV.
units.tr: Sixtus V, nursing some monstrous scheme against the Spaniards, whose power in Italy he regarded with suspicion, was about to take the side of Henry IV and Elizabeth, both of them excommunicated, when he was secretly killed by a Franciscan friar. Urban VII succeeded him, and ten days later Gregory XIV succeeded Urban. §. CCIII. CCIV.

units.la: Gregorius P. frustra armis tentato Henrico IV. eum iterum excommunicat, & subditos omnes ab ejus obedientia absolvit. Subditi vero etiam Pontificii in Parlamentis excommunicationem irritam pronuntiant, & bullam cremant. §. CCIV.
units.tr: Pope Gregory, having tried arms against Henry IV without success, excommunicates him again and absolves all his subjects from their obedience to him. The Papists themselves, however, in the Parliaments declare the excommunication void and burn the bull. §. CCIV.

units.la: Clemens VIII. Papa creatur, qui Henricum IV. tertium excommunicat. §. CCV.
units.tr: Clement VIII is created Pope, who excommunicates Henry IV for the third time. §. CCV.

units.la: Idem Sixti V. versionem S. Bibliorum vulgatam recognoscit, & immane quantum, licet Sixtus suam recognitionem edita bulla immutabilem haberi jusserit, mutat. §. CCII.
units.tr: The same Pope revises the Vulgate version of the Holy Bible, and changes it to an enormous degree, although Sixtus had ordered by his published bull that his own revision be held unalterable. §. CCII.

units.la: Clemens P. & Hispaniæ Rex Galliæ Episcopis, aliisque persuadent, ut relicto Henrico IV. alium Regem eligant. Consentiunt nonnulli in Henricum Guisii filium. Reliqui multis precibus ab Henrico IV. impetrant, ut Papæ & Hispani consilia fracturus, Pontificia sacra amplecteretur. Sic d. 15. Julii Templum Dionysii ingressus, Missam audit & absolvitur, atque mox etiam Carnuti coronatur; Jesuitis per Castellum sicarium sequente anno frustra jugulum ejus appetentibus, qui proin tota Gallia exire jubentur. ibid.
units.tr: Pope Clement and the King of Spain persuade the bishops of France and others to abandon Henry IV and choose another king. Some agree to Henry, son of Guise. The rest, after many entreaties, obtain from Henry IV that he, frustrating the plans of the Pope and the Spaniards, should embrace the Papist sacred rites. Thus on 15 July he entered the church of St Denis, heard Mass and was absolved, and soon afterwards was crowned at Chartres; in the following year the Jesuits, through the assassin Castellanus, vainly sought his throat, and for this reason they were ordered to leave the whole of France. ibid.

units.la: Idem Henricus à Pontifice etiam Romano absolutionem, sed pudendo ritu, impetrat. ibid.
units.tr: The same Henry obtains absolution also from the Roman Pontiff, but by a shameful rite. ibid.

units.la: Clemens P. fœdus sacrum ad extirpandos Evangelicos, conciliat, cui Pontificii Principes omnes, Henrico IV. & Hetruriæ Duce exceptis, subscribunt. §. CCVI.
units.tr: Pope Clement arranges a holy league for the extermination of the Evangelicals, to which all the Papist princes subscribe, except Henry IV and the Duke of Tuscany. §. CCVI.

units.la: Henricus IV. Edicto solenni Nannetensi Pacem religiosam in Gallia constituit. §. CCCXXVII.
units.tr: Henry IV, by the solemn Edict of Nantes, establishes religious peace in France. §. CCCXXVII.

units.la: SECULUM DECIMUM SEPTIMUM. §. CCVIII. — CCCL.
units.tr: THE SEVENTEENTH CENTURY. §. CCVIII. — CCCL.

units.la: Sacerdotes ex Romano seminario egressi, & Jesuitæ in Anglia novam Hierarchiam secretam constituerant. Sed inter utrosque occulta dissidia in nervum erumpunt, & vix à Clemente P. sopiuntur. §. CCVIII.
units.tr: Priests who had come out of the Roman seminary, and the Jesuits, had set up a new secret hierarchy in England. But hidden discords between the two broke out into open conflict, and were scarcely quieted by Pope Clement.

units.la: Elisabethæ Reginæ succedit Jacobus VI. Scotiæ Rex, qui Regna tria conjungit, insidiis Pontificiorum, quibus statim electus Rex liberum religionis exercitium petentibus negavit; multifariis appetitus. §. CCIX. CCXI.
units.tr: Queen Elizabeth was succeeded by James VI, King of Scots, who united the three kingdoms. He was assailed by the plots of the Papists, and when they sought free exercise of their religion, the king, as soon as he was elected, refused it. §. CCIX. CCXI.

units.la: Intestina dissidia Romanam Ecclesiam exercent, ob quæstiones à Jesuitis motas, de Papa, de confessione, auxiliis gratiæ & libero arbitrio. quæ postrema quæstio à Clemente P. non definita, inter Jesuitas & Dominicanos acerbis odiis deinceps agitata est. §. CCVII.
units.tr: Internal dissensions vex the Roman Church, over questions raised by the Jesuits concerning the Pope, confession, the auxiliary grace and free will. This last question, which Pope Clement did not settle, was thereafter pursued with bitter hatred between the Jesuits and the Dominicans. §. CCVII.

units.la: Jesuitæ à Jacobo Rege Anglia pelluntur. Contra Gallia antehac pulsi, Clementis & Mariæ Medicæ intercessione postliminio recipiuntur. §. CCV.
units.tr: The Jesuits were driven out of England by King James. On the other hand, having previously been expelled from France, they were received back by right of postliminy through the intercession of Clement and Marie de' Medici. §. CCV.

units.la: Clemens P. fidem datam à supremis potestatibus tutò violari posse asserit. § CCX.
units.tr: Pope Clement asserts that a promise given by the supreme powers may safely be violated. §. CCX.

units.la: Clementi VIII. Leo XI. & huic post dies 26. Paulus V. Borgesius Vice-Deum salutari se passus, Ecclesiæ non reformator sed deformator, succedit, frustra nonnullis confuso clamore Baronium deposcentibus. Prodierúntque mox Card. Perronio proditore, arcana conclavis utriusque. § CCXIX. & CCXXII.
units.tr: After Clement VIII came Leo XI, and after him, twenty-six days later, Paul V, Borghese, who allowed himself to be greeted as Vice-God, succeeded. He was a deformer, not a reformer, of the Church. Some vainly demanded Baronius with confused clamour. Soon the secrets of both conclaves came out, through the betrayal of Cardinal Perron. §. CCXIX. & CCXXII.

units.la: In Anglia conjuratio pulveraria Roberti Catisbeii, & complicum, Jesuitis, Garneto inprimis, consciis, in necem Regis, Reginæ, liberorum, totiúsque Parlamenti proposita, detegitur. §. CCXI. CCXII. CCXIII.
units.tr: In England the gunpowder conspiracy of Robert Catesby and his accomplices is discovered. The Jesuits, especially Garnet, were privy to it, and it aimed at the murder of the King, the Queen, their children, and the whole Parliament. §. CCXI. CCXII. CCXIII.

units.la: Jesuitarum hæresis singularis prima de jure occidendi Reges & Principes Pontifici imparentes; nec non secunda de æquivocationibus & reservationibus mentalibus invalescunt. §. CCXIV. CCXV.
units.tr: The first singular heresy of the Jesuits, concerning the right to kill kings and princes who do not obey the Pope, and the second, concerning equivocations and mental reservations, gain strength. §. CCXIV. CCXV.

units.la: Contentio acris gliscit Paulum V. inter & Venetos, ob legem Venetorum, ne Ecclesiasticis bona immobilia donare liceat, quam abrogari Papa petit. Renuentes Venetos idem excommunicat; & Jesuitis Venetorum ditione exulantibus, causâque adversis scriptis vehementer agitata, Papa foro cedere, & excommunicationem sequente anno abrogare coactus est. §. CCXX.
units.tr: A bitter contention flares up between Paul V and the Venetians over a Venetian law forbidding the Church to receive immovable property by gift, which the Pope seeks to have abrogated. When the Venetians refused, he excommunicated them as well. With the Jesuits exiled from Venetian territory and the cause vigorously debated in hostile writings, the Pope was forced to yield the matter to the civil courts, and in the following year to revoke the excommunication. §. CCXX.

units.la: Hungaria in Pacificatione Viennensi, Bots-Kajum inter & Rodolphum II. inita, religiosa pace, & Reformati in ea libero religionis exercitio potiuntur. §. CCCI.
units.tr: In Hungary, by the Peace of Vienna concluded between Bocskay and Rudolf II, religious peace was won, and the Reformed there obtained free exercise of their religion. §. CCCI.

units.la: Cæsar Baronius, Cardinalis, Ecclesiæ Romanæ hucusque Atlas, Annalium opere laboriosō, sed minùs bona fide scripto famosus, moritur. §. CCXVI.
units.tr: Caesar Baronius, the cardinal, hitherto the Atlas of the Roman Church, famous for his laborious work of the Annals, but written with less good faith, dies. §. CCXVI.

units.la: Bohemi Evangelicæ religioni addicti à Rodolpho II. Imp. plenam religionis libertatem, Majestaticis literis confirmatam, obtinent. Unde, pace religiosa stabilita, Evangelium in Bohemia, Silesia & Moravia mira incrementa capit, & Rodolphus Imp. Ordinem pacis singularem meditatur. §. CCXXIV.
units.tr: The Bohemians, devoted to the Evangelical religion, obtain from Rudolf II, the Emperor, full liberty of religion, confirmed by letters of Majesty. Hence, with religious peace established, the Gospel takes remarkable growth in Bohemia, Silesia and Moravia, and Emperor Rudolf plans a singular ordinance of peace. §. CCXXIV.

units.la: A. C. INDEX XI.
units.tr: A. C. INDEX XI.

units.la: Henricus IV. stans in procinctu, ut collecto exercitu Brandenburgicum & Neoburgicum Principes juvaret, à sicario Ravaillaco in curru, d. 4. Maii, interficitur. §. CCV.
units.tr: Henry IV, standing ready to march with an army he had assembled to aid the Princes of Brandenburg and Neuburg, is killed on 4 May in his carriage by the assassin Ravaillac. §. CCV.

units.la: Ecclesiae Romanae hoc tempore alter Atlas, post varia scripta polemica, tractatum scribit de potestate Papæ in temporalibus, qui mox publicè in Gallia damnatur. §. CCXVII.
units.tr: Another Atlas of the Roman Church, after various polemical writings, publishes a treatise on the power of the Pope in temporal matters, which is soon condemned in public in France. §. CCXVII.

units.la: Rodolphus Imp. acie victus à Fratre Matthia, mœrore confectus moritur. Ex quo tempore res Evangelicorum in Bohemia, Silesia, Germania universa, inclinari coeperunt. §. CCXXV.
units.tr: Emperor Rudolf, defeated in battle by his brother Matthias, dies worn down by grief. From this time the affairs of the Evangelicals in Bohemia, Silesia and all Germany begin to decline. §. CCXXV.

units.la: Hispaniam universam gravissimi motus affligunt ob controversiam Jesuitas inter & Dominicanos de Conceptione B. Virginis Mariæ, quæ per octo annos integros extrahitur Pontifice Paulo V. definitivam sententiam ferre, metu partium prævalidarum, non auso. §. CCXXIII.
units.tr: Spain as a whole is shaken by very grave disturbances over the controversy between the Jesuits and the Dominicans concerning the Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary. The controversy drags on for eight whole years, because Pope Paul V, fearing the very powerful parties, did not dare to pronounce a definitive judgement. §. CCXXIII.

units.la: Matthias Imp. improles Bohemis patruelem Ferdinandum obtrudit, qui Evangelicis ore, Papæ corde jurat. §. CCXXV.
units.tr: Emperor Matthias, having no children, forces upon the Bohemians his cousin Ferdinand, who swears to the Evangelicals with his mouth and to the Pope with his heart. §. CCXXV.

units.la: Pragæ Evangelicis Templa claudi vel everti, & liberum religionis exercitium labefactari varie incipit. Comitia proin instituuntur, in quibus de privilegiorum conservatione ageretur. Gravamina colleƈta Consiliariis à Cæsare relictis exponunt. Cümque Slawatam, Smekzanium, & Platterum, sibi reluctantes offenderent, inconsulto impetu, vi tamen protestationis jam A. 1609. contra turbatores pacis factæ; eos per fenestras in pomœrium arcis præcipitant, & inito fœdere contra communes Dei, Regis, religionis & Majestaticarum literarum hostes se pugnaturos Sanctè recipiunt; apologia edita facti sui causam reddunt, Jesuitas toto Regno pellunt. ibid.
units.tr: At Prague the Evangelical churches begin to be closed or destroyed, and the free exercise of religion to be undermined in various ways. Assemblies are therefore called, at which the preservation of privileges was to be discussed. They set out their grievances to the counsellors left by the Emperor. When Slawata, Smecius and Platter, who opposed them, gave offence, they, in an ill-considered rush, yet with the force of the protest already made in 1609 against the disturbers of the peace, hurl them through the windows onto the rampart of the castle. Entering an alliance, they solemnly undertake to fight against the common enemies of God, the King, religion and the Letters of Majesty. By publishing an apology they give the reason for their deed, and they expel the Jesuits from the whole kingdom. ibid.

units.la: Matthias Cæsar moritur. Ordines Bohemi spreto Ferdinando eligunt sibi Regem Fridericum V. Electorem Palatinum. Ferdinandus verò Romanorum Imperator electus, vim parat adversus Bohemos, in partes ejus concedentibus Hispanis, Electore Saxoniæ, Maximiliano Bavaro, aliisque & Paulo V. P. clerum Italiæ reliquúmque ad sumptus Ferdinando erogandos incitante. ibid. & §. CCXXVII.
units.tr: Emperor Matthias dies. The Bohemian Estates, disregarding Ferdinand, elect as their King Frederick V, Elector Palatine. Ferdinand, however, elected Emperor of the Romans, prepares force against the Bohemians, with Spain, the Elector of Saxony, Maximilian of Bavaria and others taking his side, and Paul V urging the clergy of Italy and the rest to furnish the money for Ferdinand's expenses. ibid. & §. CCXXVII.

units.la: In valle Telina horribilis Protestantium, sacra facientium, & ex improviso oppressorum laniena, ab exulibus & reliƈtis in valle Pontificiis, inde à die 9. Julii patratur. §. CCXXIX.
units.tr: In the Valtelline a dreadful slaughter of Protestants, who were worshipping and were suddenly overpowered, is carried out from 9 July by exiles and by the Papists left in the valley. §. CCXXIX.

units.la: Ingens d. 8. Nov. non procul ab urbe Praga Cæsareos inter & Bohemos pugna committitur, in qua Maximilianus Bavarus victor, Pragam occupat, Frideric o Rege novo inde Uratislaviam cum conjuge concedente. Hæc tempestas Bohemos oppressit, nova methodo à Jesuitis ad Papatum feduƈtos; atque mox universam Germaniam corripuit, Protestantiúmque res in aciem novaculæ deduxit; belli sa-cri cri classicum canente Sciopio. §. CCXXV. CCXXVI. CCXXVII. CCXXVIII.
units.tr: On 8 November a great battle is fought near the city of Prague between the Imperialists and the Bohemians. In it Maximilian of Bavaria is victorious and occupies Prague, and King Frederick, newly made, withdraws from there to Breslau with his wife. This storm overwhelmed the Bohemians, who had been seduced to Papacy by the Jesuits with a new method, and soon it seized the whole of Germany and brought the affairs of the Protestants to the edge of the razor, the trumpet of holy war sounding under Sciopius. §. CCXXV. CCXXVI. CCXXVII. CCXXVIII.

units.la: Bavarus Palatinatum superiorem, Hispani inferioris loca nonnulla occupant. ibid.
units.tr: Bavaria occupies Upper Palatinate, and the Spaniards some places in Lower Palatinate. ibid.

units.la: Paulus V. Vice-Deus nuncupatus, moritur, eique Gregorius XV. succedens, foeminae cujusdam consiliis Papatum administrat, & statim constitutionem de forma eligendi Papae edit. §. CCXXX.
units.tr: Paul V, called Vice-God, dies, and Gregory XV, who succeeds him, administers the Papacy under the counsels of a certain woman, and at once issues a constitution on the form of electing a Pope. §. CCXXX.

units.la: Heidelberga urbs d. 6. Sept. armata manu expugnata, civesque miserabiliter prostrati, trucidati sunt, direptione ad tertium usque diem continuata, & Missa introducta. §. CCXXV.
units.tr: The city of Heidelberg is stormed by armed force on 6 September, its citizens miserably cut down and slaughtered; the plundering continued until the third day, and the Mass was introduced. §. CCXXV.

units.la: Galliarum Rex, Pontifice incentore, Reformatis oppida partim vi, partim deditione facta eripit. §. CCXXXI.
units.tr: The King of France, with the Pope as instigator, snatches from the Reformed their towns, partly by force, partly by surrender. §. CCXXXI.

units.la: Japones Christiani a gentilibus suis gravissimam persecutionem, Jesuitarum culpa, sustinent. §. CCXLIII.
units.tr: Japanese Christians suffer a very grievous persecution from their pagan countrymen, through the fault of the Jesuits. §. CCXLIII.

units.la: In Hispania secta Illuminatorum emergens, spe facta veniae, opprimitur. §. CCXXXII.
units.tr: In Spain a sect of Illuminati that had emerged is suppressed, after hope of pardon had been held out to them. §. CCXXXII.

units.la: Gregorius XV. P. post Lojolitas quatuor, aliosque in Sanctorum numerum relatos, moritur, in cujus locum Urbanus VIII. Barbarinus surrogatur, qui statim electus Nepotes suos promovet, & Bullam Canonizationis Ignatii Lojolae, & Xaverii edit. §. CCXXXIII. CCXXXIV.
units.tr: Gregory XV, after enrolling four of the Loyolites and others among the saints, dies; in his place Urban VIII Barberini is put forward, who, as soon as he is elected, promotes his nephews and issues the bull of canonization of Ignatius Loyola and Xavier. §. CCXXXIII. CCXXXIV.

units.la: Durante Gallum inter & Hispanos ac Urbanum P. ob vallem Telinam dissidio, adversus Regem Galliae & Richelium vulgatis seditiosis libellis, in Regis Galliae jugulum denuo culter acuitur; & ob censuram libellorum a Stampesio proditam Clerum inter Galliae & Parlamentum contentio oritur, & a Rege finitur. §. CCXXXVI. CCXXXVII.
units.tr: While a dispute between the French and the Spaniards and Urban over the Valtelline is going on, seditious pamphlets are published against the King of France and Richelieu, and the knife is sharpened anew at the throat of the King of France. Because of the censure of the pamphlets, betrayed by Stampes, a conflict arises between the clergy of France and the Parliament, and it is ended by the King. §. CCXXXVI. CCXXXVII.

units.la: Prodit liber Santarelli de potestate Pontificis, Regum potestati iniquissimus, a Sorbona acriter perstrictus. Ob quem etiam in Jesuitas Claromontanos inquisitio instituitur, quae malam eorum conscientiam prodit. §. CCXXXVIII.
units.tr: The book of Santarelli on the power of the Pontiff appears, most unfair to the power of kings, and is sharply criticised by the Sorbonne. Because of it an inquiry is also instituted against the Jesuits of Clermont, which reveals their guilty conscience. §. CCXXXVIII.

units.la: Cotonus Jesuita, qui antehac quaestiones curiosas daemoni Hadrianae Fraxineae proposuerat, taedio inquisitionis illius moritur. §. CCXXXIX.
units.tr: Cotton, a Jesuit, who had earlier put curious questions to the demon of Hadrian's Ash-tree, dies from weariness of that inquiry. §. CCXXXIX.

units.la: Urbanus P. Bullam Coenae Domini, in qua ipsi etiam Galliarum Reges die Coenae Domini excommunicantur, renovat. §. CCXL.
units.tr: Urban VIII renews the bull of the Lord's Supper, in which even the Kings of France themselves are excommunicated on Maundy Thursday. §. CCXL.

units.la: Rupella, Reformatorum in Gallia asylum, a Ludovico XIII. iisdem eripitur; Urbano VIII. P. multum laetante. §. CCXLI.
units.tr: La Rochelle, the refuge of the Reformed in France, is snatched from them by Louis XIII, Urban VIII greatly rejoicing. §. CCXLI.

units.la: Caesar bonorum Ecclesiasticorum post transactionem Pasiavien-sem occupatorum restitutionem decreto publico petere statuit, & decretum illud hinc inde insinuat. Deploratáque adeo Ecclesiarum Evan-
units.tr: The Emperor resolved, by public decree, to demand the restoration of the ecclesiastical goods occupied since the Treaty of Passau, and this decree is circulated here and there. And the face of the Evangelical

units.la: gelicarum facies apparuit, ut ob spem earundem penitus mox ever-
units.tr: Churches appeared so deplorable that, in hope of utterly overthrowing them soon, a Jubilee was celebrated

units.la: tendarum Romae Jubilaeum agitatum fuerit. §. CCXXVIII.
units.tr: at Rome. §. CCXXVIII.

units.la: Urbanus P. sectam Jesuitiliarum bulla edita abolet. §. CCXXIX.
units.tr: Urban VIII abolishes the Jesuitical sect by a published bull. §. CCXXIX.

units.la: Gustavus Adolphus, Suecia Rex, ceu fulmen quoddam ab ulti-
units.tr: Gustavus Adolphus, King of Sweden, like some thunderbolt from the far North, with remarkable speed begins to traverse all Germany with his victories,

units.la: mo Septentrione mira celeritate universam Germaniam victoriis suis
units.tr: to subdue the Henotics, to free Germany from servitude,

units.la: peragrare, Henoticos domare, Germaniam a servitute, Ecclesiam
units.tr: and to deliver the Church from oppression. §. CCXXVIII.

units.la: ab oppressione liberare incipit. §. CCXXVIII.
units.tr: begins to free [it] from oppression. §. CCXXVIII.

units.la: Urbanus P. adversus Caesarem & Hispanos ob potentiam crescen-
units.tr: Pope Urban, who had already shown a hostile spirit toward Caesar and the Spaniards because of their growing power, had earlier stirred up the King of France against them.

units.tr: Now that fortune has turned, he bears a more hostile mind toward them, because the Catholics, by their tyranny and lust for power, ought to exult in the victories of the heretics.

units.tr: But now that fortune has turned, he bears a more hostile spirit towards them, because the Catholics, by their tyranny and lust for domination,

units.tr: ought to exult in the victories of the heretics. In turn, the Spaniards, having published a book on the power of the Pope by a Jesuit,

units.la: à Jesuita de potestate Pontificis libro, Pontificem Romae suae affigere
units.tr: try to bind the Pope to their own Rome.

units.la: conantur. §CCXLIV.
units.tr: §CCXLIV.

units.tr: The Papists, who for a long time have striven through emissary Jesuits and others to subject Abyssinia to the Roman See,

units.la: nae Sedi subjicere inde à longo tempore annitentium, molimina in-
units.tr: have seen their efforts come to an unhappy end,

units.la: felicem exitum, Patriarcha Lusitano, aliisque Pontificiis omnibus
units.tr: the Portuguese Patriarch and all the other Papists

units.la: severè proscriptis, sortiuntur. §. CCXLII.
units.tr: having been severely proscribed. §. CCXLII.

units.la: Urbanus pacis negotiationem apud Principes Pontificios in speciem
units.tr: Urban presses the negotiation of peace among the Popish princes in appearance,

units.la: urget: sed animo nonnisi bella volutat. §. CCLIII.
units.tr: but in his mind he turns over nothing but wars. §. CCLIII.

units.la: Urbanus bulla edita damnat Jansenii Augustinum, eo praetextu,
units.tr: Urban, by a published bull, condemns Jansenius' Augustinus, on the pretext

units.tr: that it contains some propositions of Michael Baius, long since

units.tr: condemned by Pius V. This bull is not accepted by most of the bishops of Belgium

units.la: Hispanici non recipitur. §. CCXLIV.
units.tr: or of Spain. §. CCXLIV.

units.la: In Hibernia laniena Evangelicorum horribilis, inde à 23.
units.tr: In Ireland a horrible slaughter of Evangelicals, beginning on the 23rd

units.la: Octobris, in gratiam R. Pontificis, patratur. §. CCLI. CCLII.
units.tr: of October, is carried out to please the Roman Pontiff. §. CCLI. CCLII.

units.la: Urbanus bullam suam adversus Jansenium & sequaces repetit &
units.tr: Urban repeats and confirms his bull against Jansenius and his followers, and imposes perpetual silence on those taking root.

units.tr: Yet they do not allow themselves to be restrained in this way; rather, in Belgium and Gaul

units.la: que sic tamen illi coerceri se patiuntur; quin potius in Belgio & Gal-
units.tr: the number of adherents grows daily, maintaining that the bull of Urban

units.la: lia crescit sectatorum numerus in dies, pertendentium, bullam Ur-
units.tr: was extorted by fraud and deceit. §. CCXLV.

units.tr: The third peculiar heresy of the Jesuits, concerning grace and free will, compounded of

units.tr: several elements, takes root. §. CCL.

units.la: pluribus conflata, radices agit. §. CCL.
units.tr: Urban VIII, a decrepit old man, having died after six weeks,

units.la: Urbanus VIII. capularis senex fato functus post sex septimanas,
units.tr: and after a discordant conclave, has as his successor Innocent X Pamphili,

units.la: conclavi diicorde, successorem habet Innocentium X. Pamphilium,
units.tr: who at once admits a blasphemous eulogy by the Italo-Greek Giovanni Battista Catum-Syritus, in which Pamphili is preferred to the Son of God. §. CCLIV.

units.la: qui statim admittit elogium blasphemum Italo-Graeci Baptistae Ca-
units.tr: CCLV. The Papacy is ruled not by him but by his creature, Olympia Maldachina,

units.la: tum-Syriti, quo Pamphilius Filio Dei praefertur. §. CCLIV.
units.tr: ...tum-Syriti, which prefers Pamphilius to the Son of God. §. CCLIV.

units.la: CCLV. Papatumque non ipse, sed glos ejus, Olympia Maldachina,
units.tr: CCLV. The papacy is governed not by the Pope himself but by his sister-in-law, Olympia Maidalchini,

units.la: altera velut Marozia, regit. §. CCLVI.
units.tr: who rules like a second Marozia. §. CCLVI.

units.la: Georgius Rakotzius, Transylvaniae Princeps, Pacem religiosam sam in Hungaria violatam restituit, & liberum Evangelicis religionis exercitium, juxta Viennensem Pacificationem stabilit. §. CCCIV.
units.tr: George Rákóczi, Prince of Transylvania, restored the religious peace violated in Hungary and established the free exercise of the Evangelical religion according to the Peace of Vienna. §. CCCIV.

units.la: Pax Imperialis Monasterii & Osnabrugis Westphalorum concluditur, adversus quam, quòd ejus pactis Ecclesia opima territoria & dignitates amitteret, primò Fabius Chisius Nuntius Pontificius; ac mox etiam ipse Innocentius Papa, edita, ferali bulla solemniter protestantur. §. CCLVIII. CCLIX.
units.tr: The Imperial Peace of Münster and Osnabrück in Westphalia is concluded. Against it, because by its terms the Church would lose rich territories and dignities, first Fabio Chigi, the papal nuncio, and soon Pope Innocent himself, by a published deadly bull, solemnly protest. §. CCLVIII. CCLIX.

units.la: Innocentius P. bulla edita propositiones quinque ex Jansenii Augustino pro libitu Jesuitarum excerptas, & à tredecim Theologis, quos inter Sforza Pallavicinus principem locum obtinebat, praesentibus Cardinalibus nonnullis examinatas, damnat. §. CCLV. CCLVI.
units.tr: Pope Innocent, by a published bull, condemns five propositions drawn from Jansenius's Augustinus at the pleasure of the Jesuits, and examined in the presence of several cardinals by thirteen theologians, among whom Sforza Pallavicini held the chief place. §. CCLV. CCLVI.

units.la: Innocentio d. 7. Jan. defuncto, post technas varias discordium Cardinalium, demum d. 8. Apr. succedit Fabius Chisius, seu Alexander VII. Mahometis Imperatoris Turcici consanguineus. §. CCLX.–CCLXIV.
units.tr: Innocent died on 7 January. After various intrigues among the cardinals, Fabius Chigi, who was also Alexander VII and a relative of the Turkish Emperor Mahomet, succeeded on 8 April. §. CCLX.–CCLXIV.

units.la: Papatus Alexandri initia foedat horribilis laniena Pedemontana, qua Evangelici ingenti numero inauditis modis à Pontificiis, Gastaldo duce, trucidantur. §. CCLXIV. CCLXVIII.
units.tr: The beginning of Alexander's papacy is disgraced by the horrible Piedmontese slaughter, in which a great number of Evangelicals are butchered in unheard-of ways by the Papists under the leadership of Gastaldo. §. CCLXIV. CCLXVIII.

units.la: Alexander P. d. 20. Sept. bullam praetumidam edit, qua Pacis Catholicorum Principum farciendae praetextu, eosdem adversus Protestantes, Sueciae cumprimis Regem Polono bellum moventem, accendere conatur. §. CCLXVIII.
units.tr: On 20 September Alexander issued a very arrogant bull, under the pretext of securing peace among the Catholic princes, by which he tries to stir them up against the Protestants, and especially against the King of Sweden, who was waging war on Poland. §. CCLXVIII.

units.la: Christina Suecia Regina, depositis fascibus, Pontificia sacra amplexa, d. 23. Dec. Romam ingressa, magnificeque ab Alexandro excepta, stabilem ibidem Sedem figit. §. CCLXIX.
units.tr: Queen Christina of Sweden laid down her sceptre, embraced the Papist religion, and entered Rome on 23 December. Alexander received her with great honour, and she fixed her permanent seat there. §. CCLXIX.

units.la: Alexander, cum prius prae se Nepotum neglectum tulisset, eosdem ad summos honores evehit, & Nepotismi Papalis perfectum exemplar praebet. §. CCLXX. – CCLXXIII.
units.tr: Alexander, who had at first made a show of neglecting his nephews, raised them to the highest honours and provided a perfect example of papal nepotism. §. CCLXX.–CCLXXIII.

units.la: Idem edita bulla non tantum Innocentii adversus Jansenitas anathemata confirmat, sed etiam definit, propositiones quinque ab Innocentio damnatas, ex Jansenii Augustino excerptas, & in sensu ab eodem Jansenio intento damnatas esse. §. CCXLVIII.
units.tr: By the same bull he not only confirms Innocent's anathemas against the Jansenists, but also declares that the five propositions condemned by Innocent, taken from Jansenius's Augustinus, were condemned in the sense that Jansenius himself intended. §. CCXLVIII.

units.la: Alexander in gratiam Hispanorum Thomam Villanovanum, Valentiae quondam Archiepiscopum in numerum Divorum refert. §. CCLXXIII.
units.tr: To please the Spaniards, Alexander enrolled Thomas of Villanova, once Archbishop of Valencia, among the saints. §. CCLXXIII.

units.la: Alexander idem Missale Romanum Gallicè editum acerbissimè perstringit. §. CCXC.
units.tr: The same Alexander sharply censured the Roman Missal published in French. §. CCXC.

units.la: Jesuitarum haeresis singularis quarta de infallibilitate Papae, in quaestionibus etiam facti, Lutetiae in Collegio Claromontano proditur, & à Sanioribus mox Theologis libello ad Episcopos misso graviter obnuntiatur. §. CCLXXVI.–CCLXXX.
units.tr: The singular fourth heresy of the Jesuits, concerning the infallibility of the Pope even in questions of fact, is put forward at Paris in the Clermont College, and is soon sharply opposed by the more sober theologians in a pamphlet sent to the bishops. §. CCLXXVI.–CCLXXX.

units.la: 1662. Alexander P. in gratiam Gallorum Francifcum de Sales, Epifco-
units.tr: 1662. Pope Alexander, wishing to enrol Francis de Sales, Bishop

units.la: pum Gebennenfem in numerum Divorum relaturus, Lutetia Lega-
units.tr: of Geneva, among the saints for the sake of the French, asks that

units.la: tum ad fe mitti petit. Miflus Dux Crequius à Corsis, Prætorianis
units.tr: a legate be sent to him from Paris. The envoy, Duke Créqui, suffers an insult at the hands of the Corsican soldiers

units.la: Papæ militibus contumeliam patitur, quam armis Rex vindicaverat,
units.tr: of the Pope's guard, which the King had avenged by arms,

units.la: nisi ei opera Florentini Principis biennio post reconciliatus Papa fatis-
units.tr: unless the Pope, reconciled two years later through the good offices of the Prince of Florence, had made amends. Only then was it permitted to greet the chorus of saints with Sales among them. §.

units.la: fecifiet. Atque tum demum Salefio Divorum chorum salutare licuit. §.
units.tr: CCLXXIV. & CCLXXVI.

units.tr: CCLXXIV. & CCLXXVI.

units.la: Idem edita Bulla certam formulam præscribit, cui Ecclesiastici om-
units.tr: By the same bull he prescribes a fixed formula, to which all ecclesiastics, when subscribing, bind themselves to renounce the errors of the Jansenists.

units.tr: §. CCLXXVIII.

units.tr: §. CCLXXVIII.

units.la: Alexander Indicem librorum prohibitorum profert, in quo ne
units.tr: Alexander publishes an Index of prohibited books, in which he does not even spare the papal bulls, and pierces celebrated Papist authors with the obelisk (the mark of condemnation). §. CCLXXXIX.

units.la: Pontificiis quidem bullis parcit, celebrésque authores Pontificios obe-
lo configit. §. CCLXXXIX.
units.tr: CCLXXXIX.

units.la: 1664. Sorbona d. 24. Martii, annitentibus Parochialibus civitatis Picto-
units.tr: 1664. On 24 March the Sorbonne, at the urging of the parish priests of the city of Poitiers, censures the propositions of Vernantius as sailing too freely before the wind of papal power. §. CCLXXX. CCLXXXI.

units.la: num, censuram in Vernantii propositiones, ceu Pontificiæ potestati
nimium velificantes, stringit. §. CCLXXX. CCLXXXI.
units.tr: CCLXXX. CCLXXXI.

units.la: 1665. Eadem Sorbona Amedei Guimenii opusculum, quo is probare su-
units.tr: 1665. The same Sorbonne calls back for censure the little work of Amadeus Guimenius, in which he tried to prove that the modern moral theology of the Jesuits is not lacking the authority of the famous teachers of the Church, and on 3 February solemnly condemns by name the doctrine of probabilism, and the other propositions contained in that work. §. CCLXXXII.–CCLXXXVI.

units.la: ftinuit, Theologiam Moralem modernam Jesuitarum, celebrium
Ecclesiæ doctorum authoritate non destitui, sub censuram revocat,
& d. 3. Febr. dogma probabilitatis nominatim, aliásque in opusculo
eo comprehensas propositiones folenniter damnat. §. CCLXXXII.-
units.tr: §. CCLXXXII.–

units.la: CCLXXXVI.
Utraque illa Sorbonæ censura offensus non parùm Alexander VII.
units.tr: Offended not a little by both of those censures of the Sorbonne, Alexander VII.

units.la: quòd per eam infallibilitatem suam in discrimen adduci putaret, Bre-
units.tr: by which he thought his infallibility was being brought into jeopardy. He sought its revocation in a Brief drawn up on 6 April and addressed to the Most Christian King.

units.la: vi ad Regem Christianissimum d. 6. Apr. exarato, revocari eam
units.tr: The King, not unaware of how much would be demanded of his Majesty if the Pope were held to be infallible,

units.la: petiit. Rex non ignarus, quantum ex Majestate peteretur, fi Pon-
units.tr: referred the Papal Brief to the examination of the Supreme Court.

units.la: tifex infallibilis haberetur, Pontificium Breve examini Supremæ Curiæ
units.tr: After mature deliberation, the Court sealed its judgment, which approves both censures of the Sorbonne

units.la: subjicit, quæ Consilio maturo consignato Sorbonæ censuram utramque
units.tr: and vigorously refutes the infallibility of the Pope.

units.la: probat, & Pontificis infallibilitatem fortiter refutat. §. CCLXXXVI.-
units.tr: §. CCLXXXVI.–CCLXXXIX.

units.la: CCLXXXIX.
units.tr: CCLXXXIX.

units.la: Inter Pontificios Doctores, Pallavicinum, Suavem & Julium
units.tr: Among the Papist doctors, Pallavicini, Suavis and Julius Clemens the Scot dispute whether the Roman Church, after the Council of Trent, has declined for the worse or not; Julius Clemens maintains that it has declined for the worse in many respects. §. CCXCI. CCXCII.

units.la: Clementem Scotum disceptatur, anne Ecclesia Romana post Tri-
dentinum Concilium in pejus deflexerit nec ne; Julio Clemente in
pluribus eam in pejus deflexisse, sustinente. §. CCXCI. CCXCII.
units.tr: CCXCI. CCXCII.

units.la: Jesuitarum hæresis singularis quinta, ex pluribus composita, de
units.tr: The singular fifth heresy of the Jesuits, made up of several parts, concerning probabilism, the rule of moral actions, and other novel hypotheses of moral theology, gains strength. §. CCLXXXII. CCLXXXIII.

units.la: probabilitate, actionum moralium regula, aliisque novitiis Theolo-
giæ Moralis hypothesibus, invalescit. §. CCLXXXII. CCLXXXIII.
units.tr: CCLXXXII. CCLXXXIII.

units.la: 1667. Eorundem hæresis singularis sexta de attritionis efficacia, & nulla
units.tr: 1667. Their singular sixth heresy, concerning the efficacy of attrition and the lack of any need for love of God for salvation, raises its head.

units.la: necessitate amoris Divini ad salutem, caput extollit. §. CCXCVI.
units.tr: §. CCXCVI.

units.la: CCXCVII. Alexander VII. flagrante Jansenitas & Jesuitas inter de dilectione Dei, an ea ad salutem necessaria sit nec ne, dissidio, bullam edit, qua definitivam suspendens, Jesuitarum hæresin deploratam de nulla necessitate amoris Dei, reprehendi impiè vetat; & quinto ac decimo post bullam illam impiam die moritur, definitivam coram tremendo tribunali Dei expertus haud dubiè. §. CCXCVII. CCXCVIII.
units.tr: CCXCVII. Alexander VII, while the Jansenists and Jesuits were fiercely disputing whether love of God is necessary for salvation, issued a bull by which, suspending a definitive judgment, he forbids the wretched Jesuit heresy of the absence of any need for love of God to be impiously rebuked; and on the fifteenth day after that impious bull he died, having doubtless experienced the definitive judgment before the dreadful tribunal of God. §. CCXCVII. CCXCVIII.

units.la: Alexandro succeedit Clemens IX. Rospigliosus. ibid.
units.tr: Alexander is succeeded by Clement IX, Rospigliosi. ibid.

units.la: Clemens Ludovicum Beltrame & Petrum de Alcantara Hispanos, nec non Magdalenam di Paley Florentinam in Divorum numerum refert; & Judæos paucis exceptis, Roma exigit. ibid.
units.tr: Clement enrols Ludovicus Beltrame and Peter of Alcantara, Spaniards, and Magdalen di Pazzi of Florence, among the saints; and, with few exceptions, he drives the Jews out of Rome. ibid.

units.la: Clemens IX. d. 29. Nov. moritur, & Cardinales Conclave ingressi, in eo quatuor menses discordibus animis transigunt. §. CCXCIX.
units.tr: Clement IX dies on 29 November, and the cardinals, entering the conclave, spend four months there with divided minds. §. CCXCIX.

units.la: Re pœne desperata Æmilius Altieri, seu Clemens X. Papa exit. ibid.
units.tr: With the matter almost despaired of, Emilio Altieri, that is Clement X, emerges as Pope. ibid.

units.la: Eo Pontifice, Jesuitis annitentibus, Hungaricæ Ecclesiæ Evangelicæ gravissimam à clero persecutionem sustinent. §. C C C. &c.
units.tr: Under this Pope, with the Jesuits pressing on, the Evangelical Church of Hungary endures a most severe persecution by the clergy. §. CCC. &c.

units.la: Georgius Barzon, Episcopus Varadiensis titularis liberum religionis exercitium ab Hungariæ Regibus Ecclesiis in Hungaria Evangelicis pactum, scripto publici juris facto oppugnat. §. CCCI. CCCII. CCCIII.
units.tr: George Barzon, titular Bishop of Varad, attacks in a published writing the free exercise of religion granted by the Kings of Hungary to the Evangelical churches in Hungary. §. CCCI. CCCII. CCCIII.

units.la: Occasione Cæsarei exercitus Hungariam ob turbas Nadastianas ingressi, Clerus Pontificius terrestres Dominos ad persecutionem Evangelicorum concitat, & mox ad Regias etiam liberàsque civitates persecutio penetrat. Unde Evangelicis passim Templa eripiuntur, Pastores vexantur, expelluntur. §. CCCIV. CCCV.
units.tr: On the occasion of the Imperial army's entry into Hungary because of the Nádasdy disturbances, the Papist clergy stir up the lay lords to persecute the Evangelicals, and soon the persecution spreads even to the royal and free cities. As a result, Evangelical churches are everywhere snatched away, and the ministers are harassed and driven out. §. CCCIV. CCCV.

units.la: Tribunal Posoniense rebellionis præteXtu Magnates Evangelicos in Hungaria plures evertit. § CCCVI.
units.tr: The Court of Pozsony, under the pretext of rebellion, overthrows several Evangelical magnates in Hungary. §. CCCVI.

units.la: Posonium prima vice ad d. 25. Sept. citantur Pastores Evangelici pauci, rebellionis impactæ causam dicturi. Comparentes triginta duo Augustani, & Reformatus unus, malè persecutionis impetum sustinent. Mortis enim metu, innocentiæ licet sibi conscii, libellis præscriptis, quorum virus non satis perceperant, diversimode subscribunt. §. CCCVI.
units.tr: Pozsony first summons a few Evangelical ministers, to answer for the alleged cause of rebellion, on 25 September. Thirty-two Augsburg ministers and one Reformed minister appear, and they bear the assault of persecution badly. For from fear of death, although conscious of their innocence, they sign in various ways the prescribed documents, the poison of which they had not sufficiently perceived. §. CCCVI.

units.tr: Pozsony summons the ministers, rectors, cantors, students and sextons, all the Evangelicals throughout Hungary, for a second time in February. Some are forbidden to obey the summons; more than two hundred and fifty others appear. They are harassed by the wonderfully twisted procedures of the court and, though not convicted, all are condemned to death on 4 April; after the condemnation they are kept in free custody. Some, overcome by the weakness of the flesh, give their names to the documents; the more steadfast ones undergo persecution in prison, and finally even in the Neapolitan galleys, so horrible that a similar example

units.tr: Clement VII, Pope, is elected. 163. His character as depicted by Giovio. He sends Campeggio to the Diet. His very poor faith toward the Emperor. ibid. Rome captured, he himself is also held captive in the Castel Sant'Angelo. Freed, he makes an alliance with the Emperor and crowns him at Bologna. units.tr: electors of the Pope. 74. etc. It claims supreme power even in temporal matters under Gregory VII. 79. etc. It decrees a Holy War and crusading warfare, so that, with the princes sent off to the East, it may rule more freely. 86. etc. Its calamitous face around the twelfth century. 90. Its Pope becomes an absolute king and depresses the emperors. 94. etc. It opposes scholastic theology to the majesty of the Divine Word, and canon law to the majesty of law and of human laws. 95, 96. etc. The faithful, the Waldenses above all, set themselves against it. 99. At the Lateran Council it defines transubstantiation and other things, and exalts the God Maozim. 103. It is sustained by the mendicant monks, the Franciscans and Dominicans. 104. The Eternal Gospel devised by the monks, teeming with blasphemies, it sluggishly suppresses, because it represented its bare Papacy. 110, 111. etc. Under Boniface VIII it obtains supreme power even in temporal matters, and so the summit is placed upon the Papacy, the Jubilee intervening, as a solemn inauguration of supreme power in spiritual and temporal matters. 115, 116. etc. It defends its Caesaro-Papacy against Louis of Bavaria. 128. etc. It is branded with the name of Babylon by the discerning, and its corruption is variously rebuked. 135. etc. It is torn by the most obstinate schism from Urban VI down to the Council of Constance. 138. etc. Abandoning the Eastern Churches, it becomes the cause of their submitting to the yoke of the Turks. 142. A cloud of witnesses against it, 147, 150, of those sustaining the most grievous persecution, 148, 150. From it comes the separation of the faithful through the Reformation of Luther and Zwingli, whose necessity the Papists acknowledged. 152. etc. 162. It experiences a free council from those who protested against the Roman Church; in whose place it instituted the tyrannical Council of Trent, which did not remove the separation of the Protestants but rather promoted it further. 164-189. It persecutes the Evangelical Church, separated from itself, in dire ways. 190-f. La Rochelle is captured by Louis XIII. 241. Urban the Pope insulting it. ibid. Ruyter, the admiral of the Dutch fleet, frees the Hungarian ministers from the Neapolitan galleys. 316.
